#### 📖 Introduction

The Activity Restriction Property Class defines the restrictions on AA Activities and Product Qualifier Rules. Activity Restrictions are used to apply restriction rules to transactions activities (For example, on the prepayment of loan amount). The activities in the life of the arrangement are monitored against the rules and breaking of a rule can result in the application of a penalty, override or rejection of the transaction.

It is possible to apply a rule while evaluating a Property (as part of schedule processing of interest or charge). If satisfied or broken, the system waives or applies the Property or an alternate Property accordingly.

The Product qualifier rules defines a rule in an arrangement to arrive at a result, and the result of the rule triggers another Activity on the same arrangement or a linked arrangement.

The system allows restrictions on an Arrangement Activity in full, wherein the Activity cannot be run altogether or prevent it from occurring by restricting it. The Activity that is restricted must be a valid Activity under AA.ACTIVITY .

There are no specific limitations in activity restrictions and periodic attributes for loans in TBC. For loans in TBC, the user can define the product qualifier rules using routines instead of the Rules engine.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes the configuration of Activity Restriction and Periodic Attributes.


##### Periodic Attribute in Activity Restrictions

The Periodic Attribute controls the attribute values of an arrangement over a period, through Periodic Rules. To achieve this, the Periodic Attribute is associated with a Product Condition.

When associating a Periodic Attribute with a Product Condition, it should:

- Define a comparison value for evaluation.
- Define a Break Result and Break Charge (it is optional).

When a Periodic Attribute is successfully associated with a Product Condition, the comparison value is evaluated against a specific value of the arrangement during run time.

The result of the comparison may lead to a Break Result Override with or without Charge or Error to stop further process, based on the condition setup.

> **⚠️ Note:** PROPERTY.CLASS=ACTIVITY.RESTRICTION

The Activity Restriction Property Class provides the following Periodic Attribute Classes from which users can define Periodic Attributes.


##### Types of Activity Restriction

Some of the standard Periodic Attribute Classes and Periodic Attributes used in loans are described below.

The user can restrict the maximum amount allowed for the Activity for any single activity. This amount is assumed as the Txn Amount in the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY record for the current activity that is processed.

The user can restrict the minimum amount allowed for the Activity for any single activity. This amount is assumed as the Txn Amount in the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY record for the current activity being processed.

The user can restrict the amount of an activity to be in multiples specified as the associated PR.VALUE . For example, if disbursal is allowed only in multiples of 5,000, a rule value of 5,000 should be defined. Processing validates that the current activity amount is a multiple of the defined amount.

The user can restrict the maximum total amount for an activity over a specified period (defined in AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE ).

The total amount that has to be disbursed over a 3-month period can be restricted using this rule. Processing determines the total amount processed within the defined period to date, and calculate and verify if the current activity request is within the specified maximum value. If it is not, either an error or override message appears.

The user can restrict the number of activities over a specified period. The maximum number of transactions allowed in a period is defined in the associated PR.VALUE . Processing determines the number of activities of the current type requested in the processing period and validates that an additional activity is within the allowed number.

The user can use this restriction to control repayment amounts by comparing the repaid amount as a percentage of the available loan balance at the start of the restriction period. The periodic attribute can be validated when a repayment is made against the loan. The periodic rule can be linked to an activity of the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PAYMENT.RULES Class. The processing takes the current committed loan balance at the calculated start period, calculates the percentage, and compares it with the total repayment in the period.

This attribute class is similar to CURR.LOAN.REPAY.TOLERANCE but provides a restriction to the repaid amount as a percentage of the total committed loan balance at the start of a given period. The periodic attribute can be validated when a repayment is made against the loan. The periodic rule can be linked to an activity of the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PAYMENT.RULES Class. The processing takes the total committed loan balance at the calculated start period, calculates the percentage, and compares it with the total repayment in the period.


##### Cooling Off in Periodic Attributes of Activity Restrictions

The Cooling Off attribute in the Term Amount Property Class indicates the period within, if an arrangement is closed, interest cannot be charged and no preclosure charges are levied. In order to achieve this, Rule Start of Periodic Attribute is set as Cooling Off in that Rule break Charge of loan pre-closure.

When an arrangement is pre-closed after the cooling off period, to assess a charge for preclosure, the following configuration is done under periodic attributes, and an option in Rule Start called Cooling Off controls the collection of charges. This option decides the start date of the periodic restriction. When Cooling Off is opted, the periodic restriction starts from the date of cooling date as specified in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS .

The Periodic Attribute is set to cooling off and period is 1 year, which implies the rule applies after cooling period for the first year (initial) of the arrangement.

Activity Restriction is set to control the Principal Decrease for the first one year after cooling period, the system triggers the override indicating the same and levies a charge for the same.


##### Illustration: Loan Payoff Setup

The Periodic Attribute under the Activity Restriction Property Class to restrict the PAYOFF Activity after cooling period is described below.

The Periodic Attribute is triggered after the Cooling off Period.

Payoff Activity is evaluated again during the Cooling off Period and triggers a charge during the Payoff Activity.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the different Activity Restriction Types available on Activities.


##### Activity Restriction Types

- Activity Restrictions—when activity restriction rules can be defined based on the activity itself (the number or count of activities or amount of the activity) or on the balances that are affected by this activity (minimum balance requirements).
- Balance Rules—when activity restriction rules are based on balance types, whenever an Activity is triggered, it can be specified to check a balance and further assign a charge if the rule is broken. For example, minimum balance requirements in an account, maximum balance permitted in an account and so on.
- Transaction Rules—when transaction rules are based on the transaction amount and the transaction count. Transaction Amount—when the activity rules are based on the Transaction Amount, whenever the activity occurs the transaction amount rules are checked. A charge can be assigned if the rule is broken. For example, transaction amount must be in multiples of 500, prescribe minimum transaction amount for initial funding of an account, etc. Transaction Count—when the activity restriction rules are based on the Transaction Count, when the activity is triggered, the transaction count rules are checked. A charge can be assigned if the rule is broken. For example, debits in an account cannot exceed 12 in a year, monthly three credits in an account generally permitted, any extra credit can attract a charge.


##### Complete Restriction

- It is possible to impose complete restriction on an Activity. When the user tries to trigger the Activity, the system displays an error with a description stating the reason for restriction. A few examples of complete restriction listed below: Amount below minimum balance is not accepted as initial deposit. Cash withdrawal cannot exceed the number of times in a calendar month.
- To define complete restriction, the Result attribute in the Activity Restriction Property Class must be defined as ERROR.


##### Partial Restriction

- Partial or conditional restriction is also based on Activities. The activity is permitted, with an override or additionally, with a charge. A few examples of partial restriction are listed below: Allow receipts in an account, but only in multiples of 100. Allow more than five debits in an account in a period, after approving an override.
- To define a partial restriction, the Result attribute in the Activity Restriction Property Class must be defined as OVERRIDE.

### 1.15  Advance Instalment Payments


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Advance payment of installments (Early Repayment) are the amount paid to the installments immediately following the period without reduction of interest, commissions and expenses derived from the contractual clauses.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.ACTIVITY`, `AA.BILL.DETAILS`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AA.PAYMENT.RULE.TYPE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *APPLY.PAYMENT*, *Advance Payment*, *Advance Payment Restriction*, *Advance Settle Date*, *Application Type*, *Apply Payment*, *Bill Status*, *Bill Type* ... +19 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Advance payment of installments (Early Repayment) are the amount paid to the installments immediately following the period without reduction of interest, commissions and expenses derived from the contractual clauses.

Advance payment options allow users to specify the maximum number of advance payments, which can be satisfied, and the number of advance payments at product level. It therefore caps the maximum balance (that is, max n of payments x payment amount) of the unspecified credit balance.

For certain products banks can allow customers to make advance payments towards their loan installments. When all past and current due bills have been settled, the remaining funds can be used to settle the upcoming bills in advance. When a customer makes an advance payment towards a bill before the due date, the following scenarios are possible:

- The advance payment does not result in any interest benefit to the customer.
- The advance payment of principal component before the due date results in an interest benefit to the customer. This benefit is due to the interest accrual on the reduced principal after the advance payment.
- The advance payment of principal, interest component before the due date results in an interest benefit to the customer. During the advance settlement of the bill: The system settles the accrued interest till date, the remaining interest component paid by the customer is apportioned towards the principal. Thus, the principal is reduced both from the advance payment of principal and any interest component that is apportioned towards the principal. The interest post advance payment is on the reduced principal after the advance payment.

> **⚠️ Note:** Advance Payment is possible for all payment types excluding the payment types based on transaction amount and routines.

There are no specific limitations for advance payment of bills in loan contracts using TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The customers can make an ad-hoc repayment of their loan amount that is outside the agreed repayment schedule and installment amount. In such cases, the system is configured to park such credits in the UNC balance. At the time of the regular due date (as per the repayment schedule), the system checks (if configured) for such balance and applies them for settlement purpose. The Apply Payment ( Repay from Credit Balance ) field should be set as LENDING-SETTLE-PAYMENT.RULES Activity for the same. If the balance available in UNC is insufficient to settle the installment amount, then the system debits the settlement account for the differential amount.

The customers also have an option to request for an installment to be skipped. The system is capable of handling such requests and this is accomplished by configuring the system with the feature pertaining to Request Payment Holiday or Postponement. The necessary setup has to be done to manage the Payment Rules and Payment Schedule that enables the system to read the installments that are skipped and recalculate the payment schedule.

The below screen shot displays the LENDING-SETTLE-PAYMENT.RULES Activity.

The following fields and the associated values have to be defined in the AA.PAYMENT.RULE.TYPE Payment Rules:

- Payment Rule Type — When it is set to Advance, the payment amount is applied only on the current balances of interest, account properties and advance due balances for the charge properties.
- Bill Type — When it is set to Installment, it indicates that this bill type is used in advance payment.
- Fwd Bill Settle — When it is set to Yes, it indicates that an early repayment of a bill component is included for updating delinquency amount of subsequent bills (as there is no outstanding bill whose delinquency amount could be reduced). Also, this attribute is meaningful only when the overdue condition has the required setup for delinquency processing.
- Advance Settle Date - When this field is set as DUE, the advance payment towards the bill components, settles the bills and parks the funds in ADV balance type from the payment date till the bill due date. This triggers a forward value dated apply payment activity and enables the bill settlement to be effective on the actual due date of the bill. On the actual bill due date, the system settles the due balance of principal and interest or moves the funds to unallocated credit based on the Advance Payment Rule Type setup. This feature is applicable only for the ADVANCE payment rule type of conventional loans and is not applicable for upfront profit contracts. This advance payment featureIt supports the constant, linear, actual, fixed equal payments, accelerated and, percentage payment types. Advance Settle Date is a no-change field, so once it is authorised the value in the field cannot be modified later.

The below screenshot displays the fields in AA.PAYMENT.RULE.TYPE .

During an advance payment, the accrued interest till the date of advance payment is collected by the system. The banks will prefer that corresponding tax for the accrued interest is also collected with the repayment of advance interest. To enable this, the Tax Inclusive field should be set as Yes in the corresponding Payment Rule Type used for the advance payment.

The system mandates that the Make Due field should be set as Yes in the Payment Rule Type when Tax Inclusive is set as Yes. As a result of this, the accrued interest collected in advance and its corresponding tax pass through the make due process thereby appearing in the loan statement.

The features pertaining to loan statements are not applicable for loan contracts in TBC.

The following fields and the associated values have to be defined in the Payment Rule Product Condition.

- Advance Payment — It denotes how the repaid amount is applied to produce the future scheduled bills in advance. This can be set to either Full or Partial. Full - Implies that the payment rules are applicable only if the payment amount can fully settle future scheduled bills. Partial - Implies that the payment rules are applicable even if the payment amount settles only a partial amount of the future scheduled Bills. The feature does not apply or control or restrict any repayment to bills issued in advance.
- Make Bill Due — It has no significance in the case of advance repayment. However, for record purpose, this field has to be updated and hence the value is set to No.
- Advance Payment Restriction - This field adds a restriction on the type of bills that can be settled in advance payment. It has the following options: NULL – Settles the current bill, creates and settles bills until all the payment amount is utilised. BILLED – Settles the current bill, sends the remaining to remainder activity. # (1 to N) – Settles current bill + n bills and sends the remaining to remainder activity. When a bill is issued in advance, it is considered as a current bill. For example, if the bank has set Advance Payment Restriction to 1 and the loan has bill issued (invoiced to the customer) in advance, then the customer can settle the issued bill and one more bill in advance.
- Settle Unearned Interest — This field is applicable for both conventional loans as well as for loans with markup interest (that is, Islamic Banking products). When Settle Unearned interest is set to Yes, the system allows the user to pay more interest than the accrued interest and stores the excess accrual amount in the Total Repay amount (TOT.RPY.AMT) field in AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS . If Settle Unearned Interest is set to Yes in a conventional loan, Advance Payment can only be set to FULL. Else, the system raises proofing errors. The below screenshot displays the fields in the Payment Rules Product Condition.

The On Activity multi-value field is updated with the list of activities (no duplicates possible) that triggers the payment schedule to be recalculated. Each Activity must have a valid record in the AA.ACTIVITY table.

From the Payment Schedule perspective, the Recalculate field is set to Term for the below activities:

- LENDING-DEFINE.HOLIDAY-SCHEDULE: This Activity is used to declare holiday.
- LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.RESPITE.PAYMENT: This Activity is used to make advance payment. PR.RESPITE.PAYMENT Product Condition.

The schedule along with the maturity date is recalculated based on the number of installments skipped.


##### Advance Payment of Instalments

The following section describes scenarios in advance payments.


##### Scenario 1: Advance Payment Benefit from both Principal and Interest Paid in Advance

When a customer makes an advance payment towards a bill that is issued in advance, the system can be configured to provide a benefit to the customer from both the interest as well as the principal paid in advance. The configuration for the scenario involves:

- Advance Payment option in Payment Rules product condition maybe set as FULL/PARTIAL.
- Advance Payment Restriction can be updated to restrict the number of bills settled in advance. The bill issued in advance is treated as a current bill and not counted in the number of bills settled in advance.
- Defer type periodic charge property can have the bills issued in advance and can be settled in advance.
- Remainder Activity must settle the excess funds in the UNC balance (unallocated credit). That is, it should be LENDING-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT.

The above configuration can be setup for all payment types excluding the payment types based on transaction amount and routines.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is possible to make advance payment types for fixed charges. It is not recommended to have advance payments for calculated charges.

The order repayment for advance bills should be: Periodic Charges, Charges, Interest and then the Principal. The interest component can be any interest like principal interest in the required repayment order. In order to collect the tax on interest component settled in advance, Tax Inclusive should be set. In the above configuration, the repayment order is

1. PCDEFER - Periodic Charges set to Defer with bill issued in advance
2. NEWARRFEE - A charge property
3. PRINCIPALINT - The interest property
4. ACCOUNT - The loan principal

After settling the bill issued for Periodic Charges, the NEWARRFEE bill (if any) is collected. Then, the principal interest accrued till the advance payment date is collected and corresponding tax for this interest is also collected. After this, the principal amount is collected for the bill.

It can be noted that, this repayment order includes Periodic Charges which can be collected in advance only when bill is issued in advance. For other components, even when bill is not issued in advance, the bill can be generated and settled. When the bill is generated and settled, the flat charge, interest accruals till date and the principal amount in the bill are expected to be settled.

If the advance payment is not sufficient to settle the bill fully, based on the Advance Payment it is possible to settle the components for which funds are available and leave the Bill Status in Advanced. If the bill is settled fully, the Bill Status is Settled.

Any funds remaining after the advance payment activity is allocated as specified in Remainder Activity . It is recommended that the Remainder Activity is set as unallocated credit when the Principal Decrease activity has a charge associated with it.

After a bill is settled in advance fully, the next interest cycle is from the advance repayment date to the next bill due date. The interest is calculated and accrued on the reduced outstanding principal. The customer can use this benefit to recalculate the loan term or repayment amount. This choice can be configured in the Payment Schedule condition with On Activity and Recalculate set of fields as shown below. For FEP, the last instalment amount is adjusted for the remaining amount.

> **⚠️ Note:** When an advance payment settles the upcoming bill fully, the interest cycle is closed for the current cycle with the advance payment date, and a new set is opened for the next cycle in the AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS table from the advance payment date. For a loan that has an interest cycle due on May 23, if the bill is settled fully on May 16, the period from the current interest accrual period (May 1, in this example) is closed on May 16. The next cycle is opened from the advance repayment date to the next bill due date (May 16 to 23, Jun in this example).


##### Scenario 2: Advance Payment with Customer Benefit (Only from principal)

When the bank wants a customer to settle bills in advance and receive an interest benefit only from the principal paid in advance, the following setup should be in place in the Payment Rules product condition:

- Advance Payment should be set as FULL.
- Advance Payment Restriction should be set as BILLED (as part of the recommended setup).
- Settle Unearned Interest should be set as YES.
- Remainder Activity must settle the excess funds in the UNC balance (unallocated credit). That is, it should be LENDING-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT.

This is possible for all payment types in conventional loans excluding the ones based on transaction amount and routines.

- If Settle Unearned Interest is set for a conventional loan, then the Advance Payment field can only be set as FULL. Else, the system raises proofing errors.
- When a bill is issued in advance, then it is considered as a current bill. For example, if the bank has set Advance Payment Restriction to 1 and the loan has a bill issued (invoiced to the customer) in advance, then the customer can settle the issued bill and one more bill in advance.

This is the recommended set-up. With this configuration, the customer can pay only the issued bill in advance. The interest period gets cycled to the next billing date after this advance bill is repaid. The repayment amount is settled against the bill components as-is billed.

> **⚠️ Note:** During an advance repayment, if the bill is settled fully, then the ongoing interest cycle in AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS is closed as on the advance payment date and the next interest cycle is opened similar to scenario 1 .


##### Scenario 3: Advance Payment with no Customer Benefit

When a customer makes an advance bill settlement, the banks may prefer the bill to be settled in advance but may not prefer to pass on any benefit to the customer due to the advance payment. Also, it may not prefer the advance payment feature to modify any or all the following:

- The total profit or interest of the loan
- Effective rate of the loan contract
- EMI Instalment amount including all the components (principal, interest and charge) over the loan tenure.

This can be achieved by the configuring the following in the Payment Rules product condition:

- Application Type is set as Payment rule type ( AA.PAYMENT.RULE.TYPE ) record that has the following values: Payment Rule Type is set as Advance Advance Settle Date (ADVANCE.SETTLE.DATE ) is set as DUE. Make Due is set as Yes
- Advance Payment is set as Full or Partial
- Advance Payment Restriction can be set as: BLANK or/ BILLED or/ a number (indicating the number of bills that can be settled in advance).
- Settle Unearned Interest is set as Yes
- It is recommended that the Remainder Activity must settle the excess funds in the UNC balance (unallocated credit). That is, it should be LENDING-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT.

> **⚠️ Note:** When the Advance Settle Date field is set as Due, then Settle Unearned Interest field should be set. Else the system throws the following error: Advance settlement date not allowed when Settle Unearned Interest is not set. The system raises error when Advance Settle Date is set as Due and Make Due is not set as Yes. Advance Settle Date is a no-change field, so once it is authorised the value in the field cannot be modified later.

This feature for advance payment supports the constant, linear, actual, fixed equal payments, accelerated and, percentage payment types. It is not available for transaction amount based and routine based payment types.

During an advance payment of the bill with Advance Settle Date set as Due:

- The system triggers the Forward Apply Payment Activity for each bill that should be settled in advance.
- The Bill status is marked as Settled . For a partial settlement, the Bill Status is Advanced.
- There is no settlement processing on the actual due date of the bill.
- Any backdated activity that results in bill reversal, should also reverse the advance payments, and replay the bill generation and advance payment as applicable.

When the payment is received in advance, the following are the accounting updates or entries:

- The system raises an entry to post the funds to ADV value the advance payment date.
- The system also raises an entry for actual settlement of the funds to respective asset types namely DUE , DUE , DUE on the advance payment date value the actual due date of the bill.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is possible to settle bills in advance even when the bills are not issued in advance (that is, the InAdv field need not be set to process an advance payment when the Advance Settle Date field is set to as Due). When an advance repayment settles a bill fully with a setup that provides no benefit to the customer, an activity namely LENDING-CYCLE.PERIOD-INTEREST is scheduled for the actual due date of the bill to close the interest cycle as on that (due) date. Thus, the interest cycle must be closed only on the actual due date and the next cycle must be opened on the next interest period.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to advance settlement of bills, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Advance Payment Notification

When a customer makes an advance payment towards the loan, the banks can configure the system to generate a notification for the advance payment.

The loan product’s Activity Messaging condition can be set up to generate an advice when the customer makes an advance payment. This can be set by configuring an advice to be generated when the Forward Apply Payment Activity is triggered on the advance payment date.

In the below screenshot the loan product has the Forward Apply payment activity configured with an advice AA-0117 to be generated whenever the activity is triggered.

The advice record for the highlighted advance payment configuration is shown below.

When a customer makes an advance payment towards the loan, it is possible to send a notification to the customer for the advance payment. The system generates an event to notify the customer about the bills settled in advance due to an advance payment.

##### Advance Payment of Instalments

The following section describes scenarios in advance payments.


##### Scenario 1 : Advance Payment Benefit from Principal and Interest Paid In Advance

Customers can make advance repayment of a bill ahead of the actual due date of the bill and get the benefit from both the principal and interest paid in advance. During an advance payment,

- The system settles the accrued interest till date, the remaining interest component paid by the customer is apportioned towards the principal.
- Thus, the principal is reduced both from the advance payment of principal and any interest component that is apportioned towards the principal.
- The interest accrual after the advance payment is on the reduced principal after the advance payment.

To achieve this, the Advance Payment Rule configuration is given in Configuration . It is possible to make advance payments with or without the bills generated in advance. However, periodic charges can be collected in advance only when bill is issued in advance. This kind of advance repayment is possible for all payment types excluding the payment types based on transaction amount and routines

It is possible to allow a payment in advance to settle the bills fully or partially by configuration of the Payment Rule Type. Banks can control the number of payments that can be made in advance using Advance Payment Restriction . When a bill in issued status is paid in advance, it is not treated as an advance payment. Hence, the value of Advance Payment Restriction configuration should be chosen accordingly.


###### Charges Settled in Advance

While advance payments are possible for all payment types except the payment types based on transaction amount and routines, it is recommended not to have calculated charges collected in advance.

When charges are part of the payment schedule, the customer can settle these charges in advance like any other advance payment. If the customer prefers to payoff the loan in this scenario, there is an option to refund the charge if it is an advance charge collected, or retain the charge if it is an obligatory charge. Only charges with the Advance Property Type are refunded to the customer during a payoff. Any other charge is understood as an obligatory charge and retained with the bank’s income.


###### Advance Repayment of the Last Bill

When the customer pays the last bill in advance, the periodic charges, charges, accrued interest till the advance repayment date and principal component are settled in the repayment order defined.

When customer pays the last bill based on the bill issued in advance, he would make the repayment for the full bill amount. The remaining amount after allocation of different components (difference between the interest component billed and the accrued interest) is parked in the Remainder Activity . As all other components are settled, the remaining amount is marked as UNC balance which is the final Remainder Activity .

In order to close the arrangement, the user must clear the unallocated credit balance using the adjust balance activity and the arrangement moves to Pending Closure status.


###### Amendments in Loan

Any modifications in the loan parameters such as rate change, disbursement, and so on after the bill is issued and before the advance payment, does not affect the issued bill and the changes are incorporated in the upcoming bills. During an advance settlement, the payment towards interest component settles the interest accrued till date of payment and the remaining amount paid towards interest is apportioned to the principal (irrespective of the bill holding an principal component). Some scenarios in interest only payments are described below. When a customer makes a payment to settle two bills in advance:

- The first bill’s repayment settles the interest accruals till date and the remaining amount is apportioned towards the principal.
- The second bill’s repayment is only towards the principal as there are no accruals for that cycle yet.
- The recalculation of interest amount happens after the payment transaction is completed and the loan term or repayment amount is recalculated based on payment schedule setup.
- The third bill after the advance payment carries the interest accruals from the advance payment date (of first bill) till the third bill due date. This bill contains the benefit from advance payment (The bill or repayment amount or term is recalculated due to the advance payment).

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the difference in interest accruals from advance paid date till number of bills settled is accumulated and collected in the next bill.

When the customer makes an advance payment to settle one bill fully and the second bill partially:

- The first bill’s repayment settles the interest accruals till date and the remaining amount is apportioned towards the principal.
- The second bill is advanced, and the partial payment is apportioned towards that bill.
- The recalculation of interest amount happens after the payment transaction is completed, changing the term or amount based on payment schedule setup.
- The payment schedule projector displays the recalculated payment amount after the advance payment of bill. The bill settled partially in advance displays the actual settlement amount after recalculation only on the due date of the bill (or when the bill is settled in advance fully).

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the difference in interest accruals from advance paid date till number of bills settled are accumulated and collected in the next bill. In this case, the second bill is partially settled, so schedule projector of the second bill includes the difference in accruals and the bill on due date (or another advance payment) includes the difference in interest accruals.


###### Changes in Arrangement post Advance Settlement

When there are changes in loan parameters such as rate change, disbursement etc., after the bill is settled in advance (irrespective of bill issued in advance) the settled bill is not changed.


###### Advance Payments in a Suspended Loan

When a loan is suspended, the accruals are not posted to PL. Instead, it is posted between the ACC SP balance and the ACC balance.

If the bill in this suspended loan is settled in advance, the repaid amount is settled against the accrued portion of interest and the remaining amount is settled against the outstanding principal. The upcoming bills are recalculated to accommodate for the customer benefits from both principal and interest paid in advance. The ACC SP balance is cleared and transferred to PL only after the loan moves to Performing status.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to advance payments in a suspended loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Advance Payment in Charged Off Loan

Once a loan is charged off, the system does not allow advance payments to be processed.

The following is an example with rate change and partial settlements.

During an advance repayment, when the bill is settled in full, the current interest cycle is closed and the interest accruals for the next period is started from that day’s COB.

During a partial advance payment, the bill is not settled in full, and the remaining amount is made-due on the due date or collected during the next advance repayment.

##### Scenario 2: Advance Payment with Customer Benefit (Only from Principal)

When the bank wants the customer to pay in advance only one mortgage loan bill and receive a benefit only from the principal paid in advance, by settling the bill as-is billed, the setup as mentioned in the Configuration has to be in place.

The above-mentioned configuration is the recommended setup. With this setup, the customer can pay only the issued bill in advance. The interest period moves to the next billing date after this advance bill is repaid. The repayment amount is settled against the bill components as-is billed.


###### Advance Repayment of the Last Bill

When the customer pays the last bill in advance, the accrued interest till the advance repayment date is settled. The repaid unaccrued portion of the interest component in the bill is stored as a positive accrual balance in ACC and this is reflected in the Total Repay Amount (TOT.RPY.AMT) field in AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS . The remaining amount is apportioned and settled against the outstanding principal. Thus, the issued bill is settled as-is billed.

To close the arrangement, the user must clear the positive ACC balance using the Adjust Balance activity and the arrangement moves to Pending Closure status.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system can have a positive balance in ACC at the time of regular maturity as a result of advance payments. In such scenarios, the positive ACC at the time of maturity should be cleared from the arrangement using an Adjust Balance activity effective the last advance payment date (or) last payment date.


###### Amendments in Loan

Any modifications in the loan parameters such as rate change, schedule change and so on, after the bill is issued and before the advance payment, does not affect the issued bill and the changes are incorporated in the upcoming bills. During an advance settlement, the payment towards the interest component settles the interest accrued till the advance payment date. The remaining amount is apportioned towards unaccrued component of interest and stored in the Total Repay Amount (TOT.RPY.AMT) field in AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS . Thus, the accrued interest ends up having a positive balance after the repayment.

Consider the following scenario in interest only payments feature:

When the customer makes a payment to settle two bills in advance:

1. The first bill’s repayment settles the interest accruals till date and the remaining amount is apportioned towards the unaccrued portion of the interest component.
2. The second bill’s repayment also settles the unaccrued portion of the interest and updates the bill as settled. There is no recalculation as the complete repayment is towards the interest and is settled against the unaccrued portion of the interest.

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the difference in interest accruals from advance paid date till number of bills settled is accumulated and collected in the next bill.


###### Changes in Arrangement post Advance Settlement

When there are changes in loan parameters such as rate change, schedule change and so on, after the bill is settled in advance (irrespective of bill issued in advance) the settled bill is not changed.


###### Advance Payments in Suspended Loan

When a loan is suspended, the interest accruals are not posted to PL. Instead, it is posted to the ACC SP balance against ACC balance.

When this bill is settled on the due date, the due balance is settled against the settlement account and the SP balance remains as such. The ACC SP balance is cleared only after the loan resumes the Performing Status and the amount in the SP balance is moved to PL.

In a similar scenario, if the bill is settled in advance, then the due interest amount is settled with the settlement account, but the SP balance is cleared only after the loan resumes the Performing status.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to advance payments in a suspended loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Advance Payment in Charged-off loan

Once a loan is charged off, the system does not allow advance payments to be processed.

##### Scenario 3: Advance Payment with No Customer Benefit

During an advance payment of a loan instalment, it is not mandatory that a benefit should be passed on to the customer. In such cases, the bills are treated as settled in advance, but the balances are updated on the actual due date of the bill. For this, the system must be setup as mentioned in the Configuring Advance Payment of Installments section.


###### Periodic Charges Settled in Advance

It is not possible to settle periodic charges in advance when the Advance Settle Date field is set as Due in AA.PAYMENT.RULE.TYPE . The system triggers an error when such a case arises.


###### Request Payment Holiday with Advance Settlement

When the customer has made an advance payment and requests a payment holiday after that, the user has to manually request for the payment holiday after the advance settled bills.

Inspite of the upcoming bill being settled, if the user requests the payment holiday effective upcoming bill, the system reverses the advance settlement (as part of the reverse replay process) and declares a holiday for the upcoming bills. The funds of the advance payment are used to settle the bills after this payment holiday.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is a rare scenario where the customer requests a payment holiday after an advance payment. In such cases, care must be taken to request the holiday from the desired date (either upcoming bills or after the advance settled bills).


###### Advance Repayment of the Last Bill

It is possible to do an advance payment towards the last bill of the loan contract when the system is configured with Advance Settle Date field set as Due. The system settles the bill components as-is and on the maturity date the arrangement moves to Pending Closure status.


###### Amendments in Loan after Advance Settlement

When the upcoming bill amounts are changed due to any life cycle event of the loan such as rate change, schedule change, term change, partial prepayment or principal decrease, disbursement, etc., the settlement of those bills in advance payment are also changed accordingly. The system reverses the advance settlement of the bills and replays the bill generation as well as the advance payments as applicable. The Bill Status and Settle Status are marked as per the revised advance settlements for the new bill amounts.

In this scenario, the system modifies the bill components differently based on whether the bill was issued in advance or not.

- When the bill is not issued in advance, but an advance payment is made to settle an upcoming bill and a rate change, schedule change, disbursement, etc. take place, the system reverse replays the payment made in advance and apportions the paid amount to the new bill amount. Thus, the total bill amount is modified.
- When the bill is issued in advance, but an advance payment is done to settle an upcoming bill and a rate change, schedule change, disbursement, etc. take place, the system reverse replays the payment made in advance and apportions the paid amount to the modified bill components. Thus, the total bill amount is not modified, however, the components of the bill gets adjusted.

The following section describes some scenarios in Constant payments where the first bill is issued in advance and the second bill is not yet issued.

When the customer makes a payment to settle two bills fully in advance:

1. The first bill’s amount settles the first bill’s interest and principal components as-is billed. The ADV balance holds the advance amount for the bill from the advance payment date till the due date.
2. The second bill’s amount settles the second bill’s interest and principal components as-is billed. The ADV balance holds the advance amount for the bill from the advance payment date till the due date.
3. Both the bills have bill status as Settled .

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the system reverse replays the advance payment, and generates a new total bill amount to include the difference in interest accruals (due to the rate change) till the due date.

When the customer makes an advance payment to settle the first bill (which is issued in advance) fully and the second bill (which is not yet issued) partially:

1. The first bill’s amount settles the interest and principal components as-is billed. The ADV balance holds the advance amount for the bill from the advance payment date till the due date. The Bill status is Settled .
2. The second bill’s amount settles the interest and principal components to the extent of the amount paid in advance. The ADV balance holds the advance amount for the bill from the advance payment date till the due date. The Bill Status is Advanced . On the due date, the remaining portion of the bill which is still not settled is made-due and the Bill Status continues to be Advanced till the customer repays the full bill amount.

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the system reverse replays the advance payment and generates a new total bill amount that includes the difference in interest accruals due to the rate change. Thus, the total bill amount is modified based on the rate change and the amount paid in advance is apportioned to this new bill amount.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting due to amendments in loan after an advance payment is processed, the TBC generates an event which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Chargeoff

When the bank decides to chargeoff a loan, the system considers the advance payments also. It books the payment in advance to Account, Interest and Charge Chargeoff PL.

If the charged-off loan is configured with Advance Settle Date as Due in the payment rule type, the ADV CO and ADV CUST balance types hold the funds received in advance (till the due date) for the company and customer books respectively.

For the chargeoff accounting, the unaccrued portion of the interest paid in advance is stored in the ACC CO and ACC CUST balance types as a positive balance. These positive interest accruals in Cust and Co balances indicate the advance payment in the company and customer books respectively. As the loan accrues, the positive balance reduces till the due date of the loan.

On the due date there is no bill for the DUE CUST whilst the positive balance in the ACC CO is cleared.

However, If the loan is charged off, the system does not allow advance payments to be processed.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to handling advance payments which were made before the loan was charged-off loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Advance Payments in a Suspended Loan

If the loan is in non-performing status (that is, the loan is suspended), then the system does not allow advance payments to be processed.

### 1.16  Change Product


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Change Product functionality allows the user to change the product of the live arrangement within the product group.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT`, `AA.PRODUCT.GROUP`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Narrative*, *Product*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Change Product functionality allows the user to change the product of the live arrangement within the product group.

When a customer requests a Change Product for a loan contract in the TBC:

- The customer chooses a product from the list of products available in the interface for example at the TPM (Temenos Product Manager) level.
- The eligibility of the customer for the new product chosen is evaluated at the Enterprise layer, for example, at the TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) level.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The LENDING-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT Activity is triggered during Change Product. The Change Product Property Class allows the user to:

- Change the product of a live arrangement to another product within the same AA.PRODUCT.GROUP .
- Set the Change Product initiation type to manual or automatic.
- Set the Change Product Activity on a specific date or after a specific period (6M, 12M).
- Define the number of days by which the Change Activity must happen in advance to the scheduled date of change product, this is helpful to negotiate the terms of new product.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Change Product Activity can be triggered manually or automatically based on the Product Condition setup.


#### 🔧 Working With

In the below screenshot the change product is configured in next five months. The details are recorded in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS application.

The Change Product Activity is scheduled for the arrangement.

- The AA.ARRANGEMENT application specifies the status of the product. The status of the old and current products display as: PROCESSED - when the arrangement moves from old product to new product, the status of old product is updated. CURRENT - when the arrangement is running on the current product. SCHEDULED - when the product is scheduled for a future date status.

Below are the sample screenshots of the arrangement with the current and scheduled product with Active Product name.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Lending Processes (Retail)

Change Product Property Class is used by all products, which allow for a change of product during their lifetime or if any arrangement is to be renewed in its lifetime. It defines the rules and behaviour to allow arrangements of one product to change to another. Additionally, it supports rollover and reset activities.

User can list the allowed products for change product. When a new product is applied onto the existing arrangement, the user loses all his negotiations done as part of the old product.

### 1.17  Chargeoff


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *For financial and regulatory reasons, a bank is required to charge-off the principal balance of a loan. This may be determined by the bank, or can occur after bank examiners determine a borrower to be high risk and/or the loan is considered under-collateralised. Also, the customer is unaware that hi...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY`, `AA.BILL.DETAILS`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `CATEG.ENTRY`, `RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Bill Type*, *Charge Off Amount*, *Charge Off Percentage*, *Charge OffOrder*, *Charge off Amount*, *Charge off Percentage*, *Chargeoff Category* ... +14 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

For financial and regulatory reasons, a bank is required to charge-off the principal balance of a loan. This may be determined by the bank, or can occur after bank examiners determine a borrower to be high risk and/or the loan is considered under-collateralised. Also, the customer is unaware that his loan has been charged off; the customer’s loan record remains intact and payments are processed accordingly.

Charge-off is not a loan default. Loan default is where the borrower has failed to make a payment for an extended period of time, whereas charge-off is when there is no longer a reasonable expectation of further payments. The customer is not aware of charge-off and related activities in his loan.

The bank may charge-off the principal balance of a loan due to reasons like loan is deemed doubtful. The loan may or may not be in non-accrual status during a charge-off. The pending receivable in the form of principal, charges and interest of a loan can be completely charged off in a single stroke or the loan principal alone can be can be charged off fully, partially or in a series of partial charge-off transactions on loan principal.

When the user triggers charge-off of a loan through an API, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in the TBC to complete the charge off process. The TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting related to charge off. The features related to handling charge-off under FASB regulations are not applicable for loans in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The key features of the charge-off functionality are as follows:

- The customer is unaware of the charge-off. The customer’s loan record remains intact and the payments are processed accordingly (described under shadow accounting)
- A shadow record holds the charged-off amounts, etc for the bank's books
- The charge-off is done in a single activity or it can also be done in parts.
- Multiple partial charge-off transactions are possible and they are recorded accordingly, for the bank's balances.
- The calculation of interest continues in the charge-off balance.
- A full or partial charge-off can be reversed and corresponding changes to the shadow record are updated.

Read the Chargeoff Property Class for more information on the configuration of an arrangement being charged off.


##### Accounting Condition for Charge-off

When a charge-off is triggered, the loan principal has to be moved from the assets of the bank and booked in the PL indicated in the Chargeoff Category for the Account Property or Property Class itself.

For a full charge-off, the billed and unbilled components (properties) are to be charged off. For such interest and charge property or Property class, the Chargeoff Category and Chargeoff Special Income are used. Read Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts for more information on special income.

During a full charge-off, the charge properties in the form of activity charges, rule break charges, periodic charges are also charged off to the respective Chargeoff Category given.


##### Dual Accounting

All activities that affect the principal or an interest balance require dual accounting (that is, accounting on the customer and the bank balances). The following lists some of the key activities which require dual accounting:

- Make Due
- Apply Payment
- Age Bill
- Credit or Debit Arrangement


##### Make Due Accounting

Each time the principal or interest is made due, AA raises entries that credit current balances (that is, CUR and ACC ) and debit due balances (that is, DUE and DUE ). Once a charge-off has occurred, these debits and credits happen on the customer balances (that is, the CUST versions) and bank balances.


##### Apply Payment Accounting

Although dual accounting is required for applying a credit to the loan, a different order of payment is required and the charge-off balances need to be credited once the bank balances are exhausted.


##### Ageing Accounting

When the Overdue Property Class is configured, each time that principal or interest is aged, AA raises entries that credit the existing due or delinquent balances (for example, DUE or DEL ) and debit the next ageing balance (for example, DEL and DEL ). Because of this internal accounting (which many other banking systems do not do), the system raises bank entries as well as the customer entries.


##### Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts

The banks require the ability to process full or partial charge-off of the loan principal. This is achieved using the Charge-off Property Class. The LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ACCOUNT Activity triggers the charge-off in parts. The Charge-off Property Class dictates the order in which the account balances are impacted (for example, current first vs. oldest aged balance first) and the application order to be observed when applying a principal or interest payment to the bank balances.

- Charge-Off increase or decrease
- Extraordinary Income (this can occur when a loan is repaid in its entirety but the book interest is less than the customer interest due to accelerated repayment of principal)

In case of the customer fully repaying the loan, there is a remainder on the loan due to the lesser bank interest that is accruing as a result of the charged-off principal. The remainder or difference, ends up in the ACC -CO balance and this amount has to be debited and then PL credited (as extraordinary income). This scenario occurs only when the calculation source for the INTEREST Property is defined as total outstanding principal that is, current + due and age principal. PL for extra-ordinary income should be defined in Chgoff Special Income attribute of the Accounting Property Class.

When a loan has been charged-off, there are certain situations where the Credit Arrangement Activity (which credits UNC ) can result in a credit accrual in the banks’ books and this leads to confusing accounting entries. To avoid this situation, a new restriction code is added to the Activity to prevent a credit to UNC if that credit results in a credit bank principal balance.

When the LENDING-CHARGE-OFF-ACCOUNT Activity is triggered, the charge-off amount is based on the charge-off order.

- If the charge-off order is set to NEWEST.FIRST, then the amount is allocated from CURACCOUNT balances first. If any remainder amount exists, then it is allocated for bills (new to old).
- If the charge-off order is set to OLDEST.FIRST, then the amount is allocated from bills (old to new). If any remainder amount exists even after allocating the account Property amounts from bills, then the charge-off amount is allocated from CURACCOUNT balance.

When the LENDING-CHARGE-OFF-ACCOUNT Activity is triggered and if the Txn Amount is greater than zero, then increase charge-off is triggered and if Txn Amount is less than zero, then decrease charge-off processing is triggered.

- If the charge-off order is set to NEWEST.FIRST, then the amount is allocated from due account charge-off balances (Old to New) first. If any remainder amount exists, then the account property balance is allocated from CURACCOUNT balance.
- If the charge-off order is set to OLDEST.FIRST, then the amount is allocated from CURACCOUNT charge-off balance. If any remainder amount exists even after allocating the account property amounts from CURACCOUNT balance, then charge-off amount is to be allocated from due or overdue charge-off bill balances (New to Old) balance.

> **⚠️ Note:** The order in which balances are to be impacted can be defined based on the status of the loan. This option is available in Chargeoff Property Class and Payment rules Property Class.

| Balance | Source |
|---|---|
| ACCINTEREST | CURACCOUNT |
| ACCINTERESTCO | CURACCOUNTCO |
| ACCINTERESTCUST | CURACCOUNTCUST |

- If a LENDING-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT is processed, then the amount credited to UNC also credits UNC CUST.
- If a LENDING-DEBIT-ARRANGEMENT is processed, then the amount debited from UNC is also debited from UNC CUST.

To complete the accounting related to balance updates in a charged-off loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


##### Handling Charge-off under FASB Regulations

For handling charge-off under certain specific regulations (FASB), the bank user uses the CHARGEOFF-REPORTING activity. The user can trigger the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-REPORTING activity and specify the required Charge off Amount or Charge off Percentage .Read Working with Handling Charge-off under FASB Regulations for more information.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Charge off Amount and Charge off Percentage fields can be updated only through the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-REPORTING activity.

The features related to handling charge-off under FASB regulations are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Write-Offs

During a negotiation with a borrower, the bank can agree to write off a portion or all of the principal balance of a loan. A write-down is a portion of the loan that the bank agrees and is not repaid by the borrower. The bills are not generated and interest is not calculated on the write-off balance. The loan may or may not be in non-accrual status when processing a write-down. The system can write-off the loan principal partially. The banks require the ability to process full or partial write-off. This is achieved using the balance maintenance activities. The key features of write-off are as follows:

- The write-off amount has been deemed as uncollectable or forgiven
- The customer is aware, that a portion of their loan has been removed or marked as uncollectable.
- The repayment schedule is adjusted based on the remaining principal balance after the write-down.
- Both the shadow and the customer records have the written-off amounts (if a charge-off is already performed).
- Multiple write-off transactions should be allowed and recorded accordingly for bank's and customer’s balances (if a charge-off is performed)
- The interest is not calculated on the written-off transaction and the written-off amount is treated as amount that cannot be recovered.

> **⚠️ Note:** Charge-offs and Write-downs are not mutually exclusive. There may be situations when both occur on the same loan.

Partial write-off of balances can be performed using the Write-Off Balance Maintenance Activity. In case if a part of a charged-off amount is to be written-off, then the order in which the write-off amount is to be allocated, is determined by the Writeoff Order attribute in the charge-off condition. The order can be defined as BANK FIRST or BANK LAST. In a partial charge-off scenario, the option can be chargeoff the BNK balances first or the chargeoff balances first using this option. In a partial write-off, the system ensures the write off amount mentioned is less than or equal to the value of the bank’s CUR balance.

> **⚠️ Note:** Partially writing off any DUE or AGE balances is done by writing off individual bills that contribute to those balances.


##### Different Repayment Order for Non-Accrual Loan

A different payment application order can be specified for a non-accruing loan. This option can be different for applying the payments to CUST and chargeoff balances. The choices are indicated in the Payment Rules and Charge off Property Classes respectively.


##### Applying Payment Received

The payment allocation in loans that have charge-off can be different. The payment rule is different for the bank and the customer balances. This is usually based upon the value of the book balances and the status of the loan (for example, partially charged-off, fully charged-off or non-accrual).

The payment allocation for customer balances is done based on the definition in Payment Rules. The bank and charge-off balances is appropriated based on the definition in Charge-off Property Class. Similar to the Payment Rules, the Charge-off Property Class also allows the user to define the order in which bank and charge-off balances need to be appropriated and the order can be defined differently based on status of the loan, that is, Performing or Suspended.

In addition to the above, the Charge OffOrder attribute in the Chargeoff Property Class allow the users to set the order in which the account balances is appropriated upon charging off a loan.

When there is a payment received in a loan that is charged off, the payment received is apportioned against the outstanding CUST balances as per the payment rules given in the Payment Rules Property Class. Likewise, for the bank recovery, the payment received is apportioned against the chargeoff balance thereby apportioning the CO balances as per the payment rules in the Chargeoff Property Class. Here both CUST and CO balances are contingent balances.

The actual non-contingent entry for the payment done by the customer, reduces the chargeoff PL. Read Extraordinary Income in Accounting Events section for more information on excess payment.

In TBC, when customer makes a repayment to a loan that is charged-off, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting.

Read Configuring Loan Charge-off for more information on how to configure Charge-off for a loan.


#### 🔧 Working With

Working with Loan Charge-off Key Features Charge-off is different from writing off the arrangement. The key features of charge-off are: A full or multiple partial charge-off transaction is possible. The interest on the charge-off balance should accrue, but is not passed to income. Reversal of charge-off transactions is possible Removal from charge-off or partial removal from charge-off (that is, a lessening of the charge-off amount) is possible as well. Dual accounting –that is, having two sets of books, the customer record vs. the bank record and applying payments independently to the two records. The charge-off feature is available for the Lending Product Line. The Charge-off Property has to be included in the product for charging off an account. Activity Class - Charge-off Full/Complete Charge-off The LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT Activity Class is used for charge-off of an arrangement. The complete outstanding in the loan is charged off. Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts It is possible to charge off a loan, in parts. The LENDING-CHARGE-OFF-ACCOUNT Activity Class is used to charge-off the Account Property balance, based on the charge-off order. This is used to both charge-off an amount of principal (that is, increase charge-off amount) and to reduce the charge-off (that is, decrease the charge-off amount) if required. If a loan is being charged-off for the first time, this Activity is responsible for creating the charge-off balances as well as the customer’s shadow balances. Handling Charge-off under FASB Regulations For handling charge-off under certain specific regulations (FASB), the bank user uses the CHARGEOFF-REPORTING activity. Differences in TBC The features related to handling charge-off under FASB regulations are not applicable for loans in TBC. Dual Accounting For loan contracts, apart from the customer balances, it is possible to store two separate balances, the bank balances along with the charge-off balances. When a Lending Product with Charge-off Property is proofed and published, the system automatically creates the balance type records to maintain charge-off balances along with the customer and bank balances. For a loan that is charged off, for CUR , the balances prior to the Charge-off Activity is stored as a shadow CUR CUST. The charge-off amount is stored in CUR CO and the amount under banks book is stored as CUR . The CUR CO charge-off balance, is the contingent balance and CUR CUST is a balance used for internal purpose and CUR is only non-contingent in nature. When the LENDING-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT activity is processed, the amount credited to UNC is also credited to UNC CUST. When the LENDING-DEBIT-ARRANGEMENT activity is processed, the amount debited from UNC is also be debited from UNC CUST. Differences in TBC To complete the accounting to update the balances in a charged-off loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system. Shadow Balances When a loan is charged-off, the borrower is unaware of this action, and continues to receive regular billing notices. As a result, when a loan is fully or partially charged off there is a situation to maintain two sets of books: A customer record (that is, the customer’s view of the balances and bills) A bank record (that is, the bank’s view of the balances). Prior to the charge-off, the customer and the bank records are the same (and therefore there is only one set of books). However once a loan is partially or fully charged off, the views are different. Customer Record Banks generally don’t communicate charge-off decision to the customers. So, a customer is unaware of a charge-off. Copying the balances prior to the Charge-off Activity creates a shadow record. This now becomes the customer record and does not include any of the effects of the charge-off. The bills and payments continue to be processed normally against this customer record. The payments received have to be apportioned as per the Payment Rules according to the customer. The customer balances are apportioned in this repayment order. Bank Record Full/Complete Charge-off For a full or complete charge-off using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT activity, there are no bank balances. The BNK balances are zero in this case. Charge-off in Parts/Partial Charge-off A charge-off creates the shadow balances for the customer record that do not include the effects of the charge-off (that is, the customer is completely unaware). As a result, the existing balances (customer balance less charge-off amount) continue to be referred to as the bank record and includes the effects of the charge-off (for example, the charged-off balance). As the arrangement advances, it also contains the interest accrual on the bank balance and charged-off balance separately. Additionally payments to the loan are allocated in a different manner on the bank record than on the customer record. This is based upon the value of the book balances and the status of the loan (for example, partially charged-off, fully charged-off or non-accrual). Internal inquiry screens display both the customer and the bank record, once a loan is partially or fully charged off. Reports breakdown the information this way as well – including both the bank balances and the customer balances. Charge-Off Balances The CUR CO and each ACC CO balance corresponds to the charge-off balance for the principal and the interest respectively. The system creates these balances by appending a CO at the end of each balance type. Differences in TBC To complete the accounting to update the balances in a charged-off loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system. Multiple Interest Accruals For a full charge-off, the system accrues interest for charge-off and the customer balances namely CO and CUST balances. There is no bank balance to accrue interest for the BNK balances. For a partial charge-off (charge-off in parts), the system accrues interest for bank balance (for example, CUR ), charge-off and the customer balances. The system also accrues interest for the chargeoff and customer balances namely CO and CUST balances. It is necessary to accrue both charge-off and customer interest on the corresponding balances separately. Differences in TBC When a loan contract in TBC is charged-off, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting and balance updates. Full/Complete Charge-off During a full charge-off, the arrangement balances are moved to the Chargeoff PL. As part of shadow accounting, CUR CUST and CUR CO balances are maintained during a full Chargeoff. This results in the accrual of balances per Interest Property for each of this principal balance. Each of them accrues interest at the same rate but based upon their balance. ACC CUST is accrued on CUR CUST and ACC CO is accrued on CUR CO. Though multiple interest accruals are done based on different balances, definition of source balance for each type of accrual is not required. Product configuration contains: Property Source INTEREST CURACCOUNT Corresponding Accruals in a full charge-off loan are: Balance Source ACCINTERESTCO CURACCOUNTCO ACCINTERESTCUST CURACCOUNTCUST Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts In a partial charge-off, there are three balances: CUR , CUR CUST, CUR CO. Hence, there are three accrual balances per Interest Property and each accrues interest at the same rate but based upon their balance. ACC is accrued on CUR then ACC CUST is accrued on CUR CUST. Though multiple interest accruals are done based on different balances, definition of source balance for each type of accrual is not required. The interest is calculated on: Property Source INTEREST CURACCOUNT Corresponding accruals in a partial charge-off loan are: Balance Source ACCINTEREST CURACCOUNT ACCINTERESTCO CURACCOUNTCO ACCINTERESTCUST CURACCOUNTCUST Product Setup and Charge-off Balances When a Lending Product with Charge-off Property is proofed and published, the system automatically creates the below balance type records to maintain customer, bank and charge-off balances. Except bank balances, other balance type records which are created by system are contingent in nature. Bank Balances Charge-off Balances Customer Balances CUR CUR CO CUR CUST DUE DUE CUST CUST UNC UNC CUST ACC ACC CO ACC CUST DUE DUE CUST CUST CUR CO balance type holds the cumulative amount that’s been charged-off against an account. ACC CO balance type is used for posting the accrued interest on charged-off balances namely CUR CO. Dual Billing In the case where a loan is in Charge-Off status, AA.BILL.DETAILS is updated with both the customer and the bank due amounts. For a complete charge-off, the reflection of the charge-off billing is found in the billed balances. The bank amount is zero For a partial charge-off, two sets of figures (the customer and bank amounts) are calculated and stored on the bill. The customer and the bank amounts differ due to the effect of the charged-off principal as well as the alternate way of applying credits to the arrangement. Illustration of Partial Charge-off The changes that happen in an arrangement when a charge-off is performed is illustrated with the help of the below example. The arrangement is in delinquent status and is being charged off using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ACCOUNT Activity giving the transaction amount as 80,000 USD. This means 80,000 USD of principal is charged off. The Loan Arrangement Overview is displayed below. The Charge-off Activity is shown below. The Loan Arrangement Overview After Charge-off is shown below. Comparison of Arrangement Balances Before And After Charge-off The ECB balances before charge-off of 80,000 is shown below. The ECB balances after charge-off of 80,000 is shown below. Note that the arrangement balances have changed as a result of the charge-off. Bill Generated Before/After Charge-off On bill generation, AA.BILL.DETAILS is updated with both the customer and the bank due amounts for each of these accruals. AA.BILL.DETAILS stores the bank related fields that get updated on and after the charge-off of an arrangement. Once the charge-off is done, then the customer balances are stored in existing amount related fields and bank balances are stored in the BNK (bank) fields. Overdue processing is triggered based on the bills getting aged. The Os Prop Amt and Or Prop Amt fields of the bill are based on the customer balances(original amount) and regular overdue processing is triggered for the same. Balance type AA.BILL.DETAILS CUR Os Prop Amt Bnk Or Prop Amt Bnk CUR CUST Os Prop Amt Or Prop Amt Key Features of Full/Complete Charge-off A complete charge-off is done using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT activity. After a complete charge-off is made in the arrangement, the Full Chargeoff field in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS application displays Yes. During charge-off, the loan principal is charged off to the PL Category assigned to the Account property class. The interest is charged off to the PL Category assigned to the Interest property class. Any tax is charged-off to the PL Category assigned to the Tax property class. Validations During a Complete Charge-off When this activity is executed, the system performs the below validations and results in error in below scenarios: The bank performs the charge off after clearing any outstanding credit balances of the loan (like UNC/INV/AVL). Hence if there are any credit balances available during a charge-off, the system raises the following error. When there is a charge with outstanding pay balance, the arrangement cannot be charged off. The pay balance must be cleared and then charge-off should be triggered in the system. Post charge-off, the banks do not prefer to disburse any further loans or increase the loan commitment further. Hence, the disbursement activity is not allowed after the charge off. During the cooling and cancel period, the loan charge-off is not allowed. Any income to the arrangement is booked to the Chargeoff PL of that Property An arrangement that has undergone partial charge-off can undergo full charge-off, but an arrangement that is completely charged off cannot be charged off further. Loans cannot go to negative rate when loan is in charge-off. Dormant loans cannot be charged off. When an arrangement has a charge set to amortise, the charge cannot be charged off. The system raises an error when the user tries to do a full charge-off when there is a charge amortisation in progress. During charge-off, the system calculates the penalty interest if this has been configured and this helps the bank to access the real charge-off amount for all the property.
