In a business situation where the bank user must capture a bill in a loan that has undergone charge-off, the user can do so with the capture bill (LENDING-CAPTURE.BILL-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE) activity on such a loan. This activity can be used only for the arrangement that has undergone a full charge-off (LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT). As a result of this bill capture activity, the system releases the bill and balances in the customer books and the charge-off books.

Consider a scenario of dispute with the customer and the contract is charged off. The bank prefers to collect some charges or re-raise a bill that was previously paid, due to a customer dispute. In this case, the bank user can capture the bill and record it as an outstanding amount with the customer.

Consider a loan that is fully charged off using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT activity. The balances charged-off include the principal and interest as highlighted below.

- Charge-off principal - 46,369.61 (Outstanding principal).
- Charge- off interest - 31.62 (Accrued interest amount after the first installment).

This loan has only one installment bill which is already settled.

In this example, the client has raised a dispute with the bank on the 3871.49 bill dated Apr 12, 2023. So, the bank decides to refund the bill. At a later date, the claim is proved false and the bank wanted to raise the bill with the same amount for the customer.

The user captures the bill in this charged-off loan using the LENDING-CAPTURE.BILL-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE activity. The details of Bill Type , Payment Type , Payment Method , Payment amount , Property , Original Property Amount , and New Property Amount are entered based on the first installment bill details.

Though the bill is to claim the dues that were refunded earlier, the capture bill can be raised only for the current value date (not forward or back-valued) for the required payment type, bill type, and the bill amount for the components required. The bill date must also be the current date (not forward or back-valued).

Post capture bill activity, a due bill is created, and the system automatically updates the respective charge-off balances and customer balances in ECB.

Post capture bill activity:

- The charge-off principal is updated as 50000 (46169.61 + 3830.39)
- The charge-off interest is updated as 72.72 (31.62 + 41.10).

When an activity is triggered back-valued after this capture bill activity, the capture bill activity is also effectively reversed and replayed. As the bill is a manually created bill, the components of the bill do not undergo a change but the bill is reversed and replayed staying unaffected.

When a loan contract in TBC is charged-off, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting and balance updates.

The following section provides examples of using SUSPEND.STATUS and CHARGEOFF.STATUS periodic attributes

The SUSPEND.STATUS periodic attribute allows the user to evaluate if loan is suspended or not and suitably configures any activity restrictions based on the suspense status of the loan. The evaluation is done based the suspend information stored in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS and allows the bank user to configure an error/override in the Activity Restriction condition.

Consider an example in which user needs to restrict a charge-off operation on a performing loan which is not suspended. If this periodic attribute is configured at product or arrangement level, then a user cannot trigger the charge off activity on a loan which is not suspended.

A rule is configured to check if the loan is in suspended status or not.

The rule is evaluated when an activity (charge off activity is considered in the case below) is triggered and based on the evaluation result an override (or error) is raised. Additionally, a rule break charge is applied if necessary.

This periodic attribute allows the user to evaluate and place activity restrictions based on the charge off status of the loan. This evaluates the charge off information in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS and allows the bank user to configure an error/override in Activity Restriction condition, based on the charge off status of the loan.

Consider an example in which user needs to restrict a resume operation on a charged-off loan. If this periodic is configured at product or arrangement level, then the user cannot trigger resume on a loan which is fully and/or partially charged-off.

A rule is configured to check if the contract is in suspended status or not. The rule can be configured to evaluate if loan is fully or partially charged-off.

The rule is evaluated when an activity (resume activity is considered in the case below) is triggered and based on the evaluation result an override (or error) is raised. Additionally, a rule break charge is applied if necessary.

The features related to handling charge-off under FASB regulations are not applicable for loans in TBC.

### 1.18  Charges


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Charges can be scheduled on a regular frequency on occurrence of a specific activity or on breaching the terms and conditions of the product features. These charges can be fixed or calculated amount or combination of both of them and these can be calculated on tiered amounts.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCRUAL.DETAILS.HANDOFF`, `AA.ACCRUAL.FREQUENCY`, `AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING`, `AA.PROPERTY`, `AC.ALLOCATION.RULE`, `AC.BALANCE.TYPE`, `AC.EVENT`, `EB.ACCRUAL` ... +2 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accrue*, *Accrue Amort*, *Accrue Period*, *Amort Period*, *Arrangement*, *Booking.Cm*, *Effective Phase*, *Event Type* ... +6 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Charges can be scheduled on a regular frequency on occurrence of a specific activity or on breaching the terms and conditions of the product features. These charges can be fixed or calculated amount or combination of both of them and these can be calculated on tiered amounts.

- Discounts can be given on the calculated charge before applying the predefined cap and floor amount.
- It is possible to accrue or amortise the charges over a period. It is also possible to stop and resume the amortisation of the charges over a period after the loan moves into non-performing status. Realisation of income is as follows: Suspend mode functionality - When the suspended loan is resumed, the realisation of income/expense which was suspended is booked to P/L immediately. Stop mode functionality – When the suspended loan is resumed, the realisation of income/expense which was stopped is resumed with a new straight line amount based on the residual tenure of the loan.
- The charge amount can be in a currency, which is different from the currency of account based on product requirements.
- The charges applied on certain activities can be grouped and collected in regular frequencies.
- The charges calculated can be waived fully or partially on charge assessment. The waived amount can be accounted to a separate profit and loss category.
- The charges can be paid to the customer as a bonus amount on occurrence of specific activities or on certain conditions. It is also possible to suspend or resume the accrual or amortisation of a ‘Credit’ type charge.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to charges (such as for suspension, accrual and amortisation of charges and so on), the TBC generates an event which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes the configuration of charges.


##### Opt Currency Charge

The Charge Property Class is dated and optionally currency specific. It can be forward dated and more than one instance can be added in the same product. It supports variation and is available for External Products. Charges can be used in the Inheritance Property Class and can be set to tracking, non-tracking or custom tracking. Optionally, delayed tracking is also possible.

For loans in TBC, the Inheritance property class is not applicable as it is used only for the purpose of balance netting. Therefore, it is not possible to use a charge in the inheritance property class for loans in TBC.

The user can define and the system can evaluate the variations in the charge amounts (that is, preferential pricing) based on factors such as customer details, channel and so on, at the enterprise layer that is, TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).

The features related to usage of charges in external products are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Charge Override

The Charge Override Property is visible in the arrangement only after the charge is triggered and validated. It is used to make any discounts on the Property.

The features related to charge override are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Charge Currency Different From Arrangement Currency

If the currency defined in the arrangement and the currency of the arrangement fee are different, then the system raises an override.

If the requesting currency and the currency defined in this field are different, then the system converts the base amount to charge currency equivalent and calculates the charge amount. The final charge amount is again converted to the requesting currency equivalent. The system calculates the converted amount using the mid-rate. The Tier Groups field defines the calculation method of charge amount for the currency. This field accepts two values namely, BANDS and LEVELS.


##### Rule Break Charges

The user can specify periodic rules in specific Product Conditions. For example, in a Term Amount Product Condition, the user can attach a periodic rule, which can be set to increase the commitment amount over a period of one year, but it cannot exceed 10% of the original commitment. When the user links such periodic rules in a Product Condition, it is possible to link a Charge Property to collect it when the rule is broken. The charge can be a fixed amount or calculated on a base amount.


##### Amortisation of Charges

Charges can be amortised by setting the Accrue Amort field as AMORT and the Accrue Period as MATURITY or defining a valid period (such as 1M, 1Y, etc.) in the AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING record. Booking of charge to income (PL) is amortised and the income is distributed to numerous period based on the amortisation term set in the AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING record and the accrual frequency set in the AA.ACCRUAL.FREQUENCY for the specific Charge Property.

If the Accrue Amort field is set to AMORT and the Accrue Period is set to 1Y, then the system amortises the charge till the end of the defined Accrue Period and the accrual depends on the frequency set for the Charge Property. The Mvmt Cr Txn and Mvmt Dr Txn fields need to be specified for the accrual of the charge amortised.

The EB.ACCRUAL record is created when a charge is amortised and holds the details of amortisation of charges such as amount of charge, charge property, start or end date of amortisation, frequency, and accrual particulars.

The below screenshot displays the AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING record.

An AC.BALANCE.TYPE record has to be created for the Booking.Cm code specified in the AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING record.

The below screenshot displays the AC.BALANCE.TYPE record.

##### Preferential Pricing

Preferential pricing refers to the use of any of the available methods (such as, Product Variations, Relationship Pricing and Promotional Pricing) to provide customers with interest rates or charges, which are better than the standard product.

The below screenshot displays the Preferential Pricing.

It is possible to define pricing benefits (that is, preferential pricing) for certain loan contracts based on factors such as customer age, rating, channel and so on. The user can define preferential pricing for loans in TBC and the system can evaluate at the enterprise layer that is, TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).


##### Rebate Processing

A rebate is the ability to create and credit the customer a payable charge. This rebate (as a credit to the customer) can happen at the point of arrangement creation or during the life of the arrangement.

The rebate canbe paid out to the customer by using the Payout Rules Property.

For credit charges (rebates), Property Type is selected as Credit in AA.PROPERTY . This indicates that this property is a payable charge to the customer and not a due charge from the customer.

As it is possible to credit the charge or rebate to the customer, PAY balance type is available for loan products.

Once this is set, the bank can calculate the credit charge in the same way as a debit charge. It can be configured:

- As an activity charge, credit to be given when a certain activity occurs
- In the Payment Schedule, on a pre-defined frequency or on a certain date
- Using the rules defined in Activity Restriction

Rebates can be applied to the customer with the following options:

- Capitalised – In this method, the amount is credited to the customer's current balance and thus reducing the outstanding amount.
- Pay (Made Due) – In this method, the amount is credited to a pay balance that can be settled either automatically or manually.
- Deferred – In this method, the activity is deferred to a later stage and eventually made due or capitalized from the payment.

The following accounting events are added to the existing allocation rules used for charges and settlement in loan products.

- CHARGE-ACT.MAKE.DUE-PAY
- CHARGE-ACT.CAPITALISE-DUE
- CHARGE-PAY-PAY
- CHARGE-ADJUST.BILL-PAY-OS.ADJ
- CHARGE-CAPTURE.BILL-PAY
- SETTLEMENT-SETTLE-PAY

The below screenshot displays SETTLEMENT-SETTLE-PAY in LOAN-SETTLE.

It defines the charges that need to be applied when an activity is triggered on the arrangement. The event triggers the rebate charge defined at the product level. On triggering this event, the rebate is credited to the customer.

The below screenshot displays the Activity Charges Product Condition.

The rebate can be paid to the customer by using the Payout Rules definition. The below screenshot displays LENDING.PAYOUT record in Payout Rules Product Condition.

Amortisation is available for rebates to realise PL from charge over a period. ##### Phase Based Charge Conditions

The system provides an option to define charges for a product. The charges can be different at various life cycle of the product, based on the requirement of the banks or financial institutions. The bank can set up charges by configuring the Effective Phase field in the Product Phases tab of the Product Designer. Read Product Phase to set up charges and read Overpayment section for a detailed example for phase based charges.


##### Pre-Closure and Dues Settlement

In an arrangement, it is possible to generate the schedules before the cooling period expires. In such a scenario, any interest, charges or principal amount that is due, has to be settled by the customer before the user can close the arrangement.


##### Tax on Charges

The Tax Property is currency based, dated and can be multiple. It is possible to define the Property on which the tax is to be calculated and the corresponding Tax code and Tax type condition for the corresponding Tax property. The Tax Property can be Property specific and Property Class specific. The bill is updated with the Tax amount and the Tax property for the corresponding Charge Property. Tax cannot be scheduled when a scheduled property has tax to be calculated for that property, tax property, and the amount is displayed in the enquiry.


##### Pre-Closure of a Loan and Rebate Processing

When a loan is pre-closed, the bank rebates the insurance amount pertaining to the residual term. At the time of pre-closing, the closure charges along with the rebate amount are considered to compensate for the calculated outstanding amount. When the insurance contract is for a specific period, the unamortised amount for a certain period (that is, from the pre-closure date to the actual maturity date) is rebated.

##### Rebate Processing

The below screenshot displays the rebate processing.

For some loan products, the customers protect their loan commitment with the help of insurance covers against risks such as death and disability. The insurance policy can be for the entire loan term or particular period such as yearly and then it is renewed at the end of every period. Rebate processing provides a facility to rebate the outstanding amount of premium for loan insurance on pre-closure or on cancellation at a later stage or cancellation within a certain grace period.

The aim of the rebate processing feature is, to render the ability to use a local routine for certain types of amortisation calculation. However, in AA, the generic accrual processing mechanism allows the user to amortise or accrue fixed amounts supplied by applications through a direct API or accounting entries. The standard method of processing is to straight line the amount on a daily basis.

It is possible to post to an internal account category (instead of PL) in the Accounting version.

The user can define the start date of accrual calculation. From that day, the accrual and account postings begin. On the first day, the calculation is based on the beginning of the accrual period – Start Date in the EB.ACCRUAL record. The changes to the grace period is considered only if the record is reversed, and if the record is reversed, no accounting activity takes place.

This feature provides an option to rebate the outstanding amount of premium for loan insurance on pre-closure or on cancellation at a later stage or cancellation within a certain grace period.

Home loan insurance, or any mortgage redemption insurance plan, is part of a banker's sales pitch when extending sizable long-term credit, such as a home loan. These plans hedge the risk of loss in case the borrower dies or becomes disabled during the loan term, especially an unsecured loan. The banks fund the insurance portion as part of the loan amount, which is repaid by the customers as part of the loan. The insurance policy can be done for the entire loan term or particular period.

The solution deals with the option to define the grace period, rebate on cancellation of an insurance contract and insurance rebate on pre-closure of a loan.

#### 📖 Introduction

Lending is part of the Retail Banking AA suite of products and it supports the following Product Groups,

- Home Equity
- Lines of Credit
- Mortgages
- Personal Loans
- Small Business Loans

A loan arrangement helps the bank to record the terms and conditions of the agreement, between the bank and its customers, relating to the loan sanctioned. The Lending module allows the creation and servicing of arrangements. Activities such as new arrangement, early closure, take over, loan cancellation, charge off, interest reset, and so on can be performed on arrangements.

There are no specific limitations in creating lending arrangements in the TBC.

When the user requests the creation of a loan contract, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in the TBC to complete the process of loan creation. The loan contract is created under the product selected, from the list of products available.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section orients the user on configuring different kinds of lending products.


##### Defining a Lending Product

- The AA Product Builder allows the user to build or modify a product. Read the Product Builder user guide for more information.
- The user must associate the appropriate Product Conditions to the (loan) product to define the attributes (tenor, interest type, repayment frequency, charges and so on) of the loan product.


##### Proof and Publish

A product must be proofed and published via the AA.PRODUCT.MANAGER application to see the product in Product Catalog. Read the Product Builder user guide for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section allows the user to create different kinds of lending arrangements.

- While creating a loan, the user inputs the customers for the loan contract.
- A loan can be created through the Product Catalog menu. Read the Product Builder user guide for more information.
- The Customer and Currency attributes are mandatorily used to create (via Product Catalog) a loan.
- The system assigns the role of the customer as Beneficial Owner by default. It is possible to add multiple owners to an arrangement. When a loan is created via the command line, the user must manually designate the loan product from the Product attribute.


##### Understanding Lending Arrangements

This section orients the user to understand the Lending Arrangement.

- The Arrangement Overview screen is enabled once the loan is approved. Arrangement - This field indicates the contract reference number. Account - This field indicates the account number of the loan contract. Product - This field indicates the name of the product under which the arrangement is created. Arrangement Date - This field indicates the effective date on which the arrangement is created. Beneficial Owner - This field indicates the name of the customer. Status - This field indicates the status of the arrangement. The Arrangement Conditions section displays the product conditions negotiated at the arrangement level. Each tab (Account Static, Penalty Interest, and Schedule etc.) pertains to one Property. These display information specific to the arrangement.
- The Account Details section displays the following information: Financial Summary - This section displays the Overdue status of the account and also displays information on total commitment, principal, amount due, total delinquent balance principal interest, penalty interest and the total tax amount. Account Dates - This section displays the dates of various parameters, such as loan start date, effective date, next payment date, maturity date and also displays the duration of maturity of the selected account.
- Overview screen provides options for requesting a payoff, payment holiday, to amend the conditions.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Create and Disburse Retail Loan (Scheduled)
- Create and Distribute Retail Loan (Manual)
- Lending Processes (Retail)

The user can create a new arrangement for any of the lending products listed in the product catalog and the interest, charges and tax for the arrangements created can be amended.

### 1.20  Customer and Eligibility


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The banks offer different loan products to its customers. There can be a single owner or multiple owners for a loan arrangement and multiple other parties involved in the loan, for example, Power of Attorney or Authorised Signatory. These customers are not the owners (borrowers) but are important an...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARR.CUSTOMER`, `AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE`, `AA.PARTY.ROLE`, `CUSTOMER`, `EB.LOOKUP`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Customer*, *Limit Id*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The banks offer different loan products to its customers. There can be a single owner or multiple owners for a loan arrangement and multiple other parties involved in the loan, for example, Power of Attorney or Authorised Signatory. These customers are not the owners (borrowers) but are important and are recorded on the loan arrangement.

Loan products can be tailored to specific sets of customers, for example, the banks can offer mortgage loan products with different terms and conditions for regular customers, staff and non-residents. To enable this functionality the bank can define the criteria to define which customers are eligible to use the bank’s lending products. It is possible to set up different eligibility rules based on the role of the customer of the arrangement.

The eligibility evaluation happens on all involved parties of the arrangement and are reviewed periodically, according to the product configuration or re-evaluated when there is change in the customer information (customer static changes).

In the TBC, the configuration and evaluation of eligibility is performed only when TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) is used.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section orients the user to configure loan ownership and understand the eligibility criteria.


##### Ownership and Other Party

The Customer Property Class is used by all products to specify the involved parties of an arrangement and their respective roles. The Customer Property Class is primarily an arrangement level class, that is, the values are input at arrangement-level, and is typically configured at the product level as fully negotiable. Each arrangement should have atleast one customer who is the legal owner of the loan.

Each involved party should be recorded along with the respective role, at the arrangement level. The customer roles are configured in AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE .

Read the Customer Property Class user guide for more information on customer roles.

Additionally, other parties can be added to an arrangement with a designated role (Guarantor, authorised signatory). Roles of other parties can be defined in the AA.PARTY.ROLE virtual table, in the EB.LOOKUP file. All owners and any other involved parties need to exist in the CUSTOMER application.

The parties should be existing entries in Party TBC, rather than CUSTOMER application.


##### Eligibility

Eligibility rules for a customer to get a loan in a particular product are configured in the Eligibility Property Class. The banks can create or configure the rules using the Rules Engine. These rules can be used to set up the eligibility conditions. The eligibility rules can be evaluated at the time of loan creation at regular intervals and whenever there is a change in customer static information. Read the Eligibility Property Class user guide for more information.

Eligibility rules set is applied on all the involved parties of the arrangement. The banks can set different eligibility rules based on the role they play in the loan. If the party does not satisfy the eligibility condition, the system displays an error or an override based on the configuration.

An eligibility condition for a loan product based on the customer’s age is shown below.

In the TBC, the configuration and evaluation of eligibility is performed only when TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) is used.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section orients the user on working with new loan arrangements.


##### Ownership and Other Party

At the time of opening a new loan arrangement, a bank user can define:

- The owners of the arrangement
- Add any number of other involved parties
- Along with the role of each party. The system ensures there is at least one beneficial owner for the loan. The user can perform tax split for each customer and the system defaults the values from AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE .

The AA.ARR.CUSTOMER table, stores the parties involved in the arrangement, along with the tax liability percentage, limit allocation percentage and GL allocation percentage at arrangement level.

Under certain circumstances, the parties involved in the arrangement may be altered. It is possible to,

- Add or remove a party to the arrangement.
- Change the ownership of the arrangement, to another party.

The Change Customer Activity (LENDING-CHANGE-CUSTOMER) can be used to change the customer or to add other parties to the loan. These parties are evaluated against the configured eligibility rules, during the Change Activity. When the ownership of the loan is changed, it impacts any limit provided to the loan. The Activity triggers a change in the limit details required for the new owners.

- In the TBC, the configuration and evaluation of eligibility is performed only when TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) is used.
- When the customer for a loan contract is updated, the limit condition is also opened for the user to edit. Any change in the limit attached to the loan can be updated using the Limit Id field in the Limit condition at this point in time. The TBC generates an event to the external limit system in order to delink the old limit from the loan and link the new limit to the loan contract. The external limit system must approve the sanctioned limit for the loan and an event for the approval is received from the external limit solution. In case the external limit system has rejected the new sanctioned limit for the loan, the TBC reverses the activity for updating the customer on receiving an event stating the rejection of the limit from the external limit system.

With the Lending TBC, the parties should be existing entries in Party TBC.


##### Eligibility

The customer’s eligibility for availing the product can be checked during the creation of a loan, at regular intervals and when there is a change in the Customer attribute or static changes have happened at a party.

In the following example, while creating an arrangement for a student loan product, the customer’s age is validated for eligibility of the loan. The customer’s age has to be between 15 and 25. As it is found to be outside the limits for a student loan an error is raised as shown below.

In the TBC, the configuration and evaluation of eligibility is performed only when TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) is used.

### 1.21  Delinquency


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The banks require past due processing for the Lending products. The overdue can either be specified in terms of days or by number of bills. The financial institution can create and manage its own overdue statuses and can have different status for different products.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.BILL.DETAILS`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AA.OVERDUE.STATS`, `AA.PROPERTY`, `AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES`, `PROPERTY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Activity*, *Age All bills*, *Age All bills, Suspend*, *Arr Age Status*, *Arr Bill Type*, *Avg Amt*, *DELIN O/S Amount*, *Date Adjustment* ... +15 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The banks require past due processing for the Lending products. The overdue can either be specified in terms of days or by number of bills. The financial institution can create and manage its own overdue statuses and can have different status for different products.

The system supports the bank’s requirement to store information relating to overdue statistics, such as number of times, average days, average amount and the dates in which funds have moved into and out of a particular aging status. When the partial settlement of outstanding with overdue is received, the overdue status can be recalculated.

It is possible to manually age an arrangement to a specific overdue status.

When the payment date falls on a holiday, the system can be configured to defer the first ageing of the bill to the end of day (EOD) of the immediate working day, thereby allowing the customers to repay their obligations without any penalty.

There are no specific limitations with handling delinquency for loan contracts in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes delinquency configuration.


##### Overdue Balances

A balance is specified by associating a Property with a balance prefix. The Property must be a financial Property like ACCOUNT, INTEREST, CHARGE, etc. For example, a balance prefix of ACC (for Accrued) can be associated with an Interest Property such as PENALTYINTEREST, which results in an ACCPENALTYINTEREST balance.

Different balances can be created for different Properties such as Committed Principal, Due Principal, Due Penalty Interest, etc.

Different overdue balances can be created by its age. (Overdue five days Principal Interest, Non-Accrual Annual Fee, etc.) The below image displays a sample multiple ba


##### Overdue Condition

The Overdue Property Class is used by Products, which require past due processing. The AA Overdue processing is based on bills, which are produced for different Properties such as Principal, Interest, Charge, etc. as per the setting in Payment Schedule Properties.

The banks can create and manage its own overdue statuses (grace, overdue, non-accrual, etc.) and can have different rules for status change and for different products. These rules can be defined in the Overdue Property Class.

Ageing process can take place depending on number of days after the bill was due or by the number of overdue bills. This selection is made in the Type field where you can specify the number of days or number of bills.

In case, the user specifies the number of bills, the user applies suffix to the number by B. For example 2B to denote 2 bills. Further, in the Effective field, the user can indicate when the aging would come into effect.

Here:

- DUE refers to the change of status, which depends on when the bill has become due.
- OVERDUE.STATUS refers to the status change, which depends on the time of previous status change.
- Age refers to the change of status of bills. When a bill is to be aged, the user can determine whether or not the balances associated with the bill amounts should be moved to new balance types corresponding to the status. The user can do this by selecting YES in MOVE.BALANCES.

Read the Overdue Property Class user guide for further information.


##### Ageing Deferment of Instalment Falling on a Non-Working Day

Deferment of ageing allows the loan customers to repay the instalments falling on a holiday without any penalty until the EOD of the immediate working day.

The Pre Grace attribute is used to defer the ageing activity. It has the following two options:

- Forward - When an instalment falls on a holiday, first ageing of such instalments is delayed. A complete working day is given for the loan customer to repay the instalments without making the instalment overdue. When the customer fails to repay the instalments by the EOD of the immediate working day, a penalty is charged from the instalment date or the ageing status changes the date depending on the configuration in the Effective Date field of the Overdue property class.
- None - Ageing is calculated from the payment date irrespective of whether the payment falls on a holiday or a working day.

> **⚠️ Note:** When an instalment has reached the worst ageing status and the arrangement is suspended and subsequently, when there are new instalments falling on a holiday, the system does not directly move the instalment to the worst ageing status. Rather, it waits until the end of the immediate working day and then moves the instalment to the worst status in case if the customer defaults from the payment. This feature is not available, when Date Adjustment is set as PERIOD.


##### Tolerance in Settlements

A default value for tolerance is set as a percentage for DAYS.WITH.TOLERANCE.ML% Condition attached to the Mortgage Seasonal Product. Any amount paid below (2% in this case) the tolerance amount for the bill, the DELIN O/S Amount field reflects the outstanding due amount. At the same time if an amount is paid above or equal to the 2% tolerance, the DELIN O/S Amount field displays zero as amount and the bill ageing status as Settled.

A default value for tolerance is set as a percentage for the BILLS.WITH.TOLERANCE Condition. Any amount that is paid below (in this example, 5 for USD) the tolerance amount for the bill, the DELIN O/S Amount field reflects the outstanding amount. At the same time if an amount is paid above or equal to the tolerance, the DELIN O/S Amount reflects zero as amount and bill ageing status as Settled.


##### Overdue Statistics on Late Payments

Over dues in AA are handled by the Overdue Property Class. Overdue can either be specified in terms of days or by number of bills.

As and when a bill moves into a particular aging status, the relevant details like the current aging status and the date of movement is stored in the respective bill. AA updates overdue status in each bill and also updates the overall arrangement overdue status in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS .

It is required to store information relating to overdue statistics such as number of times, average days, average amount and the dates in which funds have moved into and out of a particular aging status. AA.OVERDUE.STATS records these details for every Arrangement.

The file called AA.OVERDUE.STATS is updated at every stage of a bill moving to a particular overdue status. The file has updates status wise until the latest aging status is updated in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS . Once an arrangement reaches a particular aging status all further bill amounts, as and when the bills are issued, are added to the oldest aging status as updated in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS irrespective of the aging status of the bill.


##### Overdue Status Recalculation on Repayment

When a few bills have been aged and are in different or in same overdue statuses based on the overdue definition of the arrangement, on full settlement of one or more bills, the ageing statuses of the remaining bills are recalculated.

This full settlement can be of two ways:

- Full repayment of the outstanding amount of the bill.
- Delinquent settlement, such that the settled bill does not age further.

However, for the above recalculation to happen the Status Mvmt attribute in the OVERDUE Property Condition should be set as Yes for the ageing statuses for which recalculation is required.


##### Penalty Interest Included as Part of Outstanding Bills

Penalty Interest rates can be scheduled and calculated based on the overdue account balances. In this case, penalty interest is a standalone amount, which has to be settled in the arrangement.

- It is also possible to store penalty interest as part of each outstanding bill, such that settlement and adjustment of penalty happens per bill.
- An Accrue by Bill option in the Type attribute is provided in AA.PROPERTY to store accrued penalty interest in the individual bills.
- AA.INTEREST.ACCRUE performs the accrual of bills when Accrual by Bills option is set for Interest Property. Normally, accruals are processed on the whole balance, but if interest Property is set as Accrue by Bills, then the new AA.ACCRUE.BILLS routine is called after normal accrual process is completed to update bill details with accruals corresponding to that bill.


##### Overdue Balances Accounting

According to the overdue ageing definition, the status of bills change when a bill is to be aged.The user can determine whether the balances associated with the bill amounts should be moved to new balance types corresponding to the status. The user performs this action by selecting Yes in the Move Bal field.

When the balances are moved from one ageing status to another, the balance types of respective ageing is updated. Different balances are maintained for different calculation purposes, reporting and activity restrictions.

The user can set to cause automatic suspension of the arrangement when it reaches a specified status. For example, suspension of posting accruals to PL when the bill reaches NAB status.

When a balance is to move to a suspense balance type, the user must have created a balance type with suffix SP. Now, PL is not booked from accrual of interest or charges. Accrual is credited to a suspense balance type, identified by the SP suffix.

The Overdue Condition can indicate that the arrangement has to be suspended, when it reaches a specified Overdue status.

To complete the accounting related to the balance updates during overdue processing in loan contracts, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


##### Manually Ageing an Arrangement

The user can manually age an arrangement to a specific overdue status by triggering the LENDING-SET-OVERDUE Activity Class. For example, when the user wants to age the arrangement to OD3 status, the LENDING-SET-OVERDUE*OD3 activity should be used. This is possible only when OD3 status has the Age All bills, Suspend and Move Balance attributes set to YES.

To manually age only the instalment bills of the arrangement to the specific overdue status say OD3, the user can trigger LENDING-SET-OVERDUE*OD3*INSTALLMENT. The system verifies the below conditions when this activity is committed and it raises an error if the conditions are not satisfied:

- If OD3 status has the Age All bills, Suspend and Move Balance attributes set to YES
- If Arr Bill Type is set as Instalment

In a scenario where an arrangement has two bill types, say Instalment (for instalment payments) and Payment (for charge bills) and Arr Bill Type is defined as Instalment. When the LENDING-SET-OVERDUE*OD3*INSTALLMENT is triggered, only the instalment bills are aged to OD3 and the payment bills are not aged to OD3.

In an arrangement that is manually aged, the system raises an error if Arr Bill Type attribute is changed. Any other changes to the overdue conditions are applied to the arrangement only when reset overdue activity is triggered.

In order to restore/reset the arrangement back to automatic ageing, the user can trigger the LENDING-MANUAL.RESET-OVERDUE Activity Class.

##### Overdue Statistics on Late Payments

Overdues in AA are handled by the Overdue Property Class. An overdue can either be specified in terms of days or by number of bills.

As and when a bill moves into a particular ageing status, the relevant details like the current ageing status and the date of movement is stored in the respective bill. AA updates the overdue status in each bill and also updates the overall arrangement overdue status in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS .

It is required to store information relating to overdue statistics, such as number of times, average days, average amount and the dates in which funds have moved into and out of a particular aging status. AA.OVERDUE.STATS records these details for every arrangement.

The AA.OVERDUE.STATS file is updated at every stage of a bill moving to a particular overdue status. The file has updates status wise until the latest ageing status is updated in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS . Once an arrangement reaches a particular ageing status all further bill amounts, as and when the bills are issued, are added to the oldest ageing status as updated in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS irrespective of the ageing status of the bill.

- AA.OVERDUE.STATS records the overdue amounts for every arrangement age wise along with the average amount of funds that lie in that particular ageing status and number of days the funds are lying in the particular status.
- The Od Status attribute is updated when the first bill reaches its first overdue status. The Start Date and End Date are attributes the dates in which the arrangement has overdue amounts in that respective overdue status. An arrangement can move in and out of a particular aging status many number of times spending a number of days every time it comes into that particular ageing status. Pr Avg Amt attribute is updated with the average overdue amount for a particular period within the same overdue status. This amount is arrived at by calculating the daily average of the closing balances for that period. For the purpose, two points are to be taken into consideration. The bill date and amount of a bill is excluded from the number of days count and calculation of average amounts, respectively. When a new bill is issued when the arrangement is already moved into any of the overdue statuses, the bill amount is directly added to the oldest arrangement overdue status, which gets updated in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS .
- The arrangement can move into a particular overdue status and come out of the same any number of times. The count of this movement is updated in the Status Count attribute.
- The Avg Amt attribute is updated with overall average amount that is lying in the respective overdue status. This is arrived by adding the period average balances and dividing the same by number of times the arrangement has moved in and out of the perspective overdue status. This is updated in the Status Count attribute.

##### Overdue Accounting

When an arrangement is suspended, the accruals and capitalisation of interest are normal in the customers’ perspective. Internally, posting of the income to PL is stopped and booked to a suspense balance type suffixed by SP, such as ACCLOANINTSP for accrued LOANINT Property Balance, suspended.

When the user requires the balance associated with a Property to be suspended, user has to set the Type as SUSPEND in the PROPERTY record. If SUSPEND is selected, it means that the Property can be allowed to be suspended. Only INTEREST and CHARGE Properties can be suspended.

If SUSPEND.OVERDUE is defined, it means that any overdue can be suspended when the underlying Property is suspended. To define SUSPEND.OVERDUE, the Property should already be set to SUSPEND.

If SUSPEND.OVERDUE is defined at the Property level, it means that when an arrangement is suspended, any overdue in the Property is also suspended. In this case, the system reverses all the overdue that are already posted to PL and suspends posting of further accruals to PL.

The Suspend Activity can be triggered automatically by ageing process conditions or can be requested manually.

Resume Activity refers to the following:

- Setting back from non-accrual status to accrual status.
- Requested manually or triggered automatically.
- Reverse the SP balances to PL.
- Resume suspended incomes automatically.
- Settles suspended interest accruals to PL and moves due charges income to PL.

When a bill is made due in an arrangement, the accrued balance ACC moves to DUE .

Due to non-payment of bills, bill for principal due and interest due is aged to OD1 status, their due amounts also move to OD1LOANAC and OD1PRININT, respectively.

When the customer pays USD 1,500 from the current account, the current account is debited by USD 1,500 and the payment is applied to USD 300 for due interest, USD 700 to due principal and balance USD 500 as Remainder Activity adjusted to current principal.

To complete the accounting related to processing overdue amounts in loan contracts, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


##### Manually Ageing an Arrangement

The user can age an arrangement manually using the LENDING-SET-OVERDUE Activity Class. This arrangement can be reset to automatic ageing using the LENDING-MANUAL.RESET-OVERDUE Activity Class.

Banks may prefer to mark a loan of customer as non-paying asset, if any one of the other loans have become a non-paying asset. In order to move an arrangement to a particular overdue status (worst status), the user triggers the LENDING-SET-OVERDUE*OVERDUE.STATUS activity or the LENDING-SET-OVERDUE*OVERDUE.STATUS*BILL.TYPE activity for the Arr Bill Type . Read configuration section to know more.

The user can choose the activity that has to be triggered from the Activity field to manually age the arrangement, as displayed below.

Since this product has only NAB status with Age All bills, Suspend and Move Balance attributes set to Yes and the Arr Bill Type as Instalment, the respective Activities are listed in the dropdown.

After the manual asset classification, the arrangement status is updated as shown below.

The manual asset classification can also be achieved from the single customer view of the arrangement.


###### Bills Generated after Manual Ageing

In order to manually age an arrangement to a specific OD status, the Age All bills is set to yes. When this configuration is in place, and a new bill is generated in this arrangement, the bill is immediately aged to the specific OD status.

Consider an arrangement that has two bill types in it, say an Instalment bill and a Payment bill and Arr Bill Type is set as Instalment. When the arrangement is manually aged using the -SET-OVERDUE*OD3*INSTALLMENT Activity, the new payment bill raised undergoes regular automatic ageing and only the new instalment bills are aged to OD3.


###### Recording Overdue Details

The AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS (a system maintained table) records the ageing status of the arrangement in the Arr Age Status field. This is irrespective of whether the arrangement is aged automatically or manually.

- The Manual Ageing field is set to Yes, when an arrangement is aged manually.
- The Manual Age Bill Type is updated with the bill types that are aged manually based on the manual ageing activity triggered.

The AA.OVERDUE.STATS is also updated with the corresponding ageing information. The arrangement overview screen reflects the arrangement status to which it is moved manually.


###### Repayment on Manually Classified Assets

For an arrangement that is manually aged, the outstanding bills are also aged. Consider an arrangement that is aged using the LENDING-SET-OVERDUE*OD3*INSTALLMENT activity, the instalment bill is also in OD3 status. When this instalment bill settled fully, because the arrangement is manually aged, the settlement status is updated as below:

- Settle status – Repaid
- Bill Status – Aging
- Aging Status – OD3

The bill status and aging status are updated as settled only when arrangement is restored to automatic ageing using Manual Reset Overdue Activity.


###### Resetting Arrangement to Automatic Ageing

The LENDING-MANUAL.RESET-OVERDUE Activity Class is used to restore automatic ageing in an arrangement which is available in the arrangement overview screen as seen below.

Upon clicking the icon, the user is provided an option to input the date from which the automatic ageing must be restored.

On committing and authorising the activity, system restores to automatic ageing process as per the latest applicable overdue conditions. When reset activity is triggered in an arrangement, the outstanding bills that should be ageing as per regular process. User gets the override message ‘Bills are aged as per overdue condition’ to indicate the same.


###### Migration of Arrangements from Legacy System

During migration, if legacy system has a manually aged arrangement, then during takeover the arrangement should also undergo manual ageing. After the arrangements are taken over, the arrangement is manually aged as required using LENDING-SET-OVERDUE*OVERDUE.STATUS (or) LENDING-SET-OVERDUE*OVERDUE.STATUS*BILL.TYPE Activity. The effective date of this activity should be the same as takeover arrangement date.


###### Restricting Manual Classification to a Particular Status

The arrangement can be manually classified to an overdue status that has the Age All bills, Suspend and Move Balance attributes set to yes. When the bank wants to restrict the users from ageing an arrangement manually to a particular overdue status, it can be achieved using Activity Restriction.

Consider an overdue condition has two overdue status OD4 and OD5 with Age All bills, Suspend and Move Balance set to yes. The bank users can manually age the arrangement to OD4 or OD5.

When the bank wants to stop the users from manually ageing the arrangements to OD4 status, the Activity Based Activity Restrictions must be setup in the product definition.

#### 📖 Introduction

The Lending product defined and processed under the AL module can have multiple interest types defined (for example, principal interest, penalty interest, commission, etc.). For interest calculation, different calculation methods along with different interest day basis is applied. The user can have interest types like fixed, floating and periodic interest rates. The user can capture a future dated interest condition at arrangement level. Penalty interest can be calculated and stored as part of each outstanding bill, such that settlement and adjustment of penalty happens per bill. It is possible to have the interest capitalisation cycle different from the principal payment cycle and thus extend beyond the payment end date. This module also supports negative interest rates.

From a system perspective, for arrangements that follow variable rate, it is possible to send customer notification several days in advance. The notification is on the new interest rate and the payment amount.

In TBC, the notifications to customers must be handled through an external delivery subsystem based on the events generated from the loan.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes the different interest configuration topics.


##### Floating Rate or Periodic Interest Key Changes

When a backdated interest rate change for either BASIC.INTEREST or a PERIODIC.INTEREST key is chosen, the system triggers the relevant activity based on the product line. As the rate change is backdated, the system does a reverse and replay of all the activities associated to the rate change date for all the underlying arrangements. The replay function then applies the new interest rate specified and recalculates the accrued interest accordingly. In the arrangement, LENDING-CHANGE-INTEREST Activity Class is triggered.

The interest rate can be fixed or floating and with or without margin. Compounding interest is also possible.

The changes to the BASIC.INTEREST (BI) and/or PERIODIC.INTEREST (PI) keys are updated in the associated arrangements by triggering the corresponding update activities as part of the AA Service Process during COB. The user can update the BI/PI rate changes to the associated arrangements online, by running the AA.ONLINE.ACCRUAL.SERVICE online service. Read here to know more about the online processing of rate changes.

The Interest Property Class describes the basic features. The configuration of the advanced features of the Interest Property Class is described below.


##### Interest Accrual after Payment End Date

There are financial institutions, banks included, that may require the continuation of interest accruals even after the payment end date. When required the system should not make due, the interest on the payment end date, instead extend the interest schedules.

Consider an example where interest capitalisation happens every six months, and the principal is to be made due every month. Now the feature here is to continue to accrue interest after the payment end date and extend the interest schedule after payment end date. On the schedule date, system triggers the capitalisation and make due.

This is achieved by setting the Extend Cycle field in AA.PAYMENT.TYPE (available for Interest Property Classes only). If not set, the system makes due the interest on the payment end date.


##### Periodic Rate Change Set in Advance

From a system perspective, for arrangements that follow a variable rate, it is possible to send customer notification several days in advance. The notification is on the new interest rate and the payment amount. Based on the prevailing rate, the interest rate is calculated. Based on the rate change, the system recalculates the repayment amount, and the customer receives a pre-notification advice.

This field accepts a valid period definition in xxxP format, wherein xxx can be a number between 1 and 999, and P can be M (Month), D (Days), Y (Year) or W (Week).

This Advance Ratefix Period field is suitable only for single tier type of interest having a valid periodic reset frequency. This is valid only if both the Interest and Payment schedule properties have Type attribute set to FORWARD.DATED.

For example, for periodic interest, if Advance Ratefix Period field is set as 7D and the next periodic reset activity falls on 01-May-2019; then the rate as prevailing on 24-Apr-2019 is fixed. Though on 24-Apr-2019 the rate is fixed, it is applicable only from 01-May-2019, which is the Periodic Reset activity date.

Between LENDING-ADVANCE.RESET-INTEREST activity and next LENDING-PERIODIC.RESET-INTEREST activity, the user cannot alter the interest definition. For future dated conditions, if Advance Ratefix Period field is set as 7D, then:

- A new arrangement is created on 17-Apr-19 with fixed interest rate definition;
- A future dated interest condition effective on 15-May-19 is created, with floating interest definition

On 08-May-19, the LENDING-ADVANCE.CHANGE-INTEREST Activity when triggered, notifies the customer about the floating interest details. Interest definition can be changed, from - fixed to floating, floating to periodic interest, or periodic interest to fixed, etc.

Between LENDING-ADVANCE.CHANGE-INTEREST activity and next LENDING-CHANGE-INTEREST activity, the interest definition can be altered.

The following configuration is available for a new Mortgage lending product.

1. The user creates new EB.ADVICES and DE.FORMAT.PRINT records and updates them in the Activity Messaging Product Condition.
2. On the Payment Schedule Product Conditions, the LENDING-ADVANCE.CHANGE-PRINCIPALINT and LENDING-ADVANCE.RESET-PRINTICIPALINT Activities are included.
3. The Advance Ratefix Period field in the PRODUCT.DESIGNER is set to the required frequency; in the example, it is 7D (7 Days) for the Mortgage Product Group. On successful proof and publish, the product configuration is completed.

In TBC, it is possible to notify the customers in advance about a change in the interest rate for loans with periodic rate of interest. The system generates an event to send a pre-notification to the customer about the periodic rate change.

To define the effective base for the conditions, which enables the new fields, the user has to add the associated versions in AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER .

AA Product designer validations – When the Property type is not set as Forward Dated, the system raises an error.


##### Periodic Rate Change after Accrual Date

When there is a backdated publish or republish of rates, the Rate Adjustment checkbox must be set as ‘yes’ to adjust the rates and the interest accruals for the arrangement.


###### Floating Rate Set in Advance

The system can be configured to notify a customer in advance about the change in base rate for floating-rate linked contracts.

When the user creates a new record in BASIC.INTEREST (BI) table for a future date, the system evaluates if the rate change is within the period defined for the advance rate fix at the product level. If yes, during COB the system triggers the Apply Rate activity for the current day’s date. This creates a forward dated interest condition, effective from the future effective date of the BI record, that is, date on which the rate has to take effect.

The system can be configured to recalculate the payment schedule during the Apply Rate activity. This Apply Rate activity then creates a forward dated condition for the payment schedule to calculate and store the new payment amount for the revised rate. This is based on the user configuration in the payment schedule for recalculation of payment amount or term. Apart from the creation of forward dated interest condition, the system also creates forward dated conditions for the payment schedule for the same effective dates.

Within AA, the Activity Messaging Property Class is used to send advices. The system can be configured to generate an advice on a specific event. The Activity Messaging Property Class can be configured to notify the customer about the rate change. Also, it can be setup to generate a pre-notice for forward dated activities.

The handoff information for the notice has the following details:

- Old rate as of pre-notification date
- New rate as of forward date
- Effective date of rate change
- Old and new payment amount
- Effective date of new payment amount

In TBC, it is possible to notify a customer in advance about the change in base rate for floating rate linked contracts by generating an event to send the pre-notification.


##### Interest Payment In Advance - Discounted Interest

Banks can choose to provide discounted interest for loan contracts where the interest amount on the loan is collected in advance before the interest periods. This can be achieved by setting the Mode field (under Default Values (Control) tab) in the Interest property condition to Advance.

The advance interest can be collected either at a regular frequency or at the start of the loan contract by configuring the payment schedule condition.

- Interest collected in parts at a regular frequency: Set PayFreq to a defined frequency.
- Full interest amount collected during the opening of the loan contract: Set Start to R_MATURITY.

The payment type for the scheduled interest should have Payment Mode set to Advance.

> **⚠️ Note:** When advance interest is configured for a loan contract, cooling period should not be defined in the loan.


##### Periodic Interest Rate Reset Rules

Periodic Rate - A periodic rate is tied to an index (for example: EURIBOR) which is further dependent either on period or time (for example, term) and possibly an amount. The user enters the periodic interest index into Periodic Index field. Once the arrangement is active, unless changed it remains the same. It is possible to have a predefined frequency in which the periodic rates have to be changed.

Periodic Reset - Date convention, date adjustment and business day centres forms the basis for the reset frequency. The pop up box at the end of this field, allows the user to select the required reset period. For example, if Periodic Reset is set as every month on last day and in ACCOUNT property, Date Convention set as Forward Same Month and Date Adjustment set as Period, the date of periodic interest reset is forwarded to the same month, if it falls on a holiday and moves backward if it cannot forwarded within the same month.

The financial institutions receive requests from customers to reset the first periodic interest rate in the beginning of the loan account creation, which is completely independent or different from loan account creation date, loan disbursement date or interest payment schedule date.

Initial Reset Date - This field is available in the interest multi-value set, to capture the first reset date.


##### Future Dated Conditions

The Type field and FORWARD.DATED value in the AA.PROPERTY.CLASS record allows the user to introduce a new definition at the arrangement level, and is dated. Once captured with a future date, the system automatically schedules this and during close of business:

- The scheduled activity is processed
- The new condition is applied to the arrangement

In the tool bar of AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY and AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE screens, a Show tabs for expansion icon is available. This tab helps the user to identify the property, which can have a future dated condition, and allows the user to add the required condition.


##### Custom Rate Calculation

Custom rate is a type of source rate calculation (others being fixed or floating or periodic or linked rate) in the Interest Property Class. By setting the Custom Rate field to Yes as part of the tier multi-value set, the custom rate calculation can be enabled. The user has to add an API to the Custom Rate Calc field to facilitate the calculation. To configure custom values for the API, the user can use the attributes such as Custom Type , Custom Name , and Custom Value .

The system invokes the CUSTOM RATE CALC API:

- During change interest activity by the core interest processing module
- During the accrual or cap or make due processing resulting in the interest rate to be derived dynamically.

The Runtime Rate Calc attribute when set to Yes, controls the run time calculation.

Given below is an example implementation of this custom rate calculation, used by the Balance Netting Cash pool.

In case of multi-currency AR accounts (memo) and in multi-currency interest compensation, currency weighted average rate calculation can be used.

The features pertaining to Balance Netting are not applicable for loans in TBC. However, it is possible to define custom rate calculations for loans in TBC.

The features related to linked rates are applicable for loans in TBC, if the linked interest is also defined within the same loan contract. However, linked rates feature based on the Deposit account is not applicable in TBC unless the Deposit account is available in the same TBC.


##### Phase Based Interest Conditions

The system provides an option to define different interest rates for a product. The rate can be different at various stages of the life cycle of the product, based on the requirement of the banks or financial institutions. The bank can set up interest rates by configuring the Effective Phase attribute in the Product Phases tab of the Product Designer. Read Product Phase for more information.


##### Interest Compounding

The system supports the compounding of both debit and credit interest. Compounding interest applies a factor to the compound interest calculation based upon the number of compounding periods in the year. This field defines the number of compounding periods that are applicable. Compounding type provides a factor in the calculation of the interest amount only. It does not actually affect the base principal amount, that is,the calculated interest amount is exclusive of the principal amount.


##### Suspension with Capitalisation

The system allows suspension of an arrangement even if the interest is being capitalised.


##### Tax on Interest

The system has the capability to apply tax on the interest component of a loan product. Tax is optional at the product line level for lending. The user can define and the system can compute tax on Interest Property Class or any of its associated properties. TAX property is currency based, dated and can be multiple but not scheduled. The system displays the TAX property and tax amount in enquiry. This is possible when a scheduled property has tax to be calculated. In TAX.TYPE.CONDITION table, user defines the customer based tax. At the arrangement level, it is possible to remove the values of tax or TAX.TYPE.CONDITION , that the system defaults from the product level, allowing for zero or no tax calculation.

The user has to input the corresponding tax code in the Tax Code field. This field holds the value from TAX table or TAX.TYPE.CONDITION . If any of the properties of a product has to be restricted, then the user has to enter in the Property field and the corresponding values in PROP.TAX.CODE and PROP.TAX.COND .

The user can define tax only for Interest and Charge Property Classes or its associated properties. For the applicable property class or property, user has to input a value. The user has to input the value in TAX or TAX.TYPE.CONDITION .


###### Accounting Entries for Accrued Interest

When the user pays the interest prior to billing (to the customer), that is when the accrued interest is settled, the customer will prefer to see the advance payment entry in the loan statements. To display the advance payments in the loan statements, the accrued interest settlement has to pass through a make due process. To enable this, the Make Due field should be set as Yes in the Payment Rule Type used for settling (paying) the accrued interest.

An external GL system handles the accounting related features and processing for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to accrued interest, the TBC generates an event which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Tax on Accrued Interest

The system can be configured to calculate the tax on accrued interest (both principal interest and penalty interest) at the time of collection of that interest when the Tax Inclusive field is set as Yes in the corresponding Payment Rule Type used at the time of repayment.

> **⚠️ Note:** If Tax Inclusive is set as Yes, then Make Due should also be set as Yes. Else, the system raises an error when the Payment Rule Type is committed.

Only with this setup of Make Due and Tax Inclusive , the loan overview screen displays the accrued interest (both principal and penalty) along with the tax outstanding till date. Also the bills outstanding include the details of the accrued interest (both principal and penalty) and their corresponding tax.


##### Archival of Interest Accruals

The interest accrual values ( Period Start and Period End set of values with their corresponding From Date and To Date set of values) in the AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS application can be archived and stored in the AA.INTEREST.ACCRUAL.HIST table to improve the performance of the system. To achieve this, the user has to set Archive Period and Retain Period fields in AA.PARAMETER table .

Read Archival of Interest Accruals for more information on the archival processing of interest accruals.


##### Negative Rate

If a negative interest rate with a defined margin is applicable, then it is possible to select the same. The system calculates the interest on the balances based on the derived interest rate.

The user has to update the Tier Negative Rate field available in the Interest Property Condition to define the negative rate. This field can display any one of the following values:

- Blank or No - Indicates that the effective interest rate cannot be negative. However, the user can input a negative rate as reference rate. If the effective rate becomes negative as a result of the reference rate or an additional margin, then the derived rate is set as zero.
- Yes - Indicates that negative rates can be input and the reference rate or the additional margin can make the derived rate more negative.
- Block Margin - Indicates that negative rates can be used but the following conditions apply: If the reference rate is positive and the margin makes the rate negative, then the derived rate is set as zero. If the reference rate is negative and the margin makes the rate more negative, then the system calculates the interest on the reference rate (negative in this case) and ignores the margin.

- Floor Margin - Indicates that negative rates can be used but the following conditions apply: If the reference rate is positive and the margin makes the rate negative, then it is set to zero. If the reference rate is negative and the margin makes the rate more negative, then it is set to zero. If the reference rate is negative and the margin is positive, then the system ignores the original negative reference rate and uses the margin. If the reference rate is negative and there is no customer margin, then it is set to zero.

The Accounting Property Class allows the definition of fields that specify the PL head to record the negative rates separately.

The AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS has fields to capture the positive and negative rates separately.

Read Interest Property Class user guide for the more information.


##### Interest Based on Total Commitment

In the product designer, the total commitment balance can be set as Tier Source Balance interest property to ascertain the tier rate for interest calculations.

In the tiered rate structure, the tier amount is referred to total commitment balance. Based on the total commitment balance range, the tier rate is ascertained for interest calculation. When this tier-based setup is configured for a penalty interest (which is sometimes calculated even after the maturity of the loan) with tier source balance as Total Commitment, the Commitment Reversal attribute must be set as On Closure in the Term Amount condition.

- The total commitment balance is set as the tier source balance to ascertain the tier rate for penalty interest.
- The total commitment balance is 500,000, the overdue balance is 2,000 and the overdue interest tier is defined as below in the interest condition, 2% up to 200,00 2.5% up to 500,000 3.5% for more than 500,000
- The Commitment Reversal attribute is set as On Closure in the Term Amount condition. Read Commitment Reversal for more information.
- So, the interest calculation is based on 2,000 of overdue balance with 2.5% interest rate (2.5% tier is ascertained using TOTCOMMITMENT balance).
- When the overdue balance reaches 150,000 and the loan reaches maturity, the interest calculation still happens for 150,000 overdue balances with 2.5% interest rate. This is because the TOTCOMMITMENT holds the balance of 500,000 after maturity as the Commitment Reversal attribute is set as On Closure. TOTCOMMITMENT balance gets reversed only during the pending closure.

##### Floating Rate Set in Advance

The system can be configured to notify a customer X number of days or weeks in advance about the change in base rate for floating-rate linked contracts. Wherever a floating-rate is linked to the contracts, the system:

- Applies the new rate with forward-effective date on the same day the new rate is updated in the system. For example, consider the bank decides to increase the floating-rate index on January 1, 2017 with effective date as March 1, 2017. On January 1, 2017 during COB, the system updates the new rate in all the arrangements following the floating-rate index. It calculates the new payment amount for the forward-effective date.


###### Floating Rate Change Processing

- When the user creates a new record in BASIC.INTEREST (BI) table for a future date, the Change Interest activity triggers the Apply Rate activity for the current day’s date.
- This creates a forward-dated interest condition, which is effective from the forward-effective date of the BI record, that is, the date on which the rate has to take effect.
- This is applicable only if the Property Type of the Interest property is Forward Dated.
- This activity also creates a forward-dated condition for Payment Schedule to calculate and store the new payment amount for the revised rate.
- This is based on the user configuration in Payment Schedule with respect to recalculation of payment amount or term, which again depends on the Property Type of the Payment Schedule property being Forward Dated.

Consider the Principal Interest property in a mortgage contract is following an index rate maintained in

table.

- Current day’s date - January 1, 2017
- Rate change effective date - March 1, 2017

On January 1, 2017, the bank receives an intimation about the change of rate (change from 2% to 3%) due to take effect on March 1, 2017. Now, it enters the new rate in the system, that is, on January 1, 2017, it creates a new record in BASIC.INTEREST table for the index rate with effective date as March 1, 2017.

During COB processing on January 1, 2017, the system triggers the LENDING-APPLY.RATE-PRINCIPALINT activity with effective date as current day and with a forward-dated condition effective from March 1 ,2017. This activity results in two interest conditions being created.

- 2% effective from January 1, 2017
- 3% effective from March 1, 2017

4. Old payment amount
5. New payment amount
6. Effective date of new payment amount

##### Interest Payment in Advance - Discounted Interest

When a loan contract has discounted interest configured , the interest amount is collected in advance before the interest periods. In such cases, it is recommended to not define cooling period for the loan contract.

- If the interest schedule is within the cooling period, then an error is raised stating that: Advance payment schedule cannot fall within the cooling date.
- If the interest schedule is after the cooling period, then the advance interest for the first schedule is not collected during the opening of the loan. Instead, the advance interest is collected once the cooling period is crossed. As an example, consider a loan is created on Apr 1, 2023. The cooling date for the loan is Apr 7, 2023. Advance interest is configured to collect the full interest amount at the time of opening the loan contract. However, since the cooling period is configured for the loan, the advance interest bills and related accounting is generated only on Apr 8, 2023 (which is after the cooling date) instead of Apr 1, 2023 (which is the expected behaviour for discounted interest).

Consider a loan contract is created for a customer on Apr 20, 2023. The interest and payment schedule conditions for the loan are configured to collect the full interest amount for the loan contract in advance (that is, at the time of opening the loan contract).

Once the loan is created, the schedule projection shows that the full interest amount of USD 254.04 for the loan is scheduled to be collected on Apr 20, 2023 itself.

The bill for the advance interest of USD 254.04 is generated and collected from the customer.

The interest that is collected in advance will be recognised to Profit and Loss based on the accrual frequency. Therefore, the DUE interest balance becomes 0 since the customer has paid the advance interest and ACC interest balance has the full interest amount. As part of the accrual process, the following accounting entry is raised to book the advance interest to profit and loss.

Dr ACC

Cr Profit and Loss category

The AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS record for the discounted interest is also updated with the advance interest details.

The LENDING-DISCOUNT.MAKEDUE-SCHEDULE activity triggered on Apr 20, 2023 is used to process the advance interest for the loan contract.

##### Memo Interest

Where the account has been set as a memo account (BALANCE.TREATMENT in ACCOUNT property set to MEMO), any Interest property in the account is treated as a memo interest.

During accruals, accounting is suppressed automatically so as not to post anything on the accrued balance or the PL.

However, the system still maintains the AA interest accruals.

It is still possible to specify capitalisation or make due frequencies for such Interest.

During make due processing, it triggers the settlement of such accrued interest between the settlement account and a counter booking account (Read Settlement Property Class for more details).

The features pertaining to Balance Netting are not applicable for loans in TBC. However, it is possible to define custom rate calculations for loans in TBC.


##### Custom Rate Calculation

Main account currency is USD and the following is the currency wise balance (either as a multi-currency memo account or as participants in an interest comp pool).

- USD Balance: 1000
- EUR Balance: 2000 (FX Rate 1 EUR=1.23USD)
- GBP Balance: 5000 (FX Rate 1 GBP=1.4USD)

The following is the setup in the Custom Type or Name or Value set of fields where Type = Currency, Name = Fixed/Floating and Value – a Rate or an Index.

- USD 0.9 (Margin of 0.5 negotiated for this account)
- EUR 0.75
- GBP 0.3

Interest can be set in such a way that the calculation happens as follows:

Total Balance: USD 19,400 (USD 10,000 + (EUR 2,000 * 1.23) + (GBP 5,000 * 1.4)

Currency Weight (% of the currency balance against the total balance)

- USD Balance: 51.54639175 %
- EUR Balance: 12.37113402 %
- GBP Balance: 36.08247423 %

Currency weighted interest rate

- 0.664948 ((51.54639175 * 0.9) + (12.37113402 * 0.75) + (36.08247423 * 0.3))/100

Effective interest rate

- 1.164948 (0.664948 + 0.5 Margin on USD)

The features pertaining to Balance Netting are not applicable for loans in TBC. However, it is possible to define custom rate calculations for loans in TBC.
