### 1.23  Interest Adjustments


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Retail Lending Product Line is flexible and allows automatic recalculation and correction of related arrangement balances when back-valued activities are processed. The correction processing takes place in real-time and is initiated by the submission of a back-dated Arrangement Activity. For an ...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY`, `BASIC.INTEREST`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Activity Type*, *Arrangement*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Retail Lending Product Line is flexible and allows automatic recalculation and correction of related arrangement balances when back-valued activities are processed. The correction processing takes place in real-time and is initiated by the submission of a back-dated Arrangement Activity. For an arrangement, the system can process the back-dated activities.

The system allows adjustments in previous interest periods etc., and the only restriction is that the Activity cannot be dated earlier than the arrangement start date. When a backdated interest rate changes for either floating or periodic interest rate type, the system triggers the relevant Activity. As the rate change is backdated, the system does a reverse and replay of all the activities associated with the rate change date for all the underlying arrangements.

There are no specific limitations to adjusting interest for loans in TBC due to back dated activities.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

- The system provides the entire list of the Arrangement Conditions at any given period and allows negotiation (create or amend or reverse) of conditions with an effective date that can be set to the current, past or future accounting date. The processing relating to the changes and calculations triggered due to changes are performed based on the effective date of activities, and the system processes the changes when back dated activities are triggered.
- The ability to provide back dated amendment is available and processing ensures that the same final status is achieved as if the activities were processed in the correct chronological sequence.
- During the modification of the Arrangement Conditions, Related balances are modified. Calculations are re-executed.
- The arrangement status reflects the final status of the arrangement based on the Activity triggered. The arrangement state as at the close of business for any effective date is the same irrespective of the actual system date, the activities are performed.
- The correction processing takes place in real time, triggered by the effective date of the Arrangement activity. This is referred as the reverse and replay process.
- For example, the bank introduces a change to the interest rate effective a back date, then the Update Interest Activity triggers the reverse and replay process, which triggers reversal of all the entries up to the back value date and inputs the entries again (replay) after update of Interest Activity.
- It is possible to introduce activities with effective date as future date as well, which is stored as a Future Dated Activity in AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY and updates on the particular date.
- During a reverse and replay, some of the Activity may not be reversed or replayed. This is based on the value set in the Activity Type field specified in the AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS . If the activity type is NORR (No reverse and replay), NOREPLAY or NOREVERSE, then the particular AA activity is not included in reverse and replay or reverse, respectively.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes the interest adjustment topics in detail.


##### Effective Date Processing (Reverse and Replay)

- The financial position and related calculations (for example, interest) for an arrangement are based on the value date. The correct values when back-dated activities are processed are achieved by a back-out and replay of later dated activities, sometimes referred to as reverse and replay processing.
- A basic requirement for the financial products using the Arrangement module is to provide a full history of the Arrangement Conditions at any time and to be able to negotiate the conditions with an effective date that can be set to current, future or past. All calculations and processing must be performed based on the effective date of activities, and the system must be able to process corrections when back-dated activities are performed.
- When the Arrangement Conditions are modified, the related balances, calculations and arrangement statuses reflect the correct state based on the effective dated activities applied. The arrangement state at close of business for any effective date is the same irrespective of the actual system date the activities are performed.
- In most cases, an Activity is set with the same effective date as the current system date; however the ability to provide a back dated amendment is available and the correction processing ensures that the same end state is achieved as if the activities were processed in the correct chronological sequence.
- The effect of back-dated processing is illustrated with an example scenario.
- The initial details of the loan: Creation Date : 1/1/2008 on system date 1/1/2008 Loan Committed Amount: 150,000 USD Initial Disbursement : 100,000 USD effective 1/1/2008 on system date 1/1/2008 Scheduled Repayment: Quarterly Interest Only Initial Interest Rate : 5%

- All Arrangement Property Conditions are held with the effective date they apply. The date of the condition is the inclusive date from which the condition is applied.
- Each Activity performed on an arrangement (through AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY ) has an associated EFFECTIVE.DATE. Any Property Condition modified or action processed, as a result of the Activity, uses this date.
- Several activities may be performed on the same date for an arrangement and as a result the Property Conditions may be amended more than once for the same date. The Arrangement Property Conditions also contain a sequence number that is incremented with each amendment.

| From Date | Principal | Interest Rate | Days | Interest Amount | Activity | Effective Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01/1/2008 | -100,000.00 | 5% | 45 | 616.44 | DISBURSE | 01/01/2008 |
| 15/02/2008 | -100,000.00 | 6% | 14 | 230.14 | RESET RATE | 5/02/2008 |
| 29/02/2008 | -75,000 | 6% |  | 382.19 | REPAY | 29/02/2008 |
| 31/03/2008 |  |  | 31 |  | MAKE.DUE | 31/03/2008 |
| Total |  |  | 90 | 1228.77 |  |  |

- The status of arrangement and associated bills is also maintained by effective date. This allows enquiry of the system to review the state at any given date. The status is also used in processing ageing of overdue bills and can be amended during repayment.
- A back dated Activity results in all statuses on or after the effective date of the Activity to be recalculated as at the effective date. Activities processed after this date also have related statuses recalculated.

All financial balances related to an arrangement are held by effective (or value) date. A back dated Activity results in the adjustment of financial to reflect the correct balance as at the effective date of the Activity. All calculations use the effective dated balances and are therefore recalculated too.


##### Back Dated Activity Processing

A Back-Dated Activity is recorded in the same way as a standard Activity, however additional processing is required to provide automatic correction.

Read the Back Value Dated Processing section of AA user guide for more information..


##### Back Dated Periodic and Basic Interest Rate Changes

In the following example, a back dated rate change has been made to BASIC.INTEREST record 220. The original rate is 6.75%.

- On 21st Dec, the rate is changed to 8% with an effective date of 16th Dec
- The AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS record for the AA09357GH259-LOANINTEREST arrangement has previously calculated the interest for 12 days at 6.75% on 100,000 which equals to 225.
- During close of business, the system re-calculates the interest using the backdated rate change and updates AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS record.
- The calculation is 6 days (10DEC-15DEC) at the original 6.75 % on 100,000, which equals 112.50 6 days (16DEC-21DEC) at new rate 8% on 100,000, which equals 133.33 (back dated calculation) 2 days (22DEC-23DEC) continuing calculation at 8%, which is 40.70


#### 📋 Tasks

The interest adjustment period is the amount of time between interest rate adjustments, after the initial rate period is complete. The time between the day one of the loan and its first adjustment is called the initial rate period. After this period expires, the loan can reset at regular intervals, which are set out in the loan documents.

### 1.24  LendingRule78


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Rule of 78 is a method used by lenders to calculate interest on a loan. It gives greater weight to months in the earlier part of a borrower’s loan cycle when calculating interest, which increases the profit for the lender.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AA.PAYMENT.TYPE`, `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accounting Mode*, *Amount*, *Fixed Int Amount*, *Fixed Rate*, *Fixed rate*, *Flat Rate*, *Maturity Date*, *Profit Method* ... +5 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Rule of 78 is a method used by lenders to calculate interest on a loan. It gives greater weight to months in the earlier part of a borrower’s loan cycle when calculating interest, which increases the profit for the lender.

The Rule of 78 (R78) is a sum-of-the-digits method, summing up of the digits one through 12 - the number of months in a year =78 as a basis for profit accrual distribution . R78 is a method regardless of the finance tenor if it is exactly one year loan with 12 instalments. For applying Rule 78, the total interest collected from the customer is pre-calculated using the Fixed profit rate or fixed interest rate and distributes the interest over the loan life according to the R78 calculation. The interest portion charged for the prior month is much higher than the later one. By using R78, if customer does not terminate the finance before maturity, the interest amount calculated by using flat rate and Rule of 78 finance is equivalent.

Customers can pay the same amount in total. However, if customers pay off the finance early, they end up paying more than the flat rate method.

It is possible to configure and use Rule78 arrangements for both Profit bearing and upfront profit arrangements (Murabaha).

In TBC, there are no specific limitations for defining loan contracts with the Rule of 78 method for interest calculation.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The section helps the user to perform the required configurations for Rule78.


##### Interest Rate

The Interest rate for R78 arrangements is calculated and fixed upfront on the date of creating the Finance arrangement by considering the entire finance term.

> **⚠️ Note:** Rule of 78 can be used to calculate schedules only for arrangements with fixed rate arrangements. Rule of 78 cannot be used for arrangements with Periodic rate and Floating rate of interest.

Following are the values set for each field in Interest Rate:

- Rate type - Flat rate
- Profit Method - Fixed
- Fixed Rate - Profit rate

Since the interest amount is fixed on the date of booking the finance arrangement, it is not possible to increase or decrease the principal or change the profit rate of the arrangement. Hence it is not required to setup recalculation of profit amount during increasing or decreasing of principal amount and when changing the profit rate of the arrangement.


##### Payment Schedule

The payment types in AA.PAYMENT.TYPE is used to configure the R78 Principal and R78 Interest in the Payment schedule. These payment types are used to schedule the repayments for R78 finance arrangements. Also, these two configurations given below are used to identify the lending arrangement as R78 arrangement.

When R78 principal is scheduled in the payment schedule, it is mandatory to schedule the R78 interest for the repayments. Also, it is not possible to do the following:

- Duplicate the R78 principal or R78 interest schedule definition in the payment schedule.
- Capitalise the interest amount for R78 finance arrangements.

> **⚠️ Note:** The R78 interest amount need to be scheduled on the same date of R78 principal amount.

It is required to setup On Activity for with recalculate option as Payment. This is used to recalculate the R78 Principal and Interest payment amount during each scheduled repayment date.

Since the profit amount is fixed on the date of booking the finance arrangement, it is not possible to perform the following amendments:

- Changing the Repayment frequency
- Changing the Repayment date [Start date, End date]
- Payment Holiday setup

Hence it is not required to setup the recalculation as “Payment” or “Term” for these activities. At the same time, it is not mandatory to remove these activities from payment schedule product condition. When these activities are triggered, the system will raise a validation error for R78 arrangements.

- Change Schedule
- Change term
- Change interest rate
- Increase/ decrease the commitment amount
- Advance repayment of Principal and Interest amount
- Payment Holiday

Refer Scheduling Payments for additional details on Loan repayments.


##### Interest Calculation Source

The source balance used for calculating R78 interest is the principal amount of the finance arrangement. It is not possible to add any other virtual balance or balance type for calculation source in AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER .


##### Finance Term

It is required to capture the Term and schedule the Last instalment payment amount on the Maturity date for R78 finance arrangements.


##### Finance Disbursement

As per the R78 calculation, the Interest amount is calculated upfront on the date of creating the Finance arrangement. Hence it is expected to disburse the entire principal amount on the value date.

It is not possible to automatically disburse the commitment amount for loans in TBC.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the R78 Lending Arrangement inputs for Interest Bearing and Upfront Profit models.


##### Interest Bearing Model

The below Illustration is for the R78 Lending arrangement – Interest Bearing Model.


###### Term Amount

The user needs to capture the Amount and Term of the finance arrangement. Also, needs to ensure that the Maturity Date should match with the Last instalment payment.


###### Interest rate

Following are the values set for each field in Interest Rate:

- Rate type - Flat rate
- Profit Method - Fixed
- Fixed Rate - Profit rate


###### Payment Schedule

It is important to define the R78 principal and R78 interest repayment schedules in the Payment schedule definition screen. During validation, it calculates the Interest amount based upon the Term.

Instalment amount is calculated by using,

The system should be set up to Recalculate the Payment for On Activity Lending-calculate-payment schedule. This recalculates the Principal and Profit amount during each payment date.

Principal amount and Interest amount breakup for each repayment date is calculated by using the R78 calculation mechanism.

###### Repayment

The payment scheduled on the due dates are collected from the customer based upon the liquidation mode setup. If sufficient funds are not available in the customer settlement account, then it is moved into the overdue bucket.

It is not possible to process automatic settlement of bills for loans in TBC. However, the customer/user can manually settle the bill by initiating the repayment transaction in the external payment system (outside the TBC). When a payment is received, an API is triggered to credit the funds using the required repayment activity. The funds are apportioned to the balances based on the repayment rules of this Activity triggered.


###### Amendments

The profit amount for R78 arrangements is calculated upfront by using the Flat Rate input by the user. The user can collect the repayment amount from the customer on or after the scheduled due date.

But it is not possible to execute the amendment scenarios requires the profit amount recalculation. Validation error message is shown to the user.

- Change of Interest rate
- Change the repayment date
- Change the repayment frequency
- Change the Term/ Maturity date
- Advance repayment towards the Principal and Interest
- Marking Payment holiday for the scheduled payments


###### Pay-off

R78 arrangements can be pre-closed before the maturity date. While running simulation for Pay-off it generates the Pay-off bill for the outstanding amount (Outstanding Principal + Interest amount scheduled for current repayment date). It can be settled from the settlement account of the Customer.

If bonus needs to be paid from the settled portion it can be configured by using the charge product condition.

To settle the pay-off bill, the customer/user must initiate the pre-closure transaction in the external payment system (outside the TBC). When a payment for pre-closure of the loan is received, an API is triggered to credit the funds using the required repayment activity. The funds are apportioned to the balances based on the repayment rules of this Activity triggered.


##### Upfront Profit Model

Upfront profit model is used for Murabaha type of Arrangements wherein the profit amount is agreed upfront with the customer. During amendments, the profit amount is not recalculated. If the lending arrangement is pre-closed, then upfront profit amount agreed with the customer is collected from the customer. Based upon the bank’s business requirement, a portion of the unamortized profit amount can be paid as bonus to the customer.

The example given below shows the transaction input details for capturing the R78 Upfront profit arrangements.


###### Term Amount

The user needs to capture the amount and term for upfront profit arrangements in the Term amount arrangement condition.


###### Profit rate

The Flat profit rate for the arrangement is captured in the Fixed rate field. Also, the Profit method should be set as Fixed, Rate type should be captured as Flat rate and Accounting Mode as Upfront front profit.


###### Payment Schedule

The R78 Principal and Profit amount can be scheduled in the Payment schedule.


###### Upfront Profit Accounting Entries and Payment schedule

During authorisation, upfront profit accounting entries are generated for the calculated profit amount and payment schedule is generated.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. The TBC generates an event which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting related to upfront profits in loan contracts.


###### Repayment

The payments scheduled on the due dates are collected from the customer. If sufficient funds are not available, then it is moved into the overdue bucket.


###### Amendments

The profit amount for R78 arrangements is calculated upfront by using the Flat Rate inputted by the user. User can collect the repayment amount from the customer on or after the scheduled due date.

But it is not possible to execute the amendment scenarios requires the profit recalculation.

- Change of Profit rate
- Change the repayment date
- Change the repayment frequency
- Change the Term/ Maturity date
- Advance repayment towards the Principal and Profit
- Marking Payment holiday for the scheduled payments


###### Pay-off

During Pay-off (Pre closure) of the R78 lending arrangement, it is possible to configure and pay a percentage of unamortized profit amount as bonus to the customer.

Below pay-off statement shows the principal and profit amount collected from the customer along with the Bonus amount required to be paid to the customer bonus amount is configured and collected as a Charge.

There are no Tasks available for Rule of 78 feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

here are no Outputs available for Rule of 78 feature.

### 1.25  Limit Facility for Loan


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The sanctioned limit is the total exposure that the bank can take on a particular client for facilities offered by the bank. Such limits are recorded using the Limit Property Class in arrangements.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARR.LIMIT`, `CUST.GROUP.PURPOSE`, `LIMIT`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Application Ref*, *Approv Date*, *Available Marker*, *Collateral Code*, *Collateral Details*, *Collateral Link*, *Collateral Type*, *Company* ... +31 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The sanctioned limit is the total exposure that the bank can take on a particular client for facilities offered by the bank. Such limits are recorded using the Limit Property Class in arrangements.

In Lending TBC, the limit sanctioned for a loan can be updated by providing the limit key (from the external limit solution) in the Limit Id attribute of the Limit Condition. Other features pertaining to Limits are not applicable for Lending TBC. Read Introduction to Loan Limit for more information on loan limits in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Limit conditions are usually defined at product level and can be changed or negotiated at the arrangement level.

The Term Amount Property Class enables recording the nature of the limit and when limit utilisation has to be recorded. The sanctioned limit can be a revolving or a non-revolving limit. The Revolving field is used to decide if the limit has to be reinstated on regular payments or only on prepayments. When set to No, the loan is set to have a non-revolving limit. The Update Commt Limit attribute is used to decide the utilisation of the limit that can be recorded at the time of creating the arrangement or on disbursal of the loan.


#### 🔧 Working With

Loans can be provided after setting up limits. If the owner of the arrangement has a credit limit covering the account, the reference to that limit is specified in the Limit Reference field, which is mandatory for the Lending product line. The limit serial number is also recorded to indicate the limit information of the loan. It is also possible to disburse a loan without creating limits. The system generates an override message notifying the absence of limit.

If the customer is a beneficial owner, then the customer has to be a GL and Limit customer.


##### Multi party Limits with Joint Liability

The JS Liable field in the Customer Property Class indicates if the customers are jointly and severally liable when there is more than one customer associated with the sanctioned limit. If this field is enabled, it denotes that the customers are jointly liable.

The enquiry on CUSTOMER.SCV.CHECK displays the exposure at customer group level as well as individual customers who are part of the group.

> **⚠️ Note:** The enquiry works only when the System Use field is set as Risk in the CUST.GROUP.PURPOSE application.

Consider a personal loan arrangement that is created with the customers of the previously defined group. The limits are set with joint liability and since the Key Type is set to Txn Ref, the system allows to map alphanumeric Limit Reference id.

Since the customers are jointly liable, the utilisation limits are updated accordingly. The below screenshot represents the utilisation for the beneficial owner.

Once this loan is created, the available limit for the time band 366 days and above, the available limit post utilization is only 5000. When the user creates a loan for a different product that is allowed for this customer group, the system generates an override message regarding the over utilisation.

In this case, the user creates a contract for a two wheeler loan for USD 15,000.00 and 2Y Term. When the record is committed, the system generates an override message for the over utilisation to the tune of USD 10,000.00.

When the override is accepted for committing the record, the utilisation is updated accordingly. The same can be seen in the customer risk exposure for the beneficial owner.

Read Multi Party Limit – Jointly Severally Liability for more information.


##### Limit and Collateral

In the Arrangement Overview screen,

- The user can view the limit and collateral information of the arrangement at the Arrangement Overview screen level and retrieve the arrangement records based on the limit IDs. This feature enables better usability for clients. The limit information is stored in AA.ARR.LIMIT , but it does not store the limit amount, expiry date, etc. and collateral information of the borrower. Through this enquiry, the user can view the limit and collateral information of the arrangement .
- Under the Basic tab, the limit and collateral details are displayed for the arrangement, if available.
- The user can also view the Limit record created in LIMIT application by selecting the drill-down.
- The LIMIT record is attached for the arrangement.
- The limit information displays details, such as limit currency, limit amount, secured or unsecured like fixed or variable, secured amount, outstanding amount, available or excess amount, pledge customer, pledge amount.
- The collateral information displays details like customer, collateral type, currency, nominal value, execution value, third party value, net value and expiry date.
- The user can also view the arrangement based on the limit ID through ACCT.BAL.TODAY enquiry.
- On selecting the Find option, the user can view the limit details with drill-down options. In this, the user can select Account Details, which displays the Arrangement overview screen with limit and collateral details.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Set up Limit (Retail)
- Maintain/Reverse Limit
- Lending Processes (Retail)

Limit is a risk perception and bank can classify its risk product as per requirements. Limits can be sanctioned at individual customer level or at the group level.

Collateral items are offered by customers for their liabilities with the bank. Collateral may be land, buildings, stock of goods, fixed deposits, letters of credit, and so on. Assets which are maintained in the system like account balances, will be automatically valued by the system, whereas other systems have to be valued by the bank periodically. Collateral plays an indispensable part in secured limits.

### 1.26  Link Loans to Customer Portfolio


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Loans can be linked to a customers’ portfolio and the changes made in the disbursed loan reflects in the portfolio indicating movement of funds. Changes could be such as change of interest, payoff or closure, increase of term amount, term etc.*
> 
> **Applications:** `ASSET.TYPE`, `SC.POS.ASSET`, `SEC.ACC.MASTER`, `SUB.ASSET.TYPE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Margin Rate*, *Portfolio ID*, *Portfolio Id*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Loans can be linked to a customers’ portfolio and the changes made in the disbursed loan reflects in the portfolio indicating movement of funds. Changes could be such as change of interest, payoff or closure, increase of term amount, term etc.

The features related to linking of loans to the customer portfolio for the purpose of combined portfolio valuation and management are not applicable in TBC. These features can be enabled through external solutions. Read Introduction to TBC for Lending for more information about TBC for loans.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The SEC.ACC.MASTER created for a customer can be attached as the portfolio of the customer in the loan. The user can provide the portfolio of the customer in the Portfolio ID field of the Account Property Class. To allow the user to input or modify this field value at the arrangement level, the field should be set to negotiable while defining the Product Condition.

The AA valuation can be configured into the SC Module depending the parameter setting required. A simple configuration is shown below with the creation of the ASSET.TYPE and SUB.ASSET.TYPE , read the Portfolio Management user guide for more detailed information.

The ASSET.TYPE provides the link of loans to the portfolio valuation ID.

The SUB.ASSET.TYPE , links the ASSET.TYPE to the new SUB.ASSET.TYPE .

> **⚠️ Note:** Only one sub asset type at a time can be linked to an asset type.

Different margin rates for the different asset types can be specified. Note that the margin rates specified in the Margin Rate field becomes effective only for the deposit type arrangements, that is, the margin value amount in SC.POS.ASSET file gets updated only for a deposit account. The same is not applicable for loans.


#### 🔧 Working With

An arrangement becomes active in a portfolio only after a disbursal of the same has been done (in case of loans) or a settlement has been done (in terms of deposits).

Cross currency valuation, that is, arrangement being in any foreign currency and the portfolio being in local currency (USD) is possible, with the system picking rates from the currency table automatically. Any kind of changes made in the disbursed loan or settled deposit reflects in the portfolio indicating movement of funds. Changes can be such as, change interest, redemption of funds, payoff or closure, partial funding within cancel period, partial withdrawal from deposit, increase of term amount, term etc.

The portfolio ID is displayed in the Product Conditions for Lending to enable AA to be included in the portfolio valuations.

The user can view the valuation by running the SC.VAL.COST enquiry.

Only after running the enquiry, the SC.POS.ASSET file gets updated.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Create and Disburse Retail Loan (Manual)

The Portfolio ID field in the Account Property Condition allows the user to input the ID, which links the customer’s arrangements, such as, loans, deposits, or even savings under the same ID.

### 1.27  Loan Closure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *If there is no debit balance in a loan account on the maturity date, then the loan is treated as closed. If debit balance in the loan account continues even after the maturity date, then there are chances of the penalty on the outstanding debit balance. Upon closure of a loan, the arrangement record...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARR.CONDITION`, `AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT`, `AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT.HIST`, `AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY`, `ACCOUNT.CLOSURE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arr Status*, *Arrangement*, *Base Date Type*, *Closure Method*, *Closure Period*, *Closure Reason*, *Closure Type*, *Credit Amount* ... +5 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

If there is no debit balance in a loan account on the maturity date, then the loan is treated as closed. If debit balance in the loan account continues even after the maturity date, then there are chances of the penalty on the outstanding debit balance. Upon closure of a loan, the arrangement records are moved from the AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT to the AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT.HIST table. During a history restore, records are moved from the AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT.HIST to the AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT.

For accounts where the balances are settled, the closure process can be deferred until the specified defer period.

There are no specific limitations related to closure of loan contracts in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The account associated with an arrangement is automatically closed either when all balances associated with the arrangement becomes zero or when the arrangement matures (provided all the balances are settled). This is defined in the Closure Type attribute.

The attribute can hold values, Balance, Maturity and None.

- If Balance is selected, the account is closed on the same day when the account balance becomes zero.
- If Maturity is selected, once all balances are settled, the Arr Status attribute is updated to Pending Closure and account closure activity is scheduled on the date of maturity of the arrangement.
- None is applicable only if Closure Method is chosen as Manual.

The bank can specify a period from the date in which the arrangement is identified for closure after which the closure activity needs to be triggered. The system schedules the closure activity based on the period mentioned. This period can be specified in the Closure Period attribute

The bank needs to select the mode of closing the arrangement account. This can be done in the Closure Method attribute. The options available are:

- Automatic closure method: The system triggers the closure activity on maturity or on the day the balances are settled depending on the Closure Type . Hence, either Maturity or Balance needs to be selected as a mandatory value in Closure Type .
- Manual closure method: The user triggers the closure activity manually.

The bank has to restrict all transactions into the account as the account is identified for closure. This needs to be mentioned in the Posting Restrict attribute. A posting restrict in the range of 90 -99 is allowed which pertains to account closure posting restrict.

After creation of a new loan arrangement, if the loan amount is not disbursed in full within the defined Cancel Period, the system triggers the LENDING-CANCEL-ARRANGEMENT activity. It raises entries opposite to the entries raised for the new arrangement. After the arrangement is cancelled, the loan arrangement needs to be closed. For this, the system triggers LENDING-CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT, as a secondary activity during cancellation. At the cancellation stage, the status of the arrangement is updated to PENDING.CLOSURE. The system schedules the closure activity based on the Closure Period in Closure Property Condition. An account closure record (when the close activity is processed) is created for the arrangement in the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE application with a posting restrict of 90.

When the loan is cancelled as the loan amount is not disbursed in full within the defined Cancel Period, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting related to the closure of the loan.


##### Automated Closure

Automated closure option has been provided at the product designer level. The closure gets triggered automatically on maturity or once the balance in the account becomes zero as in case of a non-revolving arrangement. In case of automatic closure, this specifies the period when the Closure Activity is processed. This period begins after the system has identified whether the arrangement is ready to be closed as defined in Closure Type field.


##### Deferring Closure of Loans

Maturity Processing for loan products can be deferred until the agreed and specified defer period. At the end of the deferred period, system either moves the arrangement to a Pending Closure status or retains the Expired status if the loan is still unpaid. Once the outstanding is repaid, the Expired loans move to Pending Closure status.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Defer Closure Period is a no-change field in the Closure product condition, after initial authorization of the arrangement. Click here to know more about the configuration.


##### Arrangement Status

The arrangement status changes to Pending Closure from its previous status once the arrangement is identified for closure.

- For non-revolving arrangements the status of arrangement moves to Pending Closure once the arrangement has been fully repaid.
- For revolving arrangements, the status moves to Pending Closure once the arrangement matures and is fully repaid. The arrangement moves to Close once the closure activity is triggered and account closure record is created.

The AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT.HIST table holds records of closed arrangements. It has the similar fields as in the AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT table.


#### 🔧 Working With

The below set of screen shots show the closure of a lending arrangement. Once the principal and interest component are paid off, then the arrangement status moves from Current to Pending Closure to Closed.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Lending Close Arrangement Activity must not be used to close an active loan. The lending arrangement must be closed only by triggering a payoff of the loan.

On repaying the loan fully, the loan is moved to Pending Closure status (as the loan is set to closure when balance is zero).

As there is no closure period set, the next day (after the COB) the arrangement is moved to Closed status.

- It is not possible to automatically disburse the commitment amount for loans in TBC.

### 1.28  Loan Commitment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
>

> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accounting Mode*, *Advice*, *Amount*, *App Period*, *Base Date Type*, *Cancel Period*, *Change Amount*, *Commitment Drawdown* ... +24 more

> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Loan Commitment describes the loan amount and tenure for which the loan is sanctioned by the bank. Based on the documentary proof, the bank decides the terms and conditions of the loan.

There are no specific limitations for defining the commitment details for loans in the TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Term Amount Property Class is used to define the commitment given to a contract.

- The Amount attribute in the Term Amount Property Class is used to define the commitment (maximum) amount of the Arrangement.
- The Term attribute in the Term Amount Property Class is used to define the commitment term of the Arrangement. The Amount attribute is currency specific, that is, the user must have one instance of each Product Condition for each currency of the product (or products) that use the Product Condition.
- The Commitment Drawdown attribute in the Term Amount Property class is used to define the disbursement method for the arrangement with options as Manual, Auto or Schedule. While the Schedule option disburses funds based on the schedule definitions in Payment Schedule property conditions, the Auto option disburses the funds through Term Amount property conditions with no dependency on Payment Schedule.

- The Change Amount attribute in the Term Amount Property Class is used to increase or decrease the commitment amount of the arrangement during the life cycle using the INCREASE or DECREASE action.
- The Change Amount attribute represents the amount to be increased or decreased on the original amount.
- To increase, the input in this attribute has to be greater than zero.
- To decrease, the input in this attribute has to be lesser than zero.

- The Change Term Activity allows the user to modify (that is, increase or decrease) the term of an arrangement, subject to the negotiation rules.

The Commitment Reversal attribute in the Term Amount condition enables the user to configure the reversal of the total commitment balance either at maturity or during the pending closure process. This attribute has the following options :

- None or On Maturity - The system reverses the total commitment balance at term maturity.
- On Closure - It reverses the total commitment balance only during pending closure process.

> **⚠️ Note:** Both the commitment amount and the term can be modified during the life cycle of the arrangement, subject to negotiation rules, periodic rules and the current outstanding amount.

When a loan is pre closed (early matured) within the Cooling Period defined for the product, its interest and charges can be waived. This cooling period can be defined as the number of calendar days in the Closure and Term Amount Property Classes. These features are mutually exclusive.

The Cooling Period attribute in the Term Amount Property Class determines the time period during which the amount can be redeemed without making due any accrued interest in the case of pre-closure of an arrangement. In the case of interest already made due, redeem Arrangement Activity during the cooling period only stops paying the accrued interest and due interest paid is not reversed back.

With respect to the pre-closure charges, the charges have to be configured as Rule Break Charges with Rule Start attribute set to Cooling-off.

In AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE , the value for the Rule Start attribute set as Cooling-off calculates the start date from which restriction has to be applied. If Cooling-off is opted, then the periodic restriction starts from the cooling date as specified in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS .

The below screen shot displays the Periodic Attribute setup for charge trigger after the cooling period.

The following AC.EVENT records are used in AC.ALLOCATION.RULES .

The below screen shot displays INTEREST-ADJUST.REDEEM-PAY.

The below screen shot displays the INTEREST-ADJUST.REDEEM-PAY-CM record.

The below screen shot displays the INTEREST-ADJUST.REDEEM-PAY-PM record.

The below screen shot displays INTEREST-ADJUST.REDEEM-PAY-PY event type in the AC.ALLOCATION.RULE .

The AC.ALLOCATION.RULE set up should be as done as indicated in the above screenshots for the AC.EVENT records.

The Closure Property Class is used to define the cooling period for loan pre-closure without interest and charges. The Cooling Period field of a loan is defined as number of days (calendar) and in case it is a holiday, the Cooling Date Adj field can be used to adjust the cooling period to the next working day.

Property Class wise or Property wise choice is available for waiving or retaining the charge or interest applied during the cooling period using the Waive Class, Waive Prop and Waive Bill Type attributes. The Waive Bill Type attribute can be set to waive accrued amount, billed amount or both.

> **⚠️ Note:** For interest, only the current interest (accrued) can be waived. For charges, the waiver has to be applied on both billed and current (accrued) charges. The Cooling Period attribute in the Term Amount Property Class is mutually exclusive of the Cooling Period attribute in the Closure Property Class. If found in both the places, the system raises an error at the proofing stage.

Whenever a pre-closure within the cooling period is processed for a loan, the system generates an event, which can be captured by an external accounting system for accounting and bookkeeping purposes.

The Loan Cancellation functionality allows a loan to be automatically cancelled if the commitment amount is not fully availed by the customer in the stipulated time period. The stipulated time is defined as the number of days under Term Amount Property Class.

The system schedules the LENDING-CANCEL-ARRANGEMENT Activity, which triggers the cancellation if the loan is not fully disbursed by that cancel period.

The banks can configure a pre-advice to be sent to the customer to indicate the cancellation that would come up due to the pending disbursement. The pre-advice configuration is achieved through the Activity Messaging Property which has associated multi-value attributes, such as Pre Notice Activity and Pre Notice Days . The Pre Notice Activity attribute has to be LENDING-CANCEL-ARRANGEMENT and Pre Notice Days attribute controls the time in advance when the notification has to be sent.

In the TBC, instead of sending the notification or advice, the system generates an event which should be consumed by an external system for further processing.

Certain type of loan products require the loan to be made available in tranches over multiple time frames, this enables the borrowers to withdraw the loan amount in a phased manner to meet the periodic requirement of cash flows.

The Full Commitment Activity attribute in the Term Amount Property Class when set to Yes triggers the LENDING-FULL.DISBURSE-ARRANGEMENT Activity when the loan is fully disbursed.


##### Overdrawn Commitment

The update to commitment balances is controlled by two attributes in the Term Amount Property Class.

- Update Utilised Commitment - indicates whether to raise utilized commitment balance or not.
- Update Commit on Capitalisation - indicates how capitalisation impacts various the commitment balances.

For Retail Loans, the setup of the two attributes below can be configured in two ways

| Scenario | Update Utilised Commitment | Update Commit On Capitalisation | System Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | No | Current | Follows existing behavior and capitalised charges are maintained in CUR balance of TERM.AMOUNT. |
| B | Yes | Overdraw | Utilisation and Capitalised amounts are maintained in new balances, UTL and OVD respectively.OVD represents the capitalised amounts while UTL represents the utilised commitment amount, excluding the capitalised amount. |

##### Scenario B

In certain Lending businesses, especially in Consumer Lending scenarios, when the loan disbursement happens in multiple stages, requirement is that commitment is not to be affected when the fees are capitalised during disbursement and is handled separately without affecting the available commitment for future disbursement . This allows the bank to fully disburse the sanctioned loan amount to the customer.

A loan of USD 100 is sanctioned with two disbursements (USD 70 and USD 30). A disbursement fee of USD 5 is capitalised each time a disbursement happens. Assume there are no other interest, fees or charges.

When 70 USD is disbursed, a fee of USD 5 is capitalised on the loan and the commitment reduces from 100 USD to USD 25 . This means, only 25 USD is available for subsequent disbursement against a required amount of 30 USD.

Similar to the above scenario, when a loan is Revolving, say a loan of 100 USD is fully disbursed and subsequently an activity charge is capitalised for 5 USD. At this point the principal outstanding is 105 USD and when a repayment is triggered for say 5 USD towards the fee portion, the available commitment gets reinstated by 5 USD. This means that against a 100 USD loan, 105 could be drawn since commitment was reinstated for the repaid amount towards the capitalised fees.

For loans in which the bank wants to overcome the above behaviour, the Term Amount product condition is configured with Update Utilised Commitment field set as Yes and Update Commit on Capitalisation set as Overdraw.

> **⚠️ Note:** When the Update Utilised Commitment field is set as Yes, the Update Commit on Capitalisation field must be set to either Overdraw or Current And Overdraw. These are the only combinations allowed at this point of time for the Lending product line when the Update Utilised Commitment field is set as Yes. For other combinations the system raises a validation or proofing error.

The UTL and OVD commitment balance types are used for the above configuration.

Impact of Loan Commitment Balances during Multiple Disbursements and Fee Capitalization

A loan is disbursed in multiple tranches with a linked disbursement fee that is capitalised. Impact on commitment balance is described below.

The configuration in Term Amount product condition for Scenario B is presented below.

- Update Utilised Commitment - Yes
- Update Commit on Capitalisation - Overdraw

#### 🔧 Working With

A new loan arrangement can be created as a commitment to the customer for the loan. The loan commitment is a contingent arrangement and becomes non-contingent upon disbursal. The term and amount of loan sanction can be updated in the Term Amount Property Class to indicate the loan commitment and the term of the contract.

A loan amount can be repaid at any point during the term of the arrangement. It is quite common to charge the customers for early closure of the loan contract. The banks can indicate a period for which the customer is allowed to do a pre-closure of the disbursed amount. In this case, the customer does not owe any interest and any charges collected during the cooling period are reversed. This is facilitated through the Cooling Period field in the Term Amount Property Class.

There may be cases where the schedules can be configured and processed before the cooling period has expired. Any interest, charges or principal amount that has already been made due to the customer within this cooling period have to be paid by the customer during the pre-closure calculation and the due balances are not reversed. In the scenarios where a schedule is configured to do an activity before the cooling-off period, a suitable override is produced at the arrangement level and also at the funds transfer stage to notify the user. The same principal for cooling off is applicable for rollovers as well, only when the Base Date Type attribute is set to Agreement in the Account Property Class. Any accrual from the last make due till pre-closure is reversed.

The cooling period is indicated in the Term Amount Condition of the arrangement. After disbursement, the Cooling Date field in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS is updated to indicate the end date of the cooling period.

The processing of cooling period is similar for Loans and Deposits.

In lending, to activate the cooling period functionality, a LENDING-CALCULATE-PAYOFF Activity is triggered and the arrangement is repaid through the LENDING-SETTLE-PAYOFF Activity during the cooling period. Upon triggering these activities, the accrued interest amount for the arrangement till the repayment date is reversed. Any interest amount that is already due or capitalised is not reversed and is included as part of the payoff bill.

During the cooling period, the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PAYMENT. RULES Activity has to be used for partial repayments instead of the LENDING-SETTLE-PAYOFF Activity, as triggering the latter results in the reversal of the accrued interest amount.

The Payoff Property Class determines the amount to be repaid if the arrangement has to be pre-closed. To generate a payoff amount, a payoff request is generated, which issues an info bill. The info bill stores the amount that has to be repaid to close the lending arrangement. It also stores the due amounts, ageing amounts, current amounts and UNC amounts, if any.

The arrangement can be repaid through different channels. To trigger the SETTLE payoff activity, the transaction code of an external transaction has to be mapped to the activity. It is always assumed that the SETTLE payoff is used only for full repayments and not for partial repayments. The cooling off period is considered only when the arrangement is pre closed using the SETTLE Payoff Activity.

When a SETTLE payoff activity is triggered within the cooling period, all the accrued interest amount is reversed out. Any interest already due is expected to be repaid by the customer.

The following section describes the charges

If any charges that are due already is expected to be repaid by the customer. If it is required not to collect the charge within cooling period, then the App Period attribute in Activity Charges should be set so that the charge is made due after the cooling period. Within the cooling period, SETTLE payoff cancels all the issued bills and therefore the charges are not collected.

Charges can be applied on an arrangement when a rule is broken. The cooling-off option in the Rule Start attribute of AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE application allows applying the rule only from the cooling-off date and is checked only when the Activity is run outside the cooling period.

It is assumed that Closure Property can be associated with the product. If the Closure Property does not exist, the arrangement does not get closed. The cooling-off period is considered only when the arrangement is pre-closed using Payoff Property Class. Apply payment does not consider cooling period at all.

Payoff bill generated does not contain the accrued interest amount.

The SETTLE Payoff Activity triggered after the cooling period does not adjust any interest accruals. Interest needs to be accrued if the Activity is triggered after the cooling period.

Example

An arrangement with cooling period was created with the make due date not before the cooling end date. Trigger Payoff Activity and Apply Payment to settle the entire principal amount using the Settle Payoff option (ACSP transaction type) before the end of the cooling period. ACCINTEREST is cleared off.

For the below arrangement, the Payoff Activity has been triggered and the dues have been settled through SETTLE-PAYOFF Activity.

The below screenshot displays the cooling period as 10 days from the arrangement start date, which ends on 2nd Jan 2010.

The below screenshot displays the updated period end date with period start date in the AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS making the accrual amount zero.

Reversal of accrued interest amount is achieved by updating the Period End field in the AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS record with the same date as updated in the Period Start field resulting in zero interest accruals as shown below.

| Functionality | System Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Interest Accrued AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS | When the cooling period is given in Closure Property Class, choice to waive or apply at Property Class level or Property level, is available. |
| Interest billed AA.BILL.DETAILS | When the cooling period is given in Closure Property Class, interest billed cannot be waived. |
| Charge Accrued EB.ACCRUAL | When the cooling period is given in Closure Property Class, the accruals of charges are always waived. |
| Charge billed AA.BILL.DETAILS | When the cooling period is given in Closure Property Class, the choice to waive or apply at Property Class level or Property level, is available. When the charge is not settled, a bill is raised to refund or collect (for a due bill and pay bill, respectively) automatically. When the charge is settled, the payoff bill includes the bill raised to refund or collect (for a due bill and pay bill, respectively) automatically. |
| Charge pending to be amortised | When the cooling period is given in Closure Property Class, the choice to waive or apply at Property Class level or Property level, is available; but there is no choice of amortised or unamortised. If configured in Closure, to be waived, the bill amount is waived. The amortised portion to PL is reversed unlike Rebate unamortised. If chosen to waive, the payoff bill includes the bill that is raised to refund or collect (for a due bill and pay bill, respectively) automatically. |
| Interest pending to be amortised | When the cooling period is given in Closure Property Class, the interest is already applied and cannot be waived. |
| Activity charge in cooling period | The functionality of Cooling off feature in the Periodic Attribute continues. |

| Functionality | Term Amount | Closure |
|---|---|---|
| Interest Accrued AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS | The interest accrued is automatically waived, no choice available. | Choice is available to waive or apply at Property Class level or Property level. |
| Interest billed AA.BILL.DETAILS | The interest billed cannot be waived | The interest billed cannot be waived |
| Charge Accrued EB.ACCRUAL | Charge accrued is automatically waived, no choice to apply the charge | Accruals of Charges are always waived. |
| Charge billed AA.BILL.DETAILS | Charge billed cannot be waived. | Choice available to waive or apply at Property Class level or Property level. When the charge is not settled, the bill is raised to refund or collect (for a due bill and pay bill, respectively) automatically. When charge is settled, the payoff bill includes bill raised to refund or collect (for a due bill and pay bill, respectively) automatically. |
| Charge pending to be amortised | The charge is already applied, so cannot be waived or benefit can be given based on Rebate Unamortised. | Choice is available to waive or apply at Property Class level or Property level, there is no choice of amortised or unamortised. If configured in Closure to be waived, the bill amount is waived. The amortised portion to PL is reversed unlike Rebate unamortised. If chosen to waive, Payoff bill includes Bill that is raised to refund or collect (for a due bill and pay bill, respectively) automatically. |
| Interest Pending to be amortised | Interest is already applied, so cannot be waived. | Interest is already applied, so cannot be waived. |
| Activity Charge in cooling period | Activity restriction can be used to waive the charge that is to be applied using Cooling off attribute. | The functionality of Cooling Off feature in the Periodic Attribute continues. |

The Cancel Period attribute in the Term Amount Property determines the cancellation period of an arrangement. When the loan is not fully disbursed within the Cancel Period, the system triggers LENDING-CANCEL-ARRANGEMENT Activity. On this activity, the arrangement is updated to PENDING.CLOSURE. The system schedules the Closure Activity based on the closure period in the Closure Property Condition.

On cancellation of the arrangement, the accrued interest is reversed out, but the interest amount that is already due as part of schedule being processed, has to be repaid by the customer.

The system reversal of the accrued interest amount is achieved by updating the Period End attribute in AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS record of the arrangement with same date as updated in the Period Start attribute, resulting in zero interest accruals as shown in the below screenshot.

Cancel Period can be amended or removed after the initial creation of an arrangement through Change Term and Renegotiate Arrangement Activities, when the Cancel Period attribute is set as Negotiable and Accounting Mode in Interest Property Class is not set as Advance or Upfront Profit.

When committing the Activity, the system calculates the Cancel Period End Date and stores the value in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS table. If the Cancel Period value is removed, then no Cancel Period End Date is stored in the table or displayed in the arrangement. Also, it removes/updates any scheduled activity for cancelling the arrangement.

The option of scheduling cancellation of a lending account by specifying the number of days before which the account is cancelled can be specified in the respective Term Amount Property of the product.

The user can set the number of days before hand, as to when the pre-notification advice is to be generated, and sent to the customer, before the account is cancelled.

A work flow example for loans is shown below, while the same process can be used for the other product lines as well.

The below screenshot displays the Pre-notification Activity specified as LENDING-CANCEL-ARRANGEMENT and Pre-notification Days set as 2D.

This set up triggers the LENDING-CANCEL-ARRANGEMENT-PRE.NOTICE Activity, two days prior to the scheduled LENDING-CANCEL-ARRRANGEMENT Activity, so that the advice AA-6001 is sent.

Instead of producing the notification advice, the TBC generates an event, which can be consumed by an appropriate system to notify the customer in advance about the loan cancellation, due to the pending disbursement.

The configuration for a pre-notification or cancellation of a loan is illustrated here.

The below screenshot displays the Pre-Notification Activity and the specific number of days before the cancellation period, by when the pre-notification advice is sent in the AA.PRD.DES.ACTIVITY.MESSAGING .

The below screenshot displays the Scheduled Activity of Pre-notification and Cancellation of an arrangement.

The two-day notice set up in Activity Messaging is reflected in the AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY between the Pre-Notice Activity and Cancel Arrangement Activity.

Term loans have the Term or Maturity Date attributes as mandatory. For a term loan, when the bank prefers the system to calculate the term based on the instalment start date and the number of installments, the Maturity Date Type field should be set as Payment End Date. Here, the maturity date is calculated by the system based on the Installment Start Date and number of Payments. For this setup, the Freq and Num or Freq and End attributes are mandatory. The last schedule date of Account Property is set as maturity date of the loan.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Maturity Date Type is no-change field after authorisation. Term, Maturity Date, Maturity Date Convention and Tolerance Days fields are no-input fields when the Maturity Date Type flag is set. This feature is applicable only for Linear, Constant and Percentage Payment Types.

Here, the Maturity Date Type field is set as Payment End Date.

The arrangement overview displays the maturity date which is calculated based on the start date, frequency of repayment and number of installments.

Certain types of loan products require the loan to be made available in tranches over multiple time frames to enable borrowers to disburse the commitment amount in a phased manner to meet the periodic requirement of cash flows with the following additional features built into the product, as listed below:

- Commitment is made available in tranches over specified periods.
- Disbursements can be for the committed tranche amount and within the tranche period only.
- Disbursements can be automatic on scheduled dates or according to manual requests.
- During arrangement creation, to enable auto disbursement process, the user should provide the details, such as customer details, term amount, payment schedule details and settlement instructions.

The below screenshot displays the Arrangement Overview screen, post capturing of the details and authorisation.

The features related to automatic disbursements are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Overdrawn Commitment

The banks can setup loans with multiple disbursements, and the capitalised charges (activity charge or periodic charge) and interest are maintained outside the total commitment amount. This allows the customers to avail disbursements for the total loan amount.

For revolving loans, the banks have an option to setup the loan product in a way that a repayment or settlement toward a capitalised charge or interest, does not reinstate the commitment amount.

> **⚠️ Note:** This is applicable only for Lending Product Line.

The commitment balance processing is presented below for the scenario in which Update Utilised Commitment is set to Yes and Update Commit on Capitalisation is set to Overdraw.

A non-revolving loan is sanctioned for USD 100 and the first disbursement is triggered for USD 50 . There is disbursement activity fee linked to the product.

ECB record before disbursement

Overview after first disbursement. The Available Commitment is reduced from USD 100 to USD 50 .

ECB record after first disbursement of USD 50. The Disbursement Fee which got capitalized does not reduce the Available Commitment and is maintained in the Overdrawn Commitment balance

Then, the second disbursement is triggered for USD 50 which is for the entire remaining loan amount sanctioned to the customer by the bank.

Overview after second disbursement of USD 50. Now the loan is fully disbursed.

ECB record is updated. The fee for the second disbursement is updated in Overdrawn commitment.

A repayment of USD 2 is triggered. ECB after repayment is shown below. The Available Commitment is not impacted. Since there is USD 3 in Overdrawn commitment, it is settled first. Hence the Overdrawn commitment is reduced from USD 3 to USD 1.

When repayment triggered for an additional amount of USD 11, the entire overdrawn commitment balance which holds the remaining capitalised fee amount of USD 1 is settled and subsequently principal balance is reduced by USD 10.

A revolving loan is sanctioned for 100 USD and fully disbursed. There is a disbursement activity fee linked to the product.

Overview and ECB record before disbursement

ECB record after loan is fully disbursed with USD 100 and the disbursement fee of USD 3 capitalised in Overdrawn Commitment balance.

When a repayment of USD 3 is triggered to the loan account, the capitalised fee amount is settled and the available commitment (CUR Commitment) does not get reinstated.

When a repayment of USD 10 is triggered towards principal, since the revolving flag is set to Payment, the available commitment gets reinstated by USD 10.

ECB record after repayment below

The reinstated amount can be disbursed by the user. When a disbursement of USD 5 is triggered, ECB record is impacted as shown below. A disbursement fee of USD 0.15 is capitalized and impacts the overdrawn commitment balance.

#### 📖 Introduction

The documents and images provided for the arrangement can be viewed in the Arrangement Overview screen for AA products. AA is integrated with the Document Management and Image Management modules for managing the documents and images.

It is possible to notify the customers on occurrence of specific activities. A pre-notification can be enabled for the scheduled activities before the event takes place. The system also produces SWIFT type confirmation messages (like loan confirmation, interest payment due, rate change advice, etc) as required.

The features related to sending notifications to customers are not applicable to loans in TBC and must be handled through an external delivery system based on the events generated from the loan. Read Introduction to TBC for Lending for more information about TBC for loans.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Document Management can capture and upload (store) the documents, and the Image Management is used to store and retrieve images at arrangement level.

The AA.TXN.DOC enquiry is used to view, reverse, edit and upload the transaction documents. It is also possible to upload or reverse uploaded documents or images using the Correspondence tab as and when required. For instance, the loan agreement obtained by the bank is available at the arrangement level in the Correspondence tab (earlier named as Messages) of Arrangement Overview screen. DM.APPLICATION.INFO and DOC.GEN.CONDITION holds a record AAA. For the DM.APPLICATION.INFO with AAA DOC.GEN.CONDITION record ID specifies the activities for which document management has to be set up.

The Activity Messaging Property Class is used to configure the advices to be generated for the Activity Class or Activity for each customer role. The customer preferences can be configured for the same.

For further details read: Activity Messaging Property Class, Document Management section and Customer Preferences for Advices and Alerts under Arrangement Architechture.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Activity Messaging Property Class defines the advice to be generated for the respective Activity Class or Activity.


##### Pre-Notification Advices

Pre-Notification (Delivery Advice) is available for all scheduled activities across Product Lines (For example - Interest resets, Rollovers, etc.).

Pre-notice days are indicated for the respective Activity.

The LENDING–PRE.NOTICE-ARRANGEMENT Activity Class has SEND.MESSAGE action for delivery message processing. When an Activity is set for PRE.NOTICE, a pre notice Activity is created for that Activity dynamically.

For example, if PRE.NOTICE.ACTIVITY is selected as LENDING-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT, then an Activity named LENDING-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT-PRE.NOTICE is created automatically, based on LENDING-PRE.NOTICE-ARRANGEMENT Activity Class.

In this example, the user can view the Pre-notice Activity and Pre-notice Days set up for few scheduled activities in Activity Messaging Product Conditions for Lending.

EB.ADVICES for each Activity and respective DE.FORMATS are attached.

##### SWIFT Message Confirmation

- For AA Loan Products, if required, the system can be configured to produce SWIFT type confirmation messages. For customers who are eligible to send and receive SWIFT messages, the following messages are supported in AA. MT320 Fixed Loan or Deposit Confirmation MT330 Call Loan or Deposit Confirmation MT350 Advice of Loan or Deposit Interest Payment MT935 Rate Change Advice
- The Trade Date attribute is the date the contract is agreed with the customer or counterparty. This date can be backdated or equivalent to the Effective Date but it cannot occur after the Effective Date .
- The Effective Date attribute (value date equivalent) can be a date in the future when the actual contract starts. For example, a loan this is the first date that the funds can be disbursed or for a deposit when funds are initially expected.
- Settlement instruction can be defined in the Settlement Property Class.
- From the Overview screen, the drill down displays the advices output. MT 320 Output is shown below.
- Different SWIFT messages can also be produced based on the following activities: XXXXXX-NEW-ARRANGEMENT (Term Defined) When a term is defined in the contract, the message generated is format type MT320. XXXXXX-NEW-ARRANGEMENT (No Term Defined) When a term is not defined in the contract (that is, a call contract), the message generated is format type MT330. XXXXXX-ISSUEBILL-PAYMENT.SCHEDULE When a contract has an interest payment schedule defined, the next schedule of interest generates a MT350 (The MAKEDUE Activity can be triggered xx days in advance. XXXXXX-CHANGE.TERM-TERM.AMOUNT When an amendment to the term of the contract is made this generates an AMEND type MT320. XXXXXX-ROLLOVER-ARRANGEMENT When a rollover of the contract is made this generates a ROLL type MT320 XXXXXX-MATURE-ARRANGEMENT When the contract is due to mature this generates a MATURITY type MT320. XXXXXX-CHANGE-INTEREST When a change of interest rate is made this generates a MT935. XXXXXX-PERIODIC.RESET-INTEREST When a periodic rate change happens based on a frequency, this generate a MT935

### 1.30  Loan Disbursements
