Scheduled disbursement can be configured through Payment Schedule, which automatically debits the loan accounts and credits the specified settlement account. A loan opened in the system can also be disbursed throu...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PAYMENT.TYPE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Active Y/N*, *Actual Amt*, *Amount*, *Arrangement Id*, *Bill Type*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *Customer ID* ... +13 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Disbursement is the process to part with the committed loan amount in full or in part. Scheduled disbursement can be configured through Payment Schedule, which automatically debits the loan accounts and credits the specified settlement account. A loan opened in the system can also be disbursed through FT, Teller, Cash Pooling, or directly from the arrangement.

When a new backdated loan arrangement is opened and an AR settlement account is defined, it is possible to disburse a loan and crediting the AR account.

The Payment Schedule projection considers future scheduled disbursement event and calculates the respective payment amount on the arrangement date itself.

The features related to automatic disbursement are not applicable for loans in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describes the configuration of manual, automatic and scheduled loan disbursement.


##### Manual Disbursement

Loans can be set to have automatic or manual disbursement. When the auto disbursement conditions have not been defined before the loan has been approved, the loan has to be manually disbursed.

> **⚠️ Note:** Manual Disbursements cannot have scheduled disbursement definitions and the Include Future Disb set as Progressive in Payment Schedule Conditions.

It is possible to restrict the amount that can be disbursed in a loan. When the Periodic Attribute FULL.DISBURSEMENT is set with value YES, the system allows only full disbursement of the loan and partial disbursement is not allowed.

This setup can be used when the bank wants to restrict the loan to a single disbursement.


##### Automatic Disbursement

Disbursement rules are generally defined in the Payment Schedule Product Condition. The conditions for the automated disbursement are defined in the loan payment schedule. The disbursement can be setup to take place immediately upon loan approval or at a later date. The amount disbursed can be the full amount or loan can be partially defined.

Disbursements could be automated through payment schedule definition and the customer account can be credited using the Payout Rules definition.

The options listed below can be used to automatically disburse loans:

1. Online For a loan arrangement to disburse the loan amount immediately, configure the payment schedule as Disbursement Amount or Percentage and set the Schedule Type in AA.PAYMENT.TYPE as Online. On successful creation of the loan, the loan amount is disbursed to the customer account, for example, savings and current accounts.
2. Service Perform automatic disbursement of a loan using the AA.PROCESS.ACTIVITIES service by configuring the Schedule Type in AA.PAYMENT.TYPE as Service for the DISBURSEMENT.AMT and DISBURSEMENT.%. payment schedule types. On successful creation of the loan, the loan account number is updated in the list of contracts for which service must be run for disbursement (AA.PROCESS.ACTIVITIES.LIST). The loan is disbursed when the AA.PROCESS.ACTIVITIES is run or during the COB. This helps in improving the performance of the system and reduces the loan creation time as the disbursement is moved to a service.

DISBURSEMENT.AMT and DISBURSEMENT. % Payment types are used to define schedule disbursements in Payment Schedule record.

For scheduled disbursement, the Bill Type attribute in the Payment Schedule should be kept as DISBURSEMENT.

The below screenshots display the sample of DISBURSEMENT. % and DISBURSEMENT.AMT setup for auto disbursement.

> **⚠️ Note:** FULL.DISBURSEMENT Periodic Attribute setup in Term Amount can also be used to setup the kind of disbursement in automatic and scheduled disbursements.

Auto disbursement of funds on new loans can also be facilitated through Term Amount Property Conditions with no dependency on Payment Schedule. Read Term Amount Property Class for further details.

The features related to automatic disbursement are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Scheduled Disbursement

A scheduled disbursement is possible by indicating the Start date as the date of disbursement.

On the disbursement date, the loan amount is disbursed to the settlement account indicated and the corresponding Payout rules. When the settlement account is not set, the balance is moved to AVL .

The AVL balance type is used exclusively for scheduled disbursement. It indicates the loan amount available for disbursement. This is a contingent credit balance on the loan, which is credited when the disbursement bill is made payable.

The following accounting events are added to the existing allocation rules to support scheduled disbursements:

- ACCOUNT-MAKE.DUE-PAY-AVL
- ACCOUNT-PAY-PAY-AVL
- SETTLEMENT-SETTLE-PAY

The following Activity Classes support automatic scheduled disbursement.

- LENDING-MAKEDUE.DISBURSE-PAYMENT.SCHEDULE
- LENDING-AUTO.DISBURSE-TERM.AMOUNT

- Payout of scheduled disbursement can be defined using Settlement Property Condition.
- To achieve this, the settle Activity must be defined as LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PO.WITHDRAWAL

The Payout Property Class is used to support the automatic scheduled disbursement and payout of rebate or bonus offered in the loan arrangement. Using this Property Class, the user can define the rules to pay out the arrangement balances.

It is also used to payout the bill amount due to the customer. An arrangement can have one or more bill outstanding due to be paid to the customer. The Payout Rules Property conditions decide whether the first or the last bill has to be settled first. In addition, the sequence in which the properties are to be settled is also defined here.

When multiple disbursements are scheduled in a loan, the payment amount has to be calculated progressively considering all the scheduled and disbursed amounts.

To achieve this, future scheduled disbursements have to be defined as Forward Dated conditions and the Include Future Disb attribute in Payment Schedule Property Class has to be defined as Progressive.

It is possible to settle the funds automatically to the settlement account by a set up for Back Dated Settlement Processing.

The features related to automatic disbursement are not applicable for loans in TBC.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes the processing of loan disbursement.


##### Manual Disbursement

Arrangement loans can be disbursed using the applications, such as Funds Transfer, Teller and Payment Order. These options are available under Loan Transactions option in the User Menu.


##### Automatic Disbursement

- During an arrangement creation, the Schedule, Settlement Instructions and Commitment tabs are used to define the disbursement details.
- The disbursement amount can be defined as a value or a percentage during arrangement creation. To define the disbursement amount as a percentage, use the Percentage attribute To define the disbursement amount as a value, use the Actual Amt attribute
- The Actual Amt attribute is mandatory to define a disbursement schedule (Account - Pay), and the sum of the future schedules should sum up to the CUR .
- When adhoc payments are defined, the user must define the Actual Amt for each payment date.

The features related to automatic disbursement are not applicable for loans in TBC.

The below screen shot displays an arrangement with automatic scheduled disbursement.

Consider that a customer entered in to a loan agreement with the bank for 30000 USD on 1 April, 2020 for a loan term of one year. The first payout happens for 75% on 1 April, 2020 and the next payout happens for 25% on 1 Oct, 2020. The Include Future Disb field is set as Progressive and the disbursement payout on two different dates is scheduled by way of using forward dated conditions tab at the arrangement level. The payment amount is calculated based on the respective disbursement events.

The payment amount from 1 April, 2020 to 1 Oct, 2020 is based on 22500 USD and from 1 Nov, 2020, it is based on the outstanding balance as on 1 Oct, 2020 plus the additional payout of 7500 USD. That is, assume the outstanding on 1 Oct, 2020 is 20100 USD plus USD 7,500. The resulting amount 27,600 USD (20100 + 7500) is the base for payment amount calculation.

The below screen shot displays the bill details and activity log for the scheduled disbursement.

- The arrangement amount can be disbursed in single or multiple disbursements depending on the Product Conditions.
- Disbursements and payments can be made in a currency other than the arrangement currency.
- Drawdown and disbursements can be done through Funds Transfer or Teller.
- When a limit is not specified at arrangement level, the system generates an override during disbursement.
- Disbursement can be made to a specified customer account, NOSTRO, AA or internal account, or it can be made even in cash. Disbursement can also be done through Settlement Product Condition.
- During disbursement, the system validates the disbursement against the committed amount, the current outstanding amount and any applicable Activity Restriction.
- An arrangement account does not show any working balance when it is created, since amount is only committed. Only when a disbursement is made, the arrangement account can be debited and its working balance can be updated.
- Payout Rules is enabled in the Lending product line to payout the arrangement balances.
- The charges collected during disbursement done through FT and Teller cannot be modified or waived.
- For a back value dated arrangement the disbursement of funds can be initially backdated or alternatively paid effective today.

- The user can update any limit for the sanctioned loan using the Limit Id field in the Limit condition. The TBC generates an event to the external limit system which approves the limit attached to the loan in TBC.
- The features related to automatic disbursement are not applicable for loans in TBC.

### 1.31  Loan Pre-closure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Pre-closure is a process when a customer repays the loan before the loan tenure ends. For example, the pre-closure of a home loan implies that a customer is willing to close a home loan before the completion of its repayment period. The banks can levy a charge as a pre-closure fee.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARR.SETTLEMENT`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT.PHASE`, `AA.BILL.DETAILS`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Active Y/N*, *Arrangement Id*, *Bill Type*, *Cash Dep Amount*, *Combine Bills*, *Credit Account*, *Credit Amount*, *Credit Currency* ... +32 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Pre-closure is a process when a customer repays the loan before the loan tenure ends. For example, the pre-closure of a home loan implies that a customer is willing to close a home loan before the completion of its repayment period. The banks can levy a charge as a pre-closure fee.

This option can be executed on regular loans where the customer wants to close this contract with the bank for reasons like getting a new mortgage loan or change of ownership in underlying property. Pre-closure can also be done for non-paying assets.

There are no specific limitations related to prepayment of loan contracts in TBC.

To pre-close the loan before reaching the maturity date, the customer/user initiates the transaction in the external payment system (outside the TBC). When a payment is received to pre-close the loan, an API is triggered to credit the funds using the required repayment activity. The funds are apportioned to the balances based on the repayment rules of this Activity triggered.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section deals with the configuration of loan pre-closure.When a loan has a payoff in progress (payoff simulated) it can be identified from the single customer view of the loan.


##### Payoff Property Class

The Payoff Property Class is used to generate the payoff statement at the arrangement level.

The payoff bill can be configured to generate the payoff amount for the Expiry Days defined.

When the payoff date simulation is set for a future date, the system can be configured to settle the bills in-between, by setting Settle Dues to Yes. When set to Yes, the Settle Due Act is mandatory. The settlement activity for regular repayment under LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PAYMENT.RULES Activity Class is input here.

Settle Act is the settlement Activity for calculating the payoff amount in simulation mode or when the arrangement is paid-off in live using SETTLE Activity of Payoff Property Class. Any pre-closure charge must be configured for only to this Activity.


##### Payoff Facility

When the loan is released as facility, the payoff is also possible at the facility level. In such cases, the loan is paid off through a settlement by payment order at the facility level and thus it is possible to have a full redemption of all arrangements in the facility. Here, the system considers all the early payment charges configured in the loan. It is possible that each of the drawing under the facility has a different early payment charge configured and in such case the charges of the individual drawing (lending arrangement) are used during the payoff accordingly.

When a loan has an overpayment charge configured (using overpayment limits), then those overpayment charges are applicable even during the loan payoff.

Read Limiting Overpayments section for more information.

It is not possible to create and maintain loan contracts under a facility using TBC. Therefore, the features related to pay off at the facility level are not applicable in TBC.


##### Phase Based Overpayment Charges

Banks or financial institutions can collect a charge from the customer for making repayments that exceed the overpayment limit. It can setup such charges with different conditions over the different phases of the loan.

Effective Phase is updated for the phases that are defined in the Product Phases tab. When the Product Condition is mapped for the required Property, Effective Phase in the Product Phases tab is selected to define the applicable effective date. The phases are defined as records in the AA.ARRANGEMENT.PHASE virtual table. The following example lists the possible effective phases:

- Fixed rate initially
- Second year fixed rate effective from one year after the arrangement creation date
- Variable rate effective from two years after the arrangement creation date
- Preferred variable rate effective from three years after the arrangement creation date


##### Tax on Accrued Interest

During payoff, the accrued interest is collected by the bank. The system can be configured to calculate the tax on accrued interest (both principal interest and penalty interest) at the time of collection of that accrued interest when the Tax Inclusive field is set as Yes in the corresponding Payment Rule Type used for the payment.

When the penalty interest is set to accrue by bills and is part of the payoff statement, it is important to include the accrued penalty interest as current repayment rule type and to set Tax Inclusive and Make Due option for that repayment rule type.

The Make Due field set as Yes in the Payment Rule Type, includes the accrued interest and its corresponding tax collected in the loan statement.

> **⚠️ Note:** If Tax Inclusive is set to Yes, then Make Due should also be set as Yes. Else, the system raises an error when the Payment Rule Type is committed.


##### Payoff Tolerance

In AA, the tolerance functionality was available only for repayment of due bills. The tolerance definition is done in the Overdue Property Class. Tolerance can be defined as a percentage or as an amount. In case of amounts, tolerance amounts can be defined as currency-specific. There is also a tolerance action that can be defined.

Now all these attributes are moved to Payoff Property Class for tolerance definition at the time of payoff.

| Attribute Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Tolerance Percent | To define tolerance as a percentage of total payoff amount |
| Tolerance Ccy (Xx | To define the currency for currency specific tolerance amounts |
| ) | To define the currency- specific absolute amount |
| Tolerance Action | To define the action for the shortfall within tolerance. The only option available now is to Write-Off the shortfall. |

Tolerance definition can be done at product level and can be negotiated at the arrangement level or can directly be defined at arrangement level.

During pay-off, the funds are appropriated based on the payment rule defined in the Payoff condition. When the funds are exhausted and there are some unsettled balances in the loan, then the tolerance check is done. If the short fall amount is less than or equal to the tolerance defined (as a % or amount) then the shortfall amount is written off. The write-off sequence is from the Property or balance with the least priority. It moves from the least priority to the highest priority.

The written off amount is posted to a separate PL (GL) as defined in the underlying accounting events linked in accounting conditions.

To complete the accounting related to processing pre-closure of a loan contract, the TBC generates an event which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.

The following accounting events are released for defining the PL heads upon tolerance write-off.

- ACCOUNT-ADJUST.BILL-DUE-OS.TOL.WOF
- ACCOUNT-CREDIT-DUE-TOL.WOF
- CHARGE-ADJUST.BILL-DUE-OS.TOL.WOF
- CHARGE-ADJUST.BILL-DUE-OS.TOL.WOF.SP
- INTEREST-ADJUST.BILL-DUE-CURR.TOL.WOF
- INTEREST-ADJUST.BILL-DUE-CURR.TOL.WOF.SP
- INTEREST-ADJUST.BILL-DUE-OS.TOL.WOF
- INTEREST-ADJUST.BILL-DUE-OS.TOL.WOF.SP
- INTEREST-CREDIT-DUE-SP.TOL.WOF
- INTEREST-CREDIT-DUE-TOL.WOF
- INTEREST-CREDIT-RES-TOL.WOF


#### 🔧 Working With

Loans can be pre-closed when the customer pays off the loan outstanding. The pre-closure amount is simulated using the Payoff Property Class. Payoff statement includes all the principal, interest and charges that are due as a result of payoff.

The payoff bill generated has the itemised calculated amounts. It adjusts the system calculated amounts and shows the adjusted amounts along with the original calculated amounts in payoff statement. Whenever a new payoff statement is requested, the old one is deleted and a new payoff bill is created.

The Lending Calculate Payoff Activity can only be run in simulation mode and cannot be scheduled by the user. The activity should use the CALCULATE action to calculate the payoff amounts. The ACTION routine calculates the total outstanding amount of the loan contract as on the payoff date, including all overdue amounts and current amounts.

The Expiry Days field is used to define expiry date for the payoff bill. The number of days defined is taken as working days and the expiry date for the payoff bill is calculated as the payoff date plus the number of working days defined in this field. When the expiry date is reached, the payoff bill is purged (deleted).

If the payoff date is in future it is possible that it may be after several expected regular payment dates. In such cases there can be an automatic repayment of such dues or they can be treated as unpaid dues. When running the simulation scenario, the user can choose to uncheck any future payments or add any other transaction as they do with any other simulation.

The payoff statement includes current balances which are not yet due to pay off the loan contract fully. The CALCULATE action routine gets all the properties linked to the arrangement for the Account, Interest and Charge Property Classes.

Any credit in unallocated credit balance (UNC) of Account Property is automatically used to settle the dues as and when they are created. The credit balance is used only to settle regular dues and not for any dues resulting due to charges on activities or rule break charges.

In this illustration, there is an overdue loan with penalty interest and principal interest accrued. The product payment rules has a setup with tax configured on principal and penalty interest.

On 15th April 2021, Payoff simulation is run.

It can be seen in the payoff statement that a tax of USD 2.49 is calculated on the penalty interest of USD 24.86 and a tax of USD 56.31 is calculated on the principal interest of USD 563.08.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system collects the tax along with the accrued interest (both principal and penalty) only when Tax Inclusive field is set to Yes in the prepayment activity used.

When the user opens a payoff statement generated within loan arrangement overview screen, a Settle by Payment Order option is available as a Closure method. Clicking on the button, system generates a Payment Order application with auto-populated fields related to the arrangement. If Payin Account is available in AA.ARR.SETTLEMENT , the Debit Account Number along with the Debit Account IBAN and Debit Currency fields are automatically populated by the system. The rest of payment order information is populated with the debit payment amount, credit account, credit currency, debit value date, required credit value date from the Info bill generated for Payoff and stored in AA.BILL.DETAILS and Payment Execution Date field from system date. In the below screen shot the auto-populated fields can be seen in the Payment Order version generated after triggering Settle by Payment Order from the payoff statement.

The Payment Order is processed based on Payment Connection Method set in Payment Order Parameter . The Payment Connection Method can be Funds Transfer, Temenos Payment System, any external system or a conditional option.

To pre-close the loan before reaching the maturity date, the customer/user initiates the transaction in the external payment system (outside the TBC). When a payment is received to pre-close the loan, an API is triggered to credit the funds using the required repayment activity. The funds are apportioned to the balances based on the repayment rules of this Activity triggered.


###### Payoff Request at SCV

When the user initiates the payoff simulation, the this information is updated in the Payoff Request initiated of the Single Customer View (SCV) screen

When the user initiates a payoff request from the interface, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in TBC to complete the loan pre-closure process. The features related to initiation of payoff using the single customer view screen are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Payoff at Facility Level

The user can trigger a loan pre-closure at the facility level and route the closure proceeds settlement through a payment order at the facility level. Read Payoff Facility for more information.

Consider a facility of USD 120,000, which includes arrangements of USD 100,000 and USD 20,000 respectively. During a payoff at the facility level, the system considers the principal repayment, interest repayment and other associated charges (like principal decrease fee, early repayment charges, payoff charges and so on) at each of the drawing level (arrangement level).

During a payoff facility with settlement by payment order, the payoff settles the following outstanding amounts:

- Account - USD 120,000 (sum of the two arrangements 100,000 and 20,000 USD)
- Principal interest - 67.46 (arrangements have an interest of 56.22 and 11.24 respectively as shown below)
- Payment Fee - 2,400 (arrangements have a payment fee of 2,000 and 400 respectively as shown below)

Here, the charges (that is, payment fee) are associated with both the arrangement individually and the same is considered for the payoff of the entire facility.

It is not possible to create and maintain loan contracts under a facility using TBC. Therefore, the features related to pay off at the facility level are not applicable in TBC.


##### Pre-payment Charges

Pre-payment charges may be set as a periodic rule or an activity charge. The banks allow pre-payments up to a certain limit, which can be a percentage of the loan amount or a fixed amount for a rolling period – anniversary period that is, in a year the customer is allowed to pre-pay a percentage of the loan and is usually cumulative.

A periodic rule can be setup in Payment Rules Property to calculate the prepayment charges when excess prepayments are done. Or the pre-payment charges may simply be a fixed amount which could be setup as Activity Charges on pre-payment activity.

During simulation, the system simulates all of the scheduled activities, any user-specified activities and accruals up to the effective date. At the end of the simulation process (up to the payoff date) bills are created for all regular payments as well for any rule (Periodic Rules, Activity Charges) break charges. Based on the related activity for make-due activity the bills for regular payments may be settled or made overdue.


##### Payoff Tolerance

The user can create a mortgage arrangement with the following details:

- Tolerance Amount – 1.00
- Tolerance Currency – USD
- Tolerance Action – Write-Off

### 1.32  Loan Prepayments


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The system supports prepayments, bulk or ad hoc repayment of the loan. Such ad hoc payments can be charged and restricted based on some conditions and a penalty can also be applied if these conditions are not met.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE.CLASS`, `AA.PRD.DES.ACTIVITY.RESTRICTION`, `REPAY.TOLERANCE.CURRENT`, `REPAY.TOLERANCE.TOTAL`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Balance Type*, *Balances To Be Paid For The Property*, *Make Due*, *On Activity*, *Penalty Days*, *Penalty Type*, *Prepay Tolerance*, *Recalculate* ... +1 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The system supports prepayments, bulk or ad hoc repayment of the loan. Such ad hoc payments can be charged and restricted based on some conditions and a penalty can also be applied if these conditions are not met.

There are no specific limitations related to prepayment of loan contracts in TBC.

To prepay the loan principal in TBC, the customer/user initiates the transaction in the external payment system (outside the TBC). When a pre-payment is received, an API is triggered to credit the funds using the required repayment activity. The funds are apportioned to the balances based on the repayment rules of this Activity triggered.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describes the configuration of loan prepayments.


##### Prepayments

To configure a bulk repayment towards the loan principal, the transaction code used for the payment must be mapped to a payment activity that repays the loan principal.

The below screenshot displays the payment rule setup to repay the current (live) principal balance.

As the payment rule repays the current balances, the application order is not required. The Balances To Be Paid For The Property field is set as Balances. The Balance Type field is updated as CURACCOUNT in live principal of the ACCOUNT Property.

The loan prepayments are a bulk repayment towards the loan principal. It is optional to collect the accrued interest till date along with the bulk prepayment. The configuration for that payment rule is shown below:

The corresponding payment rule type used is shown below.

To prepay the loan amount in TBC, the customer/user initiates the prepayment transaction in the external payment system (outside the TBC). When a pre-payment is received, an API is triggered to credit the funds using the required repayment activity. The funds are apportioned to the balances based on the repayment rules of this Activity triggered.


###### Accounting Entries for Advance Interest

When the user pays the interest accrued till date along with the principal prepayment, the customer will prefer to see the repayment details in the loan statements as well. The principal repayment is for the balance type, and it appears in the account statement as a STMT.ENTRY. To display the accrued interest collected in advance in the loan statement, the accrued interest settlement should also pass through a make due process. To enable this, the Make Due field should be set as Yes in the Payment Rule Type that is used to settle (repay) the accrued interest.

- To complete the accounting related to collecting accrued interest (till date) in advance along with the principal prepayment, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.
- The loan statement features are maintained in an external solution, and are not applicable for loans in TBC.


###### Tax on Advance Interest

The system can be configured to calculate the tax on accrued interest (both principal interest and penalty interest) at the time of collection of that interest when the Tax Inclusive field is set as Yes in the corresponding Payment Rule Type used for the payment.

> **⚠️ Note:** If Tax Inclusive is set as Yes, then Make Due should also be set as Yes. Else, the system raises an error when the Payment Rule Type is committed.


##### Restricting the Prepayments

The bulk payment can be restricted based on a percentage of the original commitment amount or the current outstanding balance of the loan. The periodic attributes in the Activity Restriction Property Class can be configured to achieve this. The bank can also calculate and levy a penalty on such repayment amount, as well as take charges during the repayment activity.

The periodic attributes can be configured to restrict the prepayment amount allowed in the first one year of the loan.

This record can be added in the Activity Restriction to control the prepayment in first one year of arrangement.

The below screenshot displays the Prepay Tolerance periodic attribute that is used to apply the tolerance on prepayment amount. Here, the tolerance is applied on the total repayment amount for the life of the arrangement.

Activity Restriction configuration enables restricting the amount of prepayment or the period of prepayments. The periodic attribute created can be used in the Activity Restriction to create the control.

The below screenshot displays AA.PRD.DES.ACTIVITY.RESTRICTION setup for charging on pre-payments with prepayment capped at 25% of the outstanding commitment.

The Activity Restriction Property Class is used for setting-up repayment charges. The repayment charges may be set as a periodic rule or as an activity charge. The banks allow repayments up to a certain limit, which can be a percentage of the loan amount or a fixed amount for a rolling period, anniversary period, that is, in a year, the customer can repay a percentage of the loan and it is usually a cumulative amount.

In such cases, a periodic rule can be setup in the Payment Rules Property to calculate the repayment charges when excess repayments are done, or the repayment charges may simply be a fixed amount that can be setup as Activity Charges on repayment activity.

The Prepay Tolerance periodic attribute is used to apply tolerance on pre-payment amount based on the total commitment amount of the loan. In the above example, if the pre-paid amount exceeds by 25% of the commitment amount, penalty is charged.

Also, the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-REPAYRULE5 Activity is for settlement of current balances of the loan (which includes settlement of current balance of ACCOUNT as well) that caters to pre-payment.

The charge condition attached for rule break charge (in this case, for pre-payment above 25%) has charge routine attached:

Charge Condition for RULEBREAKCHARGE has the charge routine attached.

Consider an example of an arrangement with commitment amount 2,000,000. The allowed pre-payment as per 25% tolerance setup is 500,000. When the user makes a pre-payment above 500,000, penalty (rule break charge) is calculated on the excess amount pre-paid.

It is possible to calculate the penalty on the prepayment amount as well as taking charges during the prepayment Activity.

The prepayment can be restricted based on a percentage of original commitment amounts or the current outstanding balance of the loan and is achieved through the Activity Restriction and using the AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE.CLASS records, REPAY.TOLERANCE.CURRENT and REPAY.TOLERANCE.TOTAL .

A prepayment charge can be configured for the product. This charge is calculated using the AA.CALCULATE.PREPAYMENT.PENALTY charge routine. The penalty calculation is the values defined in Penalty Type and Penalty Days local reference fields, which can be released during implementation. Thus, when the prepayment amount exceeds the percentage allowed on the anniversary period, it is also possible to collect a penalty on the excess amount prepaid and the same can be calculated using a method from the below list:

1. No Penalty: Prepayments are permitted at any time without penalty. There are no restrictions on the amount (minimums or maximums) or the timing of the prepayment.
2. Interest till end of term: The interest that is otherwise payable to the end of the payment term on the amount of the prepayment is calculated and applied as a penalty. It is calculated as follows:
3. Penalty number of days: Period of a number of days interest is set to be calculated on the amount of the prepayment and applied as a penalty. Example: Penalty 180 Days is calculated as follows:
4. Penalty 3 months: This method of calculation is similar to #3 with the exception that the number of penalty days is not configurable and is fixed as 91.25 days based on the average number of days per month (365/12 * 3=91.25).
5. Interest Rate Differential (IRD): If DR is greater than CR, then calculate Penalty 3 Months and Interest to end of the term and take the lesser of the two.
6. Greater of 3 months or IRD: The system calculates penalty using methods 4 and 5 to determine the greater of the two and uses this amount.

For each of the penalty calculation method 3, 4, 5, and 6, the system compares the penalty calculated against method 2 and takes whichever is lesser.

The On Activity field has to be set to the Principal Decrease Activity and the Recalculate can be set to,

- Term, there by the same installment amount continues and the term decreases correspondingly.
- Payment, where the repayment amount (installment) is calculated (decreased) and the term of the loan remains the same.

This kind of penalty can be configured and collected through the periodic rule break charges in AA.PRD.DES.ACTIVITY.RESTRICTION Product Condition. The base amount for the tolerance calculation can be either total commitment amount of the arrangement or the current outstanding balance of the loan.

On a prepayment or an ad hoc bulk payment, the system can be configured to recalculate the term or the payment amount using the setup in Payment Schedule Conditions.

The On Activity field should be set to the Principal Decrease Activity and the Recalculate can be set to,

- Term, thereby the same installment amount would continue and term decreases correspondingly.
- Payment, where the repayment amount (installment) is calculated (decreased) and the term of the loan remains the same.


#### 🔧 Working With

Prepayment can settle just the loan principal in advance or settle the loan principal along with the accrued interest till date. When such an accrued interest is settled, the tax collection for the accrued interest and how they appear in loan statements are explained in the configuration section.

Consider a prepayment of a loan in this example.

A mortgage loan is created on 5th April, 2021 and balances as on 15th April, 2021 are as follows:

After a loan prepayment of USD 50,000 on 15th April, 2021.

Accrued principal interest of USD 370.19 and tax on the accrued principal interest of USD 37.02 are settled. The remaining amount of USD 49,592.79 is settled against the outstanding principal.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system collects the tax along with the accrued interest (both principal and penalty) only when Tax Inclusive field is set as Yes in the prepayment activity used.

- To prepay the loan amount in TBC, the customer/user initiates the prepayment transaction in the external payment system (outside the TBC). When a pre-payment is received, an API is triggered to credit the funds using the required repayment activity. The funds are apportioned to the balances based on the repayment rules of this Activity triggered.
- The features pertaining to loan statements are not applicable for loan contracts in TBC.

### 1.33  Loan Renewal


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The banks can renew or rollover a loan on certain conditions. The system supports the manual and automatic scheduling of the Renewal or Rollover Activity.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Change Activity*, *Default Attr Option*, *Event Date*, *GB Narrative*, *Next Date*, *Renewal Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The banks can renew or rollover a loan on certain conditions. The system supports the manual and automatic scheduling of the Renewal or Rollover Activity.

There are no specific limitations for renewal or rollover of loan contracts in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Change Activity attribute in the Change Product Property Class determines the Activity to be triggered during a loan renewal. The available options are,

- ROLLOVER—Renews with the existing arrangement conditions. The Product Conditions are not considered except for the properties that track the Product Conditions.
- RESET—Resets to Product Conditions based on reset set-up at the product level for different properties. If the user chooses the RESET Activity on the renewal date, the resetting happens on payment end date. The renewal date is updated in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS , which is calculated based on the payment end date. The arrangement is reset with the current conditions. Maturity date and renewal date are recalculated based on the payment end date.

Loan renewal can be set on a specific date or after a specific period. Also, the loan renewal can be initiated automatically or manually. Change Product Property Class can be used to parameterize these conditions. Read the Change Product Property Class user guide for more information.

The Default Attr Option attribute in the Product Conditions defines the reset arrangement conditions from the Product during the rollover process.

- When the value is set as RESETTING, the Product Conditions are reset from the Product.
- When the value is set as NON-RESETTING, the Product Conditions are maintained at the arrangement level.


#### 🔧 Working With

When a loan rollover is configured in an arrangement using the Change Product Property Class, the arrangement can be automatically renewed. The conditions for the arrangement are based on the Activity triggered during the rollover. The arrangement is rolled over with the conditions of the new product based on the value in the Default Attr Option attribute when the LENDING-RESET-ARRANGEMENT Activity is used. Only the Default Attr Option attribute with RESETTING value has the latest product conditions applied and those with NON-RESETTING value the original (current) attribute values are retained.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Renewal Date attribute in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS for the specified account is updated when the new arrangement is rolled over.

In the below screenshot, the automatic renewal is configured every month. The details are recorded in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS application.

The below screenshot displays the Reset Activity scheduled in the arrangement. As the prior days are set for two days, the Event Date field is set to 17 May 19 and the Next Date field is set to15 May 19.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Manage And Decide On Amendments (AA)

The banks can renew or rollover a loan on certain conditions. The system supports the manual and automatic scheduling of the Renewal or Rollover Activity.

### 1.34  Loan Topup


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The banks can offer its customers, an additional loan amount on the existing loan as loan top-up. Loan top-ups are cost effective to the banks as it need not invest time and money acquiring and assessing new customers. In AA, the loan top-up is an addition to the loan commitment on live arrangements...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Arrangement*, *Change Amount*, *Commitment Drawdown*, *GB Narrative*, *Include Future Disb*, *Percentage*, *Status*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The banks can offer its customers, an additional loan amount on the existing loan as loan top-up. Loan top-ups are cost effective to the banks as it need not invest time and money acquiring and assessing new customers. In AA, the loan top-up is an addition to the loan commitment on live arrangements. The system allows to increase the commitment amount of a lending arrangement to provide the loan top-up.The topped up loans can be automatically disbursed and the disbursed amount appears as a line item in the payment schedule projection.

The new payment amount including the future scheduled increase commitment can be projected in the payment schedule on the effective date itself.

The features related to automatic disbursement of the top up amount are not applicable for loans in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Term Amount Property Class is used to define the maximum commitment amount for a Product. This is defined in the Amount attribute. The Amount attribute can be fully negotiable or be set as negotiable for a maximum amount which is the cap. It is also possible to increase the commitment of this cap amount. The user can use the LENDING-INCREASE-TERM.AMOUNT Activity Class to increase the commitment amount.

The disbursement of the top-up amount can be set to automatic as per configuration in the Settlement Property Class. While performing the Activity, the user can also schedule the disbursement of this loan to the same or any future date. It is also possible to perform the disbursement using FT, TT or Payment Order.

The Commitment Drawdown attribute in the Term Amount Property Conditions should be set as Auto (as shown below) to achieve automatic disbursement of both new and top up loans respecting the given settlement instructions.

The features related to automatic disbursement of the top up amount are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Including Future Scheduled Disbursements

The repayment amount with respect to future scheduled disbursements can be known on the effective scheduled date itself when the Include Future Disb attribute in Payment Schedule property conditions is set to Progressive.

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Commitment Amount | 100,000 |
| Start | 50% (50,000) |
| START + 6M |  |


#### 🔧 Working With

A loan top-up can be achieved by increasing the loan commitment amount and disbursing it. The Change Amount attribute can be used to indicate the top-up amount while performing the LENDING-INCREASE-TERM.AMOUNT Activity.

If the arrangement is set for single disbursement, then the user cannot disburse the increased amount. Hence, any disbursements setting should be configured accordingly.

In the below arrangement, USD 87,165 is disbursed and the Status field set to Current.

In this arrangement, the initial commitment is 900,000 and disbursed.

The below screenshot displays the account details.

This loan is topped using the Increase Commitment Activity, and the commitment is increased by another 15,000 USD.

In this case, an automatic disbursement is not set for increased commitment.

The below screenshots display the financial summary and the ECB balances. It shows that the TOTCOMMITMENT and CURCOMMITMENT are increased and the amount is ready for disbursal.


##### Increase Commitment Simulation

The user can simulate the increased commitment activity and view the schedule projection in the simulated overview screen to know the payment amount of the contract based on the increased loan amount. The simulated activity when converted to live facilitates automatic disbursement to the given settlement instructions when the Commitment Drawdown is set to Auto.

Customer A buys a loan for 5000 USD for a term of two years(2Y) and later he requests the bank for an additional loan of 1000 USD. The disbursement of loan happens via Payment order. The Commitment Drawdown is chosen as Auto. The bank simulates the Increased Commitment activity and agrees with the customer to pay the top up amount. After the customer agrees, the top up activity gets converted to live for automatic disbursement of top up amount for the given settlement instructions. The projection of schedules after the increased commitment disbursement is based on the increased amount plus the remaining principal outstanding.

The features related to automatic disbursement of the top up amount are not applicable for loans in TBC.

### 1.35  Loan WriteOff


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A bank writes off a loan when the borrower becomes insolvent due to various reasons and the underlying loan, or an asset is no more recoverable from the customer. The bank may book such loans as bad loans and eliminate a portion or a whole amount of such loan from its balance sheet.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCE.BALANCES`, `STMT.ENTRY`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A bank writes off a loan when the borrower becomes insolvent due to various reasons and the underlying loan, or an asset is no more recoverable from the customer. The bank may book such loans as bad loans and eliminate a portion or a whole amount of such loan from its balance sheet.

There are no specific limitations related to writing off loan contracts in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no separate configuration for write off of loans. The Balance Maintenance Property Class has to be available in the product.


##### Accounting for Write-off Arrangement

When the LENDING-WRITE.OFF-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE (arrangement write-off) activity is triggered, the system triggers the LENDING-ADJUST.BALANCE-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE activity for adjusting the balances.

The accounting entries are posted according to the accounting and the soft accounting allocation rule configurations. In the illustration used for write-off arrangement activity, the accounting condition for this product has an allocation rule that is, the LOAN.ACCOUNT allocation rule is attached on the ADJUST.BILL action. Accounting set up and allocation rules can be seen in the below screenshot:

For the ADJUST.BILL action, the contra entry is captured in the internal account (U-AAWOF). This is categorised in ACCOUNT.CLASS as AA Write-off.

To complete the accounting related to write-off of loans in TBC, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


#### 🔧 Working With

A write-off can be performed at three levels of an arrangement:

- Write-off Bills – Reduces liability on due bills
- Write-off Balances – Reduces outstanding principal balance
- Write-off Arrangement – Reduces all the loan bills and balances

When the loan principal is written off, the CUR (Outstanding Principal Balance) and UTL (Utilisation Balance) are updated. When the outstanding bills are written off, the corresponding due and overdue balances in the loan are updated.

| Pre Bill Write-Off | Post Bill Write-Off |
|---|---|
|  |  |

| Pre Balance Write-Off | Post Balance Write-Off |
|---|---|
|  |  |

| Pre Write-Off | Post Write-Off |
|---|---|
|  |  |


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Manage And Decide On Amendments (AA)

There are no Tasks available for Loan Write-off feature.
