### 1.36  LoanRestructuring


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When a customer is not able to repay the debts due to the inability to comply with the initially agreed repayment terms and conditions with the bank, the customer or a debt management advisor (on behalf of the customer) approaches the court with a request for restructuring the existing loans. Once t...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.AARANGEMENT`, `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT`, `AA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allocate As Per Ml*, *Allocate as Per Ml*, *Allocate as per MI*, *Allocate as per Ml*, *Arrangement*, *Auto Terminate ML*, *Auto Terminate Memo Loan*, *Book Memo Loan* ... +9 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

When a customer is not able to repay the debts due to the inability to comply with the initially agreed repayment terms and conditions with the bank, the customer or a debt management advisor (on behalf of the customer) approaches the court with a request for restructuring the existing loans. Once this restructuring is approved by the court, the restructuring activities take place (for example, interest can be suppressed). The customers can make repayments based on the restructured terms and conditions agreed upon between the bank and the customer.

The features related to loan restructuring are not applicable for loan contracts in TBC. Read Introduction to TBC for Lending for more information about TBC for loans.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The loan restructuring functionality provides an end-to-end process for restructuring a loan. The system provides the ability to initiate the restructuring process on the Original Loan (OL) on receipt of the related documents issued by the court. Based on the documentation provided, the user can trigger the corresponding restructure activity in the respective OL.


##### Restructuring Codes

Loan restructuring codes are used as part of the restructuring process which reflects the restructuring status of the Original Loan (OL) arrangements throughout the different stages of the restructuring process. The restructuring codes are updated on the OL arrangement on receipt of the court documentation, confirming the start of each of the stages.

The table below gives an illustrative list of different restructuring stage codes used as a standard practice. The implementation setup can have its own codes defined to illustrate the restructure status.

| Restructuring Codes | Description |
|---|---|
| INPROG | Corresponds to the initial restructuring stage which commences from the moment the bank receives the Court Intimation Receipt. The intimation signifies that the customer or debt advisor or bank has approached the court with a request for restructuring of his debt. This stage implies that the court is in the process of reviewing the customer’s request, overall debt, and financial circumstances. |
| APPRVE | Corresponds to the restructuring stage during which Technical Loan (TL) booking should be available. This stage commences from the moment the bank receives the Court Order on Approval Decision for restructuring. It signifies that the customer’s request is approved, and the debt must be restructured as per the Court Decision by stating the new terms and conditions that will be applied. It is further implemented using the TL. |
| REJECT | Corresponds to the restructuring stage in one of the following situations: The customer’s request for restructuring is rejected by the court because he/she is being inconsistent or unreasonable as per his/her current financial circumstances. This stage commences when the bank receives the Court Rejection Decision for restructuring, which signifies that the customer’s request is rejected, and the loan must revert to its original parameters. The bank has concluded that the customer(s) is/are unable to pay towards the TL and has decided the reversion to REJECT stage. When reverting from APPRVE to REJECT, all TLs must be manually closed before the actual change of status. (The rejection does not exclude the bank from approaching the court again in the future). |


##### Defining Restructure Stages usingAA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS

The AA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS table helps the user to define various stages of the restructuring process that the Original Loan (OL) has to undergo. The attributes in the table are:

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Restructure Status | Used to hold the restructure codes . The restructure status can take values defined in the restructure code like INPROG, APPRVE, and REJECT that denote restructure status of the loan. |
| Description | Used to display the restructure code’s short descriptions - business-wise description of the respective restructuring stage relating to the code. These can be amended even after the initial setup. |
| Previous Status | Used to display the allowed movements between the different restructure codes or stages. The system verifies the current restructuring status of the loan arrangement against this field in the AA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS table on triggering the restructuring process as well as on moving between the different restructuring stages. It validates if the arrangement is eligible to move to the status corresponding to the restructuring activity triggered. |
| Book Memo Loan | Used to define the stage during which the Technical Loan (TLs) booking functionality is allowed. The Book Memo Loan field must be set to Yes only on that particular restructure stage where a technical loan can be booked. This field is not mandatory itself, as restructuring does not always make use of the memo loans functionality. Yet this can be set for one restructure stage only. There is no restriction on the number of memo loans that can be booked under a single OL. |
| Auto Terminate Memo Loan | Used to define a specific behavior of the TLs when the outstanding balances of the OL become zero. This is referred to as automatically terminating the Technical Loans (TL) and is the default behavior for the TLs when the OLs reach zero outstanding and/or fulfill the closure conditions. |
| Allocate as Per Ml | If set as Yes, it indicates that the same portions of payments applied to a TL should also be applied to the OL per property (if a due amount for the respective property is in place). This is a no-change field and cannot be amended once set. |

> **⚠️ Note:** Once defined, the code names and the sequence of the restructure stages cannot be changed.

The below screenshot shows AA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS setup:


##### Configuring Restructure Rules Conditions

Consider a scenario where a customer or a debt advisor approaches the court for a loan restructure due to the financial inability to repay the debt and the corresponding restructure process takes place based on the terms and conditions of the court. This scenario is explained in the below diagram:

Each of the restructuring stages can have different characteristics from the point of view of suppression of penalties, interest accruals, and charges. The Restructure Rules Property Class is used to configure these components, which provides the bank with the ability to set restructure code-specific rules for suppressing or resuming accruals per property or property class. Read Restructure Rules Property Class for more information.

The below screenshot shows the configuration set up for the Restructure Rules Property Class for the above business requirement:

Based on the above setup, the system performs differently at each restructure status:

The system suppresses the property classes and properties listed against INPROG Rule Status in the Restructure Condition. Based on this setup during the INPROG stage in the original loan, the system:

- Stops the accrual of penalty interest
- Stops applying charges, fees or commission
- Stop any further scheduled or non- disbursements. Read Configuring Periodic Attribute and Activity Restriction for more information.

> **⚠️ Note:** The interest properties that are not marked as applicable for suppression under INPROG Rule Status, continue to accrue. The instalment amount and schedules are processed as per the payment frequency and continue to produce the bills.

The suppression of charges and penalty interest accruals commences as per the activity date that is when the LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*INPROG activity is triggered.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system can be configured for a RESUME action in the Rule Action field for the corresponding property or property class. But resuming any suppressed accruals is not applicable when there is no suppression done already.

The system suppresses the property classes and properties listed against APPRVE Rule Status in Restructure Rules product condition. Based on the setup, the APPRVE stage characterises the continuation of the suppressed during the previous, that is, INPROG stage properties or property classes. So, the system continues to:

- Stop the accrual of Penalty Interest
- Stop applying charges, fees or commission
- Stop any further scheduled or non- disbursements (configured using Activity Restriction)

> **⚠️ Note:** The properties not marked as applicable for suppression under APPRVE rule status continue to accrue.

Hence, the properties continue to remain in the suppressed state as the Suppression is already triggered at the INPROG stage.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system can also be configured to add a different property, say PRINCIPALINT for suppression at this stage.

A Resume action can be configured in the Rule Action field for the corresponding property or property class at this stage but it is not applicable at this restructure stage.

The REJECT stage characterises the termination of the suppression and resume of the suppressed properties or property classes from the INPROG or APPRVE stage. During the REJECT stage, the system is configured to:

- Resume the Penalty Interest accruals as well as charge any fee or charge linked to the OL.

The system resumes the property classes and properties listed against REJECT Rule Status in Restructure Rules product condition. The effective date can be set up either as an Activity date or Suppress Date. So, penalty interest and charges accruals resume and can now accrue, either when activity LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*Reject is triggered or from Suppress Date which is the date on which inprog activity triggered. At this stage, the Original Loan goes back to the normal status as how it functioned before Restructuring.

While suppressing accruals is always from when restructure activity was initiated, the resuming of accruals can happen from the activity date of resume or from the suppression date.

In summary, based on the above setup, the technical loan booking is enabled at the APPRVE stage. On an original loan, the accruals of penalty interest and charges are stopped at the INPROG and APPRVE stage and are resumed at the REJECT stage. Top-ups and changes of the product are configured to be stopped at the INPROG and APPRVE stage. These are resumed at the REJECT stage.


##### Defining Restructure Activities

For each restructure code, the system creates a corresponding activity when Rebuild Activities at the Product Group level is set as Yes.

> **⚠️ Note:** The restructuring activities can be triggered back-dated or current-dated. Future-dated is not allowed.

Some key information on the restructuring activities are:

- The LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT Activity Class helps to record the activity log and perform restructuring. The activity includes the corresponding restructuring code to indicate the stage to restructure. For instance, LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*Inprog corresponds to the INPROG restructuring code.
- The Restructure activities can be triggered only on loans with current status (not for loans in pre-closure or closure).
- Before rejecting, if the user prefers to negotiate the effective date of resume of properties at the arrangement level, the LENDING-UPDATE-RESTRUCTURE.RULES activity is available, and this must be triggered before changing the restructure code to REJECT. This activity updates the Restructure Rules condition as per the user’s choice after which REJECT can be triggered.
- The Restructure activities can be reversed in the same sequence, that is, the latest Restructure activity has to be reversed first. If reversal of APPRVE activity has to take place, any TLs existing under the OL should be closed or terminated before triggering the reversal of the APPRVE restructure activity.


##### Configuring Periodic Attribute and Activity Restriction

The RESTRUCTURE.STATUS periodic attribute class available as a part of Activity Restriction Property Class, caters to deriving the restructuring status on the effective date of the activity. The bank can use this to restrict any commitment increase, change product, and so on based on the respective restructuring status on the OL.

The below screenshots show the periodic attribute configuration for Restructure status under Activity Restriction Property Class:

> **⚠️ Note:** The system does not default disabling or enabling the activities on the Original Loan based on the restructure code. As the combination of restrictions varies from bank to bank.

Using Activity Restriction and the respective periodic attribute, activities like increase commitment, change term, change product, rollover, disbursements, and so on, can be controlled on the original loan with different restructured status. The below screenshot shows the configuration to restrict the disbursement and change term amount activities once the arrangement is in INPROG and APPRVE status.

The setup below is to restrict disbursements and increase commitment at the INPROG and APPRVE stages:

When the arrangement is in INPROG or APPRVE status, the Activity Restriction Condition can be configured to restrict the increase in commitment amount and any further disbursements.

At the REJECT stage, the Activity Restriction Conditions are not configured, and hence the arrangement gets back to its original status where the other restructure rules don’t apply until further Restructure Activity is triggered.

> **⚠️ Note:** Some of the restricted functionality from the above-mentioned scenario may differ from bank to bank. Hence, these are available as configurations in Activity Restriction.


##### Memo-Enabled Property Class

For a technical loan, the user can attach the property of only memo-enabled property classes. The memo-enabled property classes are:

- Account
- Accounting
- Activity API
- Activity Mapping
- Activity Messaging
- Activity Presentation
- Alerts
- Balance Maintenance
- Closure
- Customer
- Interest
- Officers
- Overdue
- Payment Holiday
- Payment Rules
- Payment Schedule
- Payoff
- Settlement
- Statement
- Term Amount


##### Configuring Payments to OL and TL

Based on the terms and conditions between the bank and customer, the servicing and mapping of payments between the OL and the TLs are established. Accordingly, the payment allocation rules of the TL and OL are chosen by the bank for distributing the payments between both. Ideally, all repayments are applied to the TL first, then passed to the OL and applied there as well. The system raises an override when the repayment is made directly to the OL instead of the TL. The two approaches that the bank can use, based on the payment behavior between OL and TL are:

When the payments are applied to the TLs first and then passed to the OL, the banks have the following types of options possible:

- The banks require the same portions of payments applied to the TL to be applied to the OL per property (if a due amount for the respective property is in place). This is available when Allocate as per MI field is set to Yes. As per this set-up, the TL triggers the Apply Payment activity on the OL, since the same payment amounts per property need to be applied on the OL. If the respective property has no due portion in the OL or it is less than the repaid in the TL, the excess is applied based on the remainder activity maintained in the OL (that is, principal decrease or unallocated credit).

- The banks have not configured to settle the same portion of payment applied in TL to the OL, the repayment is apportioned based on the repayment rules in the OL.

- When the bank prefers a specific repayment rule to be applied to the restructured loan (the original loan that has undergone restructuring), the bank can configure it using the Restructure option in the Financial Status field.
- If the banks do not require a restructure-specific payment allocation rule to be used when the payment is passed from the TL to the OL, the payment coming from the TL is applied to the OL as per the OL’s own payment allocation rules.

Read Payment Rules Property Class for more information.

When the system should continue to allow payments to the OL, even after TLs have been booked under the respective OL, there are two types of options available:

- When the bank prefers a specific repayment rule to be applied on the restructured loan (the original loan that has undergone restructuring), it can configure it using the Restructure option in the Financial Status field.
- When the bank does not use a restructure-specific payment allocation rule, when the direct payment reaches the OL it is applied as per the OL own payment allocation rules. This payment does not affect the TL balances in any way.

Read Payment Rules Property Class for more information.


##### Accounting for Loan Restructuring

In compliance with the latest regulations, the OL arrangements are the ones that get reflected in the reporting and affect the Profit or Loss (PL) accounts of the banks. The TL arrangements are of memo nature, as they are supposed to be shadow loans that are accepting and reflecting, yet redirecting the payments to the OL arrangement, where the actual accounting takes place. The TLs are kept off-balance sheet. An example of booking of a TL and the corresponding balance update for the TLs are shown below:

| Activity | Action | CR | DR |
|---|---|---|---|
| NEW | ACCOUNT-DISBURSE |  | CURLOANACCOUNTINF |
| ACCRUE |  |  | ACCLOANINTERESTINF |

The above table shows that, when a new TL is created and disbursed, the outstanding balances are updated in CUR Balance INF which is CUR INF. When the interest accruals take place, the balances are updated in ACC INF. So, the accounting entries for the accruals are not posted to PL.

Since Term Amount balances are contingent in nature and memo balances are required to hold balances in INF and considering that no disbursement or change in term amount is allowed, it is decided not to maintain Term Amount balances for a TL. The system can be configured not to perform further disbursement or change the term amount in a restructured loan as per the Activity Restriction configuration.

For Term Amount Property Class, the system is configured such that, the Commitment property is used on a TL. The loan balances are visible through Account property only, as Commitment property is just used to input the respective term amount values. Increasing commitment and disbursing the same can be restricted through a configuration.

The Term Amount Property Class only has limited functionality, no accounting is generated on the same. From the below screenshot it is clear, that the Arrangement Activity page has Commitment property listed, whereas ECB has only the Account property.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Loan Restructuring functionality aims to initiate and maintain the end-to-end process of Court Order Restructuring (Forbearance, Standstill Agreements, and so on), using a separate loan arrangement of memo type, that is, Technical Loans (TLs). There are a variety of other restructuring approaches, which might not need an explicit booking of a memo loan arrangement. For example, a back value dated payment holiday can be declared for the missed repayments based on the bank’s decision. Read Payment Holiday for more information.


##### Debt Restructuring using Memo-type Loans

This section of the user guide deals with debt restructuring using memo-type loans.

The system provides the ability to initiate the restructuring process on the original loan (OL) on receipt of the related documents issued by the court. Based on the documentation provided, the user can trigger the corresponding restructure activity on the respective OL.

After triggering the restructure activity namely LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*Inprog, the restructure status is recorded in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS (and in the activity log). The details of restructure are updated on the OL Arrangement Overview page.

It is now possible to reflect the Court Order (or bank decision) in the system and maintain it in a separate memo type of a loan arrangement called Technical Loan (TL), which is created in parallel to the existing OL of the customer.

The OL can have multiple TLs booked under the master arrangement based on the business requirement. The OL overview page displays the list of all current TLs details linked to the OL. It is also possible that the single TL amount or the sum of different TL amounts could be more than the OL outstanding amount. The link between Master Loan and Technical loan(s) details can be viewed in AA.AARANGEMENT table in the Sub Arrangement field.

As the loan undergoes restructuring process accordingly, the suppression and resumption of properties at different stages of the OL are stored in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS . Based on the customer’s behaviour, the banks can also close the TL(s) and revert to the OL arrangement at any point in time.

An example of working of the OL and TLs during a restructure is summarised in the image below.

On triggering any of the restructuring activities in the OL, the system still allows the user to negotiate all its current parameters. Once a Restructure activity is triggered, the system allows negotiation of the following property classes:

- Interest
- Charge
- Activity Charges
- Periodic Charges
- Payment Schedule
- Settlement
- Account
- Activity Restrictions
- Payment Rules
- Restructure Rules
- Term Amount

When the OL undergoes restructuring, the different stages of the restructuring process are characterised by the restriction of different functionality such as increase of commitment amount, further disbursements, rollover, auto-settlement, recycler, and so on, being disabled or enabled based on the restructuring code and stage. As the combination configurations vary from bank to bank, the system does not default the disabling or enabling these activities based on the restructure code. This scenario is explained in the below table:

The life of a Technical Loan is explained in the below diagram:

Some features of the TL are:

- The TL is excluded from the Product Catalogue of the bank and is a default product only for loan restructuring. It is ensured using a dedicated flag which indicates whether the product is memo in nature, and is available at the product designer level.
- Term Amount balances are not maintained for the memo loans due to their contingent nature and the lack of need of actual disbursement, due to which top up or increase of commitment amount is also not applicable for TL.

- The system is configured such that the allocation priority in the TL can be different to the allocation priority in the OL, that is, the TL has its own payment allocation rules which define how the payments are applied to just the TL only.

- The TL must be released in the product that has Memo Enabled set to yes in the Product Designer.
- The TLs do not support restructuring themselves, that is, the Restructure Rules Property Class is not applicable for memo type of arrangements.
- The system does not allow the existence of TLs’ if the OL has been fully settled. Auto-Closure of the TLs is the default behavior of the system in such scenarios (read Closure for more information).
- It is not possible for the TL itself to be linked as a settlement or linked account or linked to a bundle.
- Automatic settlement as well as ageing is applicable for the TL products.
- The TLs are booked as un-secured loans due to their memo-type nature.
- Archival of the TLs is possible only when the OL has been fully settled and closed.


##### Loan Restructuring Process

The working of the OL and TL and the associated stages are explained in this section.

The INPROG (Read Restructuring Code table) code represents the restructuring code or status corresponding to the initial restructuring stage. Upon receiving the intimation of the court’s progress, the Restructure activity is triggered using LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*Inprog on the corresponding arrangement. As per the applicable configuration, the OL arrangement moves to INPROG status.

The INPROG Restructuring activity is reflected in the Activity Log on the loan Arrangement Overview page for the effective date. The information on suppressed properties is updated in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS .

> **⚠️ Note:** The INPROG activity can only be triggered back value dated or current value dated but cannot be future-dated.

The system is configured such that, the users cannot book memo loans under this status, as the Book Memo Loan field is not set for INPROG status. Read AA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS for more information. The restricted activities configured, remain restricted throughout the INPROG and APPRVE stages. Read Activity Restriction configuration for more information.

Consider a personal loan (original loan) created for USD 100,000, effective Jan 13, 2021, and the OL has due bills generated. The financial status of the arrangement is in a non-accrual basis which means, the customer has become insolvent for some reason during the period. The below screenshot shows the OL status before the Restructure activity got triggered.

The balances of the respective properties, before the Restructure activity initiation, can be seen using EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES.BALANCE:

Using the New Activity tab from the Arrangement Overview page or LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*Inprog activity, the INPROG Restructure activity is triggered on Mar 1, 2021. As per the applicable conditions, this means that the bank receives the Court Intimation Receipt on its process of reviewing the customer’s request for debt and circumstances. In the below screenshot, on approval of arrangement the restructure code becomes INPROG.

As per the applicable conditions, the penalty interest and charges are suppressed from the date the Restructure activity is initiated. Hence, the accrued penalty interest amount is reduced from USD 109.17 to USD 18.94 and stops further accrual from Mar 1, 2021. Charge property also is suppressed from the activity date. Read Restructure Rules Conditions for more information.

The AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS screenshot above shows the details of the properties that are suppressed from their effective date, March 1, 2021 (the activity date, the date on which Restructure activity gets triggered).

In the below screenshot, when the Increase Commitment activity is performed for the arrangement, the system validates the Activity Restriction conditions and raises an error stating that the requested activity is not allowed on the arrangement that is under restructure status. If Activity Restriction is not configured, the system does not restrict any activities to be performed on the OL. Read Activity Restriction Configuration for more information.

The INPROG to APPRVE (Read Restructuring Code table) restructuring code represents the restructuring stage during which the TL booking is made available. Once the restructure is approved by the court, it is triggered using LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*Apprve. The arrangement moves from INPROG to APPRVE status as per the applicable conditions.

The APPRVE restructuring activity is reflected in the Activity Log on the loan Arrangement Overview page for the effective date. The information on the suppressed properties is updated in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS . At the OL level, the TL reference is held in the Sub Arrangement field in AA.ARRANGEMENT .

> **⚠️ Note:** The APPRVE activity can only be triggered back value dated or current value dated.

At APPRVE status, the TLs are booked, as the Book Memo Loan field is marked as Yes. Read AA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS for more information. At the APPRVE stage, a new enquiry displays the icons for boo king or simulation of the TLs. A TL can be booked either back-dated, current-dated or future-dated using the Create Restructured Loan or Simulate Restructured Loan icons on the OL Arrangement Overview page. When the user chooses to create a restructured loan, all the TL parameters are updated as per the Court Order received or as per the bank’s decision.

The restricted activities configured, remain restricted throughout the INPROG and APPRVE stages. Read Activity Restriction configuration for more information.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Pay-out settlement instructions are not mandatory for the TLs. Technical Loans are automatically disbursed when created. There is no need for manual disbursement. An event type ACCOUNT-DISBURSE-DUE-INF is in place with the help of which the CUR INF balances are updated automatically without contra target.

Consider a personal loan (original loan) created for USD 100,000 effective on Jan 13,2021 and is in INPROG status. Using the New Activity tab from the Arrangement Overview page or LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*Apprve activity, the APPRVE Restructure activity is triggered on Mar 10, 2021. As per the applicable conditions, this means that the bank receives the Court Order on approval for restructuring and the debt can be restructured as per the Court Decision.

From the below screenshot, on approval of the arrangement, the restructure code moves to APPRVE. Once this stage is reached, the enquiry to create or simulate a restructured loan (Technical Loan – TL) appears.

Using the Create Restructured Loan icon, the TLs are created which in turn appear under the Technical Loan Arrangements tab on the Arrangement Overview page. These can be viewed further using the drill-down option for technical loan details.

Here, a TL for USD 90,000 is created for 1Y, effective Mar 10, 2021. Due bills are generated for the principal interest component. As per the applicable conditions only limited property classes are supported for a TL. Read Memo Enabled Property Class for more information.

.

For an OL, as per the setup, the Penalty Interest property and Charge property class are suppressed. This implies, that the bills are not accrued from the activity date. The master loan details are reflected on the TL Overview page.

The above screenshot AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS show the details of the properties that are suppressed, under APPRVE status on the OL. Read Restructure Rules Conditions for more information.

The memo enabled loans have their balances placed under a balance suffix called INF. The screenshot below shows that outstanding due balances are placed under the applicable properties INF balance as per the setup.

> **⚠️ Note:** Reversing an OL arrangement status from INPROG, APPRVE or REJECT to Null, is not allowed once TLs are booked.

When a user prefers to reverse the restructure, the TLs should be closed, and the activities should be reversed in the latest-first order.

The INPROG/APPRVE to REJECT (Read the Restructuring Code table) restructuring code represents that the customer petition for restructuring is rejected by the court.

REJECT is triggered using the LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*Reject activity at the INPROG/APPRVE stage of the arrangement. The arrangement moves from INPROG/APPRVE to REJECT status as per the applicable conditions set. In case of Reject activity triggered from APPRVE to REJECT, a validation is in place such that, any linked TLs must be manually closed before rejecting. TLs cannot be booked under REJECT status, as the Book Memo Loan field is not set to YES for this restructuring stage. Read AA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS for more information.

The REJECT Restructuring activity is reflected in the Activity Log on the loan Arrangement Overview page for the effective date. The information on resumed properties are updated in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS .

> **⚠️ Note:** The INPROG/APPRVE to REJECT activity can only be triggered back value dated or current value dated.

The Activity Restriction configuration is not applied on the REJECT status. Hence the arrangement gets back to the normal status where increase commitment, change product, and other such activities can take place effectively as per the conditions set. Read Activity Restriction configuration for more information.

For any migrated contracts for which the SUPPRESS or RESUME related activity has commenced in the legacy system, a record of the respective dates is not available. The Retrospective Resume can take place only backwards from the date of migration. If the migration of the TLs is back-dated, the Retrospective Resume from the actual date of suppression is possible.

Consider a personal loan of USD 200,000 which is in APPRVE stage. Using the New Activity tab from Arrangement Overview page or the LENDING-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT*Reject activity is triggered. Validation is in place in case there are live TLs already available for the OL, all the linked TLs should be closed manually before rejecting the restructure. In the below screenshot this is evident:

The arrangement’s restructure status is changed from APPRVE to REJECT where original conditions are applied as before the Restructure was triggered.

The above screenshot of AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS shows the details of the properties that are resumed, under the REJECT status as per the effective date (suppression date in this case). Reject is triggered on Feb 1, 2022 and Resume action is effective from 25 Jan, 2022, as the suppression is triggered earlier on Jan 25, 2022. Read Memo Enabled Property Class for more information.


##### Payments to OL and TL

The system responds in two ways during the payments’ distribution between the TL and the OL. The banks can choose from any of the following options:

- Approach 1 - The system should continue to allow direct payments to the OL, even after the TLs’ are booked under the respective OL.
- Approach 2 - The system should restrict direct payments to the OL and ensure that the payments always go through the TL first (once such is booked).

To facilitate this, an override AA-ARR.DIRECT.PAYMENT.NOT.ALLOWED is raised when a payment is made directly to the OL. This can be configured as Type error to stop the direct payment.

In this illustration, a payment rule is configured where the payment between OL and TL are not mapped property-specific, that is, the Allocate As Per Ml field is set as Null whereas, payments to OL are directed from the TL. The funds are apportioned based on the due bills generated on the OL. Since the TL is a mirror account, a payment to TL only shows the movement of funds and not actually recorded in the financial records.

OL and TL before payments are,

A payment of USD 30,000 is made against the TL, effective Apr 14, 2021.

The screenshot above shows that the funds movement, out of USD 30,000 the bills are apportioned accordingly on the TL:

- The due principal interest of USD 193.66 is settled
- The delinquent principal outstanding of USD 7410.21 is settled
- Remaining excess amount of USD 22,396.13 is credited to UNC (unallocated credit – Overpayment on TL)

The same payment of USD 30,000 is applied on the OL which is directed from TL and allocated as per the original loan payment rules.

OL after payment is,

In the above screenshot the outstanding dues are settled. Out of USD 30,000 the bills are apportioned as per the Payment Rules conditions of the current loan:

- The principal interest of USD 622.64 is settled
- Principal outstanding of USD 12,222.25 is settled
- Due portion of the accrued penalty interest of USD 18.94 is settled
- Remaining excess amount of USD 17,036.17 is applied as principal decrease, hence reducing the outstanding total principal to USD 70,741.58

The payments are apportioned as per the Payment Rules configured for the OL.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Allocate as per Ml field is set as Yes, then the system only settles the principal outstanding bill and principal interest bill on both the TL and OL with the same portion of outstanding bills on TL, as only these properties’ bills are outstanding on the TL. The excess payment on OL in this case is applied as a remainder amount and applied either as UNC or principal decrease, as per the applicable payment rule set up.

Consider an OL with a principal outstanding of USD 70741.58 and the corresponding TL has a principal outstanding of USD 82589.79. When the customers choose to directly make payments toward the OL without being directed from the TL, a validation is in place to notify the same.

The OL and TL prior to payments are,

A payment of USD 5,000 is made against the OL.

In the Arrangement Overview page, it is applied as principal decrease and the corresponding principal outstanding is reduced by USD 5,000 as per the payment rules.

The principal outstanding balance is reduced from USD 70741.58 to USD 65741.58 as there is no other due on the contract. Whereas the overview of TL remains the same. The screenshot below shows that the balances remain unaffected.

An overpayment can occur in the following two scenarios:

- The amount repaid to the TL exceeds the due bill(s) on the TL. There might be components outstanding in the OL that are settled in the overpayment made to the TL.
- When the amount repaid to the TL exceeds the due bill(s) on the TL and the corresponding OL is fully settled and pending for closure, then the payment is passed only to the OL as an unallocated credit. In such instances closure of the OL is not possible until the OL unallocated credit is cleared.

Read Approach 1 Illustration for overpayment on OL and TL.


##### Closure of OL and TL

When the OL outstanding balances reach zero, the system checks for any outstanding TLs under the respective OL.

- If there are no underlying TLs, the closure of the OL is processed as per the product set-up.
- If there are underlying TLs, the system checks for the set up in the Auto Terminate ML in AA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS : If Auto Terminate ML is set to yes, the system triggers an automatic write-off of the remaining TLs’ balances and this TL is closed based on the closure condition. If there is no specific closure setup, then the TL is closed during COB. After the balances are cleared in the OL, the OL is closed based on the closure condition. If Auto Terminate ML is not set, the user should manually close the TL though the OL is closed due to a payment in the OL (as per closure setup in OL).

Read Closure Property Class for more information.

Archival of the respective underlying TLs should not be possible until the OL is closed.

The OL can be closed using the Payoff or Write off activities. For the loan shown below, the Payoff activity is triggered. Once the payoff bill is settled with the outstanding dues, the arrangement moves to Pending Closure status and the balances become zero.

When the arrangement is in Pending Closure status, only Close Arrangement activity is allowed. In this case, when the Reject activity is triggered, the system validates and further Reject Restructure activity is restricted.

During COB, as per the Closure Property condition of the OL, the Close Arrangement activity is scheduled and triggered. The arrangement moves to Closed status.

The TL is automatically closed during the same COB based on the Auto Terminate ML field which is set as Yes (closure condition is honored).

- During COB, the system checks whether the OL balances are zero.
- Once it is validated, the Write-off activity is triggered on the TL, making the TL balances zero. Based on the closure conditions of the TL, the Close Arrangement activity is scheduled and triggered.
- The arrangement is moved to Closed status.


##### Write-off of TL

When the OL in APPRVE status is moved to REJECT status, the user may prefer to payoff the TL loan under the OL. The system helps to manually trigger the write-off of the TLs. If for any reason the OL is already closed, the write-off is the only activity allowed on the TLs at that point of time.

To close a TL, in the below screenshot, a write-off is manually triggered on the TL on Mar 31, 2022. All the loan balances become zero and the arrangement moves to Pending Closure status.

The loan balances become zero when the write-off is triggered.

If the master arrangement is still live, when the Close Arrangement activity is triggered on the TL, validation is in place such that the closure of TL is allowed only after the closure of the master loan.

In the below arrangement, the OL is first closed by triggering the payoff. The Close Arrangement activity is triggered on the TL using LENDING-CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT. The TL arrangement is now closed manually.


##### Migrated Contracts

Any loans for which restructuring is initiated in the legacy system should be appropriately migrated based on the respective restructuring stage in the legacy system. The following sequence of activities have to be followed to capture the restructuring code on the migrated contracts:

1. TAKEOVER
2. CAPTURE BALANCE
3. RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT , where CODE stands for the latest restructure code in the legacy system.

When the TLs are created using the Takeover activity, the CUR INF balances must be updated using the Capture Balance activity.

It is imperative to perform the Restructure activity corresponding to the latest restructure code which the migrated contracts have in the legacy system, as the Restructure activity indicates, if there is a property that is suppressed or resumed.

If REJECT restructure activity needs to be triggered for an already migrated loan in the system and the suppression date resides in the legacy system, then the properties specified to be resumed on triggering REJECT (that is, on triggering the respective resume-initiating activity), is resumed as on the Activity Date that is, REJECT date.

During a Reject activity for any migrated contracts, the SUPPRESS or RESUME related activity commences in the legacy system, a record of the respective dates is not available. As such the Retrospective Resume can take place only back from the date of migration. If the migration of the TLs is back-dated, the Retrospective Resume from the actual date of suppression is possible.

Read Migration of Lending Arrangements for more information.

#### 📖 Introduction

Existing contracts are most likely to be present when the Temenos' system replaces the existing legacy system. Therefore, these contracts need to be transferred to our system, which is referred as Takeover.

As the situation at each new implementation is different, a general approach is adopted when planning and executing the takeover of existing retail loans into the retail lending product line. Read the Working with section for more information.

When the user migrates a loan through a front-end API, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in the TBC to complete the migration process. During takeover, the user can update the details of the limit associated with the loan using the limit condition.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Takeover of live contracts uses the Balance Maintenance Property Class. For more information on configuration, read the Balance Maintenance Property Class.

During the migration of data from the legacy system to Temenos' system, it is possible to improve the performance of the takeover process by updating certain AA tables through a background service. Read Customer Arrangement Offline Update for more information.


##### Migration Consideration for Advance Payment Setup

The following are some migration scenarios for advance payments.


###### Bills Issued In Advance

During the migration of a loan contract from legacy system to AA, it is possible that the loan product has a facility to settle the bills in advance.

For loans that have the bills generated in advance but are not yet settled, the Temenos' system allows the takeover of the bill in the issued status (that is, the bill is made due during the advance repayment or the bill due date). To accommodate this, the capture bill activity allows bill date/issue date to be back dated and settle date/due date to be future dated.

It is possible to takeover a bill in Issued status only when Bill Produced field is set and the advance payment feature is enabled for the loan contract.


###### Bills Issued and Settled In Advance

The following section describes scenarios in advance payments for bills issued and settled in advance.


##### Scenario 1: Advance Payment Benefit from both Principal and Interest Paid In Advance

For loans that have the bills generated in advance but are already settled, during the takeover:

- The principal outstanding is the remaining balance after the bill is settled in advance.
- The accruals from the advance settlement date till the takeover date are captured.
- The next due date is updated explicitly in the system, so that AA doesn’t generate another bill (since it has already been settled).

If the bill for a conventional loan is settled in advance, before the due date, then the interest period is cycled to the next due date of the bill during takeover. Thus, the system starts accruing interest on the principal balance after the last advance payment. The next bill is generated as per the configuration, that is, based on the next due date and the number of days mentioned in the advance payment setup.


##### Scenario 2: Advance Payment with Customer Benefit (Only from Principal)

Consider a conventional loan product with the following configuration:

- Advance Payment is set as FULL.
- Advance Payment Restriction set as BILLED (as part of recommended setup).
- Settle Unearned Interest set as YES.

It has an advance bill which is taken over as a settled bill (that is, the bill is issued in advance and settled prior to the due date), the interest accrual for that period is a positive balance considering the interest accruals paid in advance. In this case, the user has to trigger a Capture Balance activity to capture and store the accrued interest as a positive balance.

The user can also trigger the Adjust Balance activity to adjust the interest accruals to a positive amount during takeover.

The above-mentioned configuration is the recommended setup for advance payment with interest benefit for customer only from the principal amount paid in advance. With this setup, the customer can pay only the issued bill in advance.

- Takeover of interest accruals (that is, ACC ) as a positive balance can be made possible only when Settle Unearned Interest is set to YES.
- If Settle Unearned Interest is set for a conventional loan, then the Advance Payment field can only be set to FULL. Else, the system raises proofing errors.
- When a bill is issued in advance, then it is considered as a current bill. For example, if the bank has set Advance Payment Restriction to 1 and the loan has bill a (invoiced to the customer) in advance, then the customer can settle the issued bill and one more bill in advance.


##### Scenario 3: Advance Payment with no Customer Benefit

During an upgrade or migration, the product can be configured with an advance payment rule. The Advance Payment Rule should have the payment rule type setup with Advance Settle Date (ADVANCE.SETTLE.DATE) set as DUE. This ensures that no benefit is passed to the customer for any advance payment. If the loan has any advance payments in the legacy system, then the advance payments should be triggered after the takeover activity .

During the takeover activity, the user closes the legacy contracts and moves the accrued balances to a control account. The balance under the advance payment is also moved to the control account and the outstanding principal and the accruals till date are captured. In this scenario the sequence of steps involved during migration are:

- Take over contract
- Capture principal balance
- Capture accruals

Similar to accruals, the advance payment is also moved from the legacy system to Temenos' system.

- Once the takeover is completed, the user must trigger a capture balance to capture the ADV balance. Now, the user can see the Forward Apply Payment activities triggered by the system to settle the bills for the respective future date.

When the system moves to the actual due date, it is evident that the settlement process is suppressed as the bill is already settled. The system clears the DUE , DUE and DUE effective on the bill due date with the advance balance type. If the advance payment has a principal repayment component, the system updates the GL only on the due date of the bill for the reduced CUR .

In TBC, during the takeover of a loan that has an advance payment processed for an upcoming instalment, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting and balance updates.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the migration of lending arrangements.


##### General Approach

The following general approach is recommended:

- Analyse existing products and create equivalent products using the AL module.
- Determine requirements for historic data in Temenos' system.
- Prepare extract of legacy loan contract data and balances.
- Create new arrangements from the legacy loan contract data.
- Create the outstanding legacy bills.
- Update the penalty balances.

To takeover legacy loans to AL, the following activities must already have taken place before creating the arrangements:

Each loan arrangement has to be linked to a customer in the CUSTOMER application. Every loan has to be captured in the Temenos' Lending module to ensure that the associated client data is made available in our system and the legacy loan data can be associated with the customer number in the Temenos' system.

In TBC, during migration of a loan contract, the information related to owners and other parties can be input from an external system such as Party TBC. The system evaluates this customer information against the records found in the external system.

For each customer in a loan arrangement, a corresponding LIMIT record is created in our system before creating the arrangement.

In TBC, during the takeover of a loan, the user can update the sanctioned limit amount for the loan using the Limit Id field in the Limit condition.

A loan can be a long-term contract in the legacy system, which can be ongoing for several years. The usual practice for the takeover of financial contracts is for the contract to be takeover to take place with an effective date that is equal to a scheduled date (for example, interest or principal due date).

The contract is created with principal balance and interest rates at the selected event date as a new contract. Interest rate and principal changes after the event date are loaded into our system as future-dated activities. Details of previous history and balances are not used in the contract processing in our system.

The date chosen can be the last payment date, which can be a past date.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is possible to takeover a contract in the middle of an interest period, but this adds additional complexity to the process. Interest calculations are split in the two systems with associated profit and loss being accrued partly in the legacy system and Temenos' system.

Existing contracts are analysed to identify the earliest date that can be used to create an arrangement.

The existing products in the legacy system has to be analysed and products have to be created for the Lending Product Line that provides the same functionality.

The legacy system is unlikely to provide functionality in exactly the same way as Temenos' system and data may not map directly from the legacy system to our system.

Properties, Product Property Conditions and Products have to be created with an effective date that is on or earlier than the earliest contract date for takeover identified in the legacy data.

Products have to be published, including any known future conditions and made available for sale before arrangements can be created.

It is unlikely that the legacy system has the concepts of product inheritance and negotiable attributes as our system so the legacy products are likely to be supported best by:

- Not using any inheritance in the product structure.
- Making the majority of attributes negotiable for arrangements.

In TBC, the loan contracts are migrated to products which are designed and defined using a product management system like the TPM (Temenos Product Manager).

The AA module supports the ability to record arrangement level conditions for information purposes only. Once the arrangement is created, it is possible to load historic conditions if required. Any data loaded prior to the creation date in our system are not used for processing and is not a mandatory requirement.

Temenos' system cannot process the adjustment to loan contracts with an effective date prior to the takeover date. The usual approach is to make the amendment in the legacy system if still available, or manually calculate the adjustment. The adjustment can then be applied to the arrangement in our system effective the takeover date.

The value of outstanding bills have to be taken over into Temenos' system with an effective date equal to the start date of the arrangement in our system or the takeover date. Data has to be made available for overdue bills.

The value of penalty interest and charges calculated (accrued) by the legacy system has to be made available at the takeover date (that is, effective date of arrangement creation in our system). It provides the ability to take these balances over.

The following data should be made available (or be able to be derived) in Temenos' system:

- Customer number.
- Product name.
- Effective Date for the takeover of the contract.
- Currency of Arrangement.
- Outstanding principal balance as at the Effective Date.

> **⚠️ Note:** A possible scenario is that a contract that has passed its maturity date in the legacy system but has outstanding bills and has a current principal of zero at the effective date of takeover.

A separate extract of overdue bills for existing arrangements has to be prepared. It includes,

- The bill due date.
- The breakdown of properties and outstanding amount for the bill.
- A legacy contract identifier that should be possible to link to the created arrangement number after takeover.

Any outstanding penalty interest or charge accrual balances for loans should be prepared and should identify

- The Property name (for example, PENALTYINT)
- The balance amount for the Property.

During migration or takeover activity the TAKEOVER.CASHFLOW-REPORTING Cashflow type activity class allows the user to specify the EIR or carry cost which is handed off to the Cashflow engine.

Read Capturing EIR/AMC during Migration in Reporting Property Class for further information.

- It is possible to configure the reporting condition to hand off the required information to an external system for calculating the annual percentage rate for loans in TBC. The TBC generates a business event to hand off the cashflows to an external system for further processing to take place. All other features related to Reporting condition are not applicable for TBC.
- The features pertaining to EIR as well as AMC are not applicable for loans in TBC and can be enabled using external solutions.

The following section describes the methods used in triggering TAKEOVER CASH FLOW REPORTING Activity

###### Takeover Sequence

The following section describes the takeover sequence in detail.


###### Takeover process – AA Contract with Reporting PC (in IFRS standard)

This process is for existing bank with AA loans & IFRS reporting in their system but switching to FASB standards (from IFRS).

1. Update Reporting condition for the loan product.
2. Proof and Publish the product.
3. Trigger IFRS activity.
4. Update EIR or AMC as required and commit.
5. EB Cashflow gets updated.


###### Takeover process – AA Contract without Reporting PC (without IFRS standard)

This process is for existing bank with AA loans without IFRS module initially but later comply.

1. Add Reporting condition for the loan product.
2. Proof and Publish the product.
3. Trigger IFRS activity.
4. Update EIR or AMC as required and commit.
5. EB Cashflow gets updated.


###### Full Takeover from legacy (Non AA, Non IFRS case)

This process involves migration of loans from legacy system into Temenos' solution with AA & IFRS functionality.

1. Create Loan product with Reporting condition
2. Complete loan Takeover sequence to migrate the outstanding loan bills and balances.
3. Trigger IFRS activity.
4. Update EIR or AMC as required and commit.
5. EB Cashflow gets updated.

### 1.38  Migration RFR LIBOR


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *There is a business need for banks to be able to identify the contracts that would require a rate change to Risk Free Rates (RFR)s and migrate them away from LIBOR.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARR.INTEREST`, `AA.INTEREST.DETAILS`, `RFR.CONDITION`, `RFR.MIGRATION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Application Field Name*, *Application Field Name, Field Operand, and Value From, Value To definition*, *Application Field Name.*, *Application Name*, *Context Name Value*, *Dflt Delta Spread*, *Dflt RFR PI Key*, *Exc Field Operation* ... +32 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

There is a business need for banks to be able to identify the contracts that would require a rate change to Risk Free Rates (RFR)s and migrate them away from LIBOR.

The automated migration tool assists the banks to have capabilities to validate multiple contracts in one selection and convert from (L)IBOR to RFRs in one go. This tool helps in identifying the live contracts that are linked to IBOR rates based on the user selection criteria that will be eligible for conversion and convert them successfully.

The features related to Migration of LIBOR Lending Contracts to Risk Free Rates are not applicable for loans in TBC. Read Introduction to TBC for Lending for more information about TBC for loans.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The conversion from a (L)IBOR contract to a Risk Free Rates (RFR) contract cannot happen mid interest period and the recommendation is to complete the task on the current interest capitalization point.

The migration conversion process is handled by the following applications and service.

- RFR.MIGRATION
- RFR.CONDITION
- RFR.MIGRATION.DETAILS
- Service – RFR.MIGRATION.SERVICE

The migration process itself is performed as two-step processing.

- Preview Mode – To update the migration related tables with the expected changes for eligible contracts.
- Execute Mode – To carry out the actual migration to update the LIVE contacts with new RFR fields and details.


##### RFR.MIGRATION

The basic selection criteria for migration with respect to application and the logistics (like version for conversion) is defined to select the list of contracts that require conversion from (L)IBOR to RFR.

The RFR.MIGRATION table has the following attributes and accepts the appropriate values to it. The records are selected for conversion based on the configuration given in this table. The record ID for this table is a free text field and the user can create one with any alphanumerical value.

- GB Description – Indicates the description of the record.
- Application Name – Indicates the application name or product name that records for conversion belong to.

- IBOR Cut Off Date – Indicates the IBOR discontinuation date.Mandatory input
- Version Name – Indicates the valid version of application to be used for migration process by the OFS Routine.
- OFS Routine – Indicates the API to perform the RFR migration.

> **⚠️ Note:** Currently only AA.PERFORM.RFR.MIGRATION is accepted

- Mode – To identify the process stage of the migration. Preview – Indicates the verification process and does not update the contract at this stage. Execute – Indicates that actual contract update is carried out.
- Int Period End Date – Indicates the interest period end date of the contract. Valid Date – Indicates that the migration API would identify the contracts that are greater than or equal to this date and the next working date. Blank – Indicates that the migration API would identify all the contracts that are eligible for migration with respect to other conditions.
- Application Field Name – Indicates the field name from the application to be used as a selection.
- Field Operand – Indicates the operation to be performed on the field during the evaluation of the contract between the selections. Values allowed are EQ; GE; GT; LE; LK; LT; NE; NR; RG Mandatory input for the field operand RG
- Value From – Indicates the value to be verified from the application or product with respect to Application Field Name.
- Value To – Indicates the value to be verified upto, from the application or product with respect to Application Field Name.
- Routine Name – Indicates the user-defined API that can be attached to this field to get the list of arrangements to perform the migration.

> **⚠️ Note:** Conditions defined ( Application Field Name, Field Operand, and Value From, Value To definition ) and Routine Name attributes are mutually exclusive.

This record can be viewed and amended in RFR.MIGRATION.LIST enquiry.

Sample version that can be attached to RFR.MIGRATION is shown below.


##### RFR.CONDITION

The RFR.CONDITION table is used to define the exclude contract conditions and include the new Periodic Interest key and the adjustment spread information with respect to RFR. The record of this table must be a valid AA product. The following attributes conditions are defined.

- GB Description – Indicates the description of the record
- Exclude Application Field – Defines exclude condition after the selection of records based on selection definition in RFR.MIGRATION .

To exclude contracts with PERIODIC.INDEX value as ‘01’ from Interest Property Class.

> **⚠️ Note:** The field name could be any valid field from any of the Property class of the arrangement.

- Exc Fld Operand – Defines the Operand for selection. The values allowed are EQ, NE, LT,GT, etc.
- Exc Value From – Defines the field value for the Exclude Application field.
- Exc Value To – Defines the field value range that would be excluded from the migration process.
- Exc Field Operation – Indicates the operation to be used when more than one condition exists. Mandatory input when multiple conditions are to be processed together.
- Dflt RFR PI Key – When none of the conditions are satisfied, this default key value is used for conversion
- Dflt Delta Spread - When none of the conditions are satisfied, this default spread value is used as adjustment spread for conversion. The spread value can be input along with ‘+’ or ‘-‘sign and is considered as Margin Operand .
- RFR PI Key – When the conditions are satisfied, this value is used as RFR Key for contracts in conversion.
- RFR Delta Spread - When the conditions are satisfied, this value is used for conversion. The spread value can be input along with ‘+’ or ‘-‘sign and would be considered as Margin Operand . This spread value is added or subtracted to the Margin Rate.
- RFR Int Property – Identifies the Multiple Interest Property .

> **⚠️ Note:** If same RFR PERIODIC.INTEREST key is used for multiple Interest properties, will still need to define all the properties separately.

- Application Field Name – Specifies Valid name from any of the property class that is part of the arrangement.

To exclude contracts with PERIODIC.INDEX value as ‘20’ from Interest Property Class.

- Field Operand – Indicates the operand to be used while selecting the data from the Application Field Name.
- Value From – Indicates the value to be verified against the field value of the application during the evaluation of the contract.
- Value To - Defines the range of the field value

- Field Operation – Defines the operation to be performed when multiple conditions are defined. Options – And; OR This record can be viewed and amended in RFR.CONDITION.LIST enquiry.


##### RFR.MIGRATION.DETAILS

Migration contract information is recorded in this table while processing data, based on the selection criteria of include and exclude conditions defined in RFR.MIGRATION and RFR.CONDITION .

The applicable ID to this table updated by the system are:

- @ID: RFR.MIGRATION table ID – Preview
- @ID: RFR.MIGRATION table ID – Execute

Launch the RFR.MIGRATION table in preview mode to initiate migration and this updates the RFR.MIGRATION.DETAILS table with selected data and ID as Rfr Migration Id-Preview.

The migration check can be run multiple times in preview-mode for verification without impacting the underlying contracts.The selection validates the following conditions.

- Contract is linked to Periodic Interest Key
- Contract Maturity Date is greater than the IBOR Cut-off Date and the current Inte Period End Date
- Contracts that satisfied the Exclude conditions has Exclusion Flag set as ‘Yes’ in RFR.MIGRATION.DETAILS table
- Contracts that satisfy conditions other than the exclude conditions are assigned with values from RFR PI Key and RFR Delta Spread
- Contracts with none of the conditions satisfied are assigned with Dflt RFR PI Key and Dflt Delta Spread .

RFR.MIGRATION.SERVICE should be started from TSA.SERVICE after defining the selection criteria.

The service API updates the RFR.MIGRATION.DETAILS as below.

The selection can be viewed using the MIGRATION.DETAILS enquiry for PREVIEW mode.

Preview mode of RFR Migration Process – Flow Diagram

Execute mode should be triggered only after the verification of the results from the preview mode.

> **⚠️ Note:** This mode is applicable only for the Interest period end date and the inbuilt intelligence ensures that the mode is triggered only once.

Launch RFR.MIGRATION again in Execute mode, after thorough verification of results from preview mode. Upon authorization, the data with ID as ‘-Preview’ is selected from RFR.MIGRATION.DETAILS .The execute mode runs the following eligibility check again to ensure integrity of data:

- Contract is linked to Periodic Interest Key
- Contract Maturity Date is greater than the IBOR Cut-off Date and the current Int Period End Date.
- Contracts that satisfied the Exclude conditions has Exclusion Flag set as ‘Yes’ in RFR.MIGRATION.DETAILS table
- Contracts that satisfy conditions other than the Exclude conditions are assigned with values from RFR PI Key and RFR Spread
- Contracts with none of the conditions satisfied are assigned with Dflt RFR PI Key and Dflt Delta Spread .

The Migration API updates the RFR.MIGRATION.DETAILS with id as ‘Rfr Migration id-Execute’. The OFS responses for each migrated contract are recorded in the details table for verification and reconciliation purpose.

RFR.MIGRATION.SERVICE should be started from TSA.SERVICE after defining the selection criteria.

The API updates the eligible contract by triggering Change-Interest Activity and also the execution results to the migration details table along with migration status.

> **⚠️ Note:** For contracts having multiple Interest properties have multiple respective change Interest activity triggered for the properties.

OFS Error messages if any at the time of posting the records are captured in the Migration Status attribute and otherwise Success.

Successful Migration is updated as below.

The Contract list can be viewed using MIGRATION.DETAILS enquiry and MIGRATION.OFS.STATUS for EXECUTE mode

Execute mode of RFR Migration Process - Flow diagram


##### Migration Types

The migration is possible only for the scheduled Interest properties on the capitalisation date. There are two types of migrations possible by using the migration tool.

- Current dated migration – The migration happens on the capitalisation date set as TODAY
- Future dated migration – The migration happens on capitalisation date set as a Future date.

> **⚠️ Note:** Back dated migration is currently restricted and not possible to perform by using RFR.MIGRATION .

The current dated migration is when Int Period End Date or the capitalisation date for the given interest period is set as TODAY.

The below screen shot is example for the current dated migration where the Int Period End Date and the Current system date are the same. Based on this definition the system selects the list of arrangements whose current period end date is 15-April-2021 and posts the OFS message to convert the LIBOR to RFR.

The Future dated migration is when the Int Period End Date or the capitalisation date is a future date and not a business date. The below screen shot is example for the future dated migration where the Int Period End Date is greater than the current system date.

Base on this definition the system selects the list of arrangements whose current period end date is 19-April-2021. The LENDING -RFR.MIGRATION-INTEREST is scheduled for the Int Period End Date and is triggered during the COB for conversion.

> **⚠️ Note:** Changes executed through auto-migration cannot be rolled back and should be handled manually. Due to the fact that all RFR interest properties should be scheduled in the payment schedule definition, both Principal Interest Property and Penalty Interest Property should have same payment frequency. Interest properties with the type Accrue by Bills cannot be migrated to new RFR rates. Penalty interest property condition with open period and no schedule definitions cannot be migrated using the auto-migration tool and should be handled manually. Multi-Tiers with different Interest types like Floating, Fixed and Periodic cannot be migrated using migration tool. Back dated migration cannot be performed using the auto migration tool. Arrangements with OVERDUE balances cannot be migrated using the auto-migration tool and should be migrated manually.
