##### Impact of Change Schedule in Payment Holiday

When the bank/FIIs defines the Repay Period as Deferred, the holiday interest linked to Payment Type or Bill Type gets deferred for the specified period as mentioned in the Repay Period . At the end of holiday period, the system generates a holiday interest payment type automatically for the holiday interest balances associated with the loan and schedule the holiday interest Payment Type by mirroring the schedule associated with the Interest Property in the Payment Type or Bill Type (as defined during UPDATE-PAYMENT.HOLIDAY Activity). Read Payment Type for Holiday Interest for more information.

Once the Payment Holiday is defined, any change in the schedule (frequency change, bill type change, payment type change, start/end dates), cancels or voids all the future Payment Holiday defined (cancels the existing payment holiday). That is, if an arrangement is in a Payment Holiday Period or has defined a Payment Holiday Period for a future date, the change in schedule cancels all the payment holidays from the date of change of schedule.

An override is raised by the system for modification in the schedule of loan carrying Payment Holiday or having a future date Payment Holiday. Fresh holiday instructions need to be declared, if necessary for additional bills.

> **⚠️ Note:** The change in schedule affects the Payment Holiday, irrespective of the usage of the Repay Type field, while defining the Payment Holiday.

For example, during a payment holiday, if the user tries to change the future schedule dates of the loan, then the existing payment holiday from the current date is cancelled by the system and user should request a fresh payment holiday for the recent holiday.

The same holds good when there is payment holiday scheduled in future and the payment schedule is changed prior to that scheduled payment holiday.

A mortgage arrangement of USD 300,000 for 25 years, is opened and disbursed as on Apr 15, 2021. Repayment is set as monthly, and Payment Type set as Constant.

As per the customer request, the bank/FIIs applied for a Payment Holiday, from May to Sep. Now the customer requests a change in the repayment schedule of the arrangement from monthly to bi-weekly, before the payment holiday gets exhausted. This results in raising an override stating 'Change in payment schedule will ignore payment holiday requests if available' and there by makes all the existing Payment Holiday defined as void.


##### Payment Holiday Dates

The following section describes backdated and future dated payment holidays with illustrations.


###### Back Dated Payment Holidays

When a customer is unable to repay his loan and has missed few installments, it is possible that the bank declares those missed installments as payment holidays and restructures the loan. In this scenario, the holiday start date cannot be less than the Activity effective date. For the holiday start to be backdated, the Activity has to be run backdated. This means that, the bank or FIIs can provide a Back Dated Payment Holiday, if the LENDING-UPDATE-PAYMENT.HOLIDAY activity is also back dated.

Consider a mortgage that is in NAB status due to outstanding bills.

Now the customer approaches the bank/FII requesting for a back dated payment holiday, from Feb 1, 2022 to May 1, 2022 and the same gets approved. Accordingly, bank/FIIs agrees for the same.

After the payment holiday is declared, the customer does not miss any payment and his overdue status is reassessed based on the new schedule. The loan is not in NAB status after this restructure of declaring a back value dated payment holiday.


###### Future Dated Payment Holiday

If the start date is in the future, then the base date for holiday payment calculation, is the previous payment date of the holiday start date.


##### Amending Payment Holiday

Payment holiday definition can be reversed, by reversing the actual activity. Any amendments to the existing holiday payments definition can be made by using the CHANGE-PAYMENT.HOLIDAY activity. This functionality helps the bank/FIIs to modify or cancel an already defined Payment Holiday.


##### Payment Holiday Limit

Payment Holiday Limits allow the bank/FIIs to provide flexible payment or payment holiday options to the customer, by either reducing the repayment amount or by skipping the same, upto a defined limit agreed by the bank/FIIs and the customer. The Payment Holiday limit can be defined by configuring the Payment Schedule Condition as explained in Payment Holiday Limit.

When the repayment obligation is reduced or skipped for a customer, the system compares the amount reduced from the original repayment and with that of the available payment limit defined. An error or an override can be defined, if the limit is breached as per the banks/FIIs convenience.

There can be situations, when the schedule payment amount may change due to changes in rate of interest, term or cancelling the declared holiday in the loan. In such circumstances, the system automatically updates the Payment Holiday limit based on the new payment amount and triggers an alert to the customer when the limit is breached.

Consider the following conditions:

- The maximum limit for flexible repayment is USD 30000
- Every month instalment is due for USD 10000.

Consider a contract, having a term of one year for USD 120000 as on Jan 1,2020. The customer now requests for a payment holiday of the entire installment, for the months of Apr, May and Jun. Accordingly bank sanctions the payment holiday. Thus the Payment Holiday Limit now is USD 30000 and the Utilised Payment Holiday Limit is USD 30000.

Later the customer approaches the bank requesting for cancelation of the Payment Holiday, for Jun. This is approved by the bank and thereby the Available Payment Holiday limit becomes USD 10000 and Utilised Payment Holiday Limit now is USD 20000.

Now, the bank decides to increase the interest for the said contract, after Apr. This results in increasing the payment amount from USD 10000 to USD 11000 for the month of May. Since the month of May is within the defined Payment Holiday, the Utilised Payment Holiday Limit increases to USD 21000 and the Available Payment Holiday limit becomes USD 9000.

A mortgage arrangement of USD 500,000 for 25 years, is opened and disbursed as on Jan 1, 2022. The Payment Holiday Limit for the arrangement is set at USD 50,000.

A Payment Holiday is applied on the arrangement, for the months of Feb to Jun 2022, for the Payment Type Constant, Repay type Deferred and Repay Period left blank (that is, the system collects the interest accrued during the Payment Holiday or Holiday Interest, equally throughout the life of the loan).

The bank as on Apr 19, 2022 decides to increase the margin of the interest from 0.50 to 25.00.

This in turn affects the scheduled payments from Apr 19,2022 and the same can be seen in the schedule of the arrangement. However as the arrangement is in the Payment Holiday Period (that is, from Feb to Jun 2022), the said increase in the interest, is adjusted with Payment Holiday limit. The same can be observed, by the reduction of Available Payment Holiday limit from USD 35.381.95 to USD 34.113.45 as shown below.

Consider a loan having a Payment Holiday Limit of USD 3000 and monthly installment of USD 4500. In this scenario, while placing a Payment Holiday request, the system displays an error message, as the available Payment Holiday Limit is less than the monthly instalment and thus the New Payment Amount field should be entered maximum to the extent of 3000 USD.


##### Revolving Payment Holiday Limit

A Payment Holiday Limit can be configured to reinstate to its initial defined Payment Holiday limit, due to adhoc or excess repayments, over and above the due amount. This can be configured as defined in the Payment Holiday Limit in Payment Holiday configuration. Upon creation of an arrangement, the customer can request for a repayment holiday. The system evaluates the Repayment Holiday Limit for the product and accordingly reduces or skips the repayment obligation, as per the Flexible Payment Limit available. For revolving Payment Holiday Limit, any excess payment towards the principal, results in the evaluation of the Available Payment Holiday Limit with that of the Payment Holiday Limit defined and there by restoring the Payment Holiday limit to the extend of the defined Payment Holiday Limit (This is termed as Limit Restoration). The Available Holiday Limit is updated online and the same is evident in the Arrangement Overview page. This process can be understood from the scenarios below.

Consider a one year loan, starting from Jan 1, 2021, for an amount of USD 120000. The monthly repayment is say USD 10000 and Payment Holiday Limit USD 30000.

After settling the bills of Jan, Feb and March, the customer requests for a payment holiday on Mar 20 for next two bills. As the payment holiday is given for USD 20000, the holiday limit is reduced to USD 10000. When the customer makes a repayment of USD 50000 towards the principal of the loan on Mar 25, it reinstates the Payment Holiday Limit to its initial defined Payment Holiday Limit of USD 30000.

Consider a loan account in overdue status for USD 4500. The Payment Holiday Limit for the said loan is defined as USD 5000 and the Available Payment Holiday Limit for the loan as of now, is USD 2000.

The customer now approaches the bank for an excess payment of USD 6000.

The system adjusts excess payment, against the overdue amount of USD 4500 and the remaining amount of USD 1500 is used to replenish the Available Payment Holiday Limit (maximum to the extend of the initial defined Payment Holiday Limit of USD 5000). The New Available Payment Holiday Limit is USD 3500.

Consider a loan having Payment Holiday Limit of USD 5000 and monthly installment amount of USD 4500. The customer holds an excess amount of USD 6000 in his loan account.

Now the customer requests a Payment Holiday for the coming two months, summing to an amount of USD 9000 (that is, 2*USD 4500=USD 9000). The customer expects the same to be approved (as he holds an excess amount of USD 6000 in his loan account and has a Payment Holiday limit of USD 5000), however the system raises an error, as the system while defining the Payment Holiday checks the Payment Holiday limit and the customer only has a Payment Holiday Limit of USD 5000.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system does not consider the excess amount during repayment holiday request evaluation.


##### Controlling Payment Holidays Count

Banks/FIIs can control the number payment holidays allowed in an arrangement by configuring the HOLIDAY.COUNT periodic attribute in the Payment Schedule product condition. (Read Controlling Payment Holidays Count Configuration for more information)

Consider a mortgage arrangement in Lending product line, where the number of payment holidays that can be defined in a year is restricted to five (using the HOLIDAY.COUNT.YEARLY periodic attribute). If the user defines more than the stipulated payment holidays, the system raises an override.

When the customer tries to define a payment holiday for six instalments, the system displays the following override message: Maximum negotiable value of 5 has been exceeded by 1 in field SCHEDULE.


##### Defining Restriction on Consecutive Payment Holidays

The system supports restriction of payment holiday in parallel (that is, if an arrangement is within a payment holiday, further definition of a payment holiday is restricted, unless and until the current payment holiday period has expired), through the HOLIDAY.RESTRICT.LIFE periodic attribute, configured in the Payment Schedule product condition (Read Payment Holiday Configuration for more information).

> **⚠️ Note:** The system restricts definition of parallel payment for payment holidays having Repay Type as Deferred, without the configuration of the Periodic Attribute in the Payment Schedule product condition.

Consider a mortgage arrangement in Lending product line with HOLIDAY.RESTRICT.LIFE periodic attribute configured to raise an error, while defining a parallel payment holiday. Payment Holiday is already defined for the months of February, March, April, May, June and July.

The system’s current date is April 19, 2022 and the user tries to define a payment holiday for the month of August. The system displays the following error: Multiple Holiday requests are restricted in same holiday period.


##### Paying-off during Payment Holiday

Payoff Simulation and Direct Payoff of the loan arrangement, in a holiday or grace period, as well as, the loan arrangement carrying the unbilled holiday interest, is possible. The payoff statement is generated for the entire loan outstanding including the accrued holiday interest and due holiday amount.

Consider that a user triggers a payoff on a loan which is within the payment holiday period. The principal is 1000, due interest amount is 200, accrued interest is 50 and holiday interest balance is 20 (holiday balance represents accrued holiday interest which is yet to be billed).

The loan payoff simulation generates a payoff statement reflecting the holiday interest property along with the property like principal, interest and any fees or charges.

For the above example a payoff statement is generated with the components below.

- Payoff amount = 1270
- Account = 1000
- Interest = 270 (that is, Due Interest Amount=200, Accrual Interest=50 and Holiday Interest= 20)

Payoff bill includes the holiday interest accrual as part of the overall payoff bill.

Consider a user triggers payoff on a loan after payment holiday period ends. The principal is 1000, due interest is 205 (that is, Due interest for the current bill is 200 and the due Holiday Interest is 5), accrued interest is 50 and holiday interest balance is 15 (holiday balance represents accrued holiday interest which is yet to be billed).

The loan payoff simulation generates a payoff statement reflecting the holiday interest property along with the property like principal, interest and any fees or charges.

For the above example a payoff statement will be generated with the components below.

- Payoff amount = 1270
- Account = 1000
- Interest = 270 (that is, Due Interest Amount=205, Accrued Interest=50 and Holiday Interest=15)

Payoff bill includes the due holiday interest amounts and holiday interest accrual as part of the overall payoff bill.


##### Cancelling Holidays Declared

The user has an option to cancel or shorten the holidays declared, through Modify/Cancel Payment Holidays field in the Arrangement Overview page. The system triggers LENDING-CHANGE-PAYMENT.HOLIDAY when a payment holiday is modified or cancelled.

The payment holiday can be fully cancelled or modified to cancel specific number of holidays. But this cancellation should be consecutive. Out of four schedules marked as holiday, it is possible to:

- Cancel first
- Cancel last
- Cancel first few
- Cancel last few

But it is not possible to cancel the holidays in between or in a random order.

Change in schedule after cancel of payment holiday for Jul is:

Cancellation or shortening of holidays can be done only for consecutive schedules and error is raised when the user attempts to cancel the non – consecutive holidays.


##### Payment Holiday During Migration

The system allows migrations of loans under active Payment Holiday definitions. There are possibly two scenarios to be considered during migration or upgrade of loans.

- Loan under payment holiday period at the time of migration
- Loan completed grace or holiday period repaying holiday interest at the time of migration


###### Legacy Migration

The migration sequence in case of legacy loans with payment holiday is as follows:

1. Takeover arrangement
2. Capture outstanding loan bills and balances
3. If the loan is migrated during the holiday period, capture accrued interest (Holiday Interest).
4. Capture any future holidays using ‘Update Holiday’ and recalculate options can be configured suitably.


###### Upgrading Clients

For a customer upgrade to a loan product having payment holiday functionality,

1. Cancel existing holiday instructions
2. Re-configure fresh holiday instruction with defer option.


###### Legacy Migration

The migration sequence in case of legacy loans with payment holiday are as follows.

1. Takeover Arrangement
2. Capture outstanding loan bills and balances including the Holiday Interest due and accrued
3. Update ‘Schedule’ for ‘Holiday Interest’ and specify start and end dates based on the period over which the holiday interest is billed


###### Upgrading Clients

For a customer upgrade to a loan product having Payment Holiday,

1. The accrue interest is billed fully at the end of the Holiday Period
2. The holiday Instructions are performed if needed with Holiday functionality in the New Loan Product.
3. If bank perform upgrade after the end of holiday period and before billing of accrued holiday interest and wishes to use deferred functionality, then they can reverse the earlier holiday requests and reconfigure fresh holiday instructions with defer option.

The Update Holiday activity allows Payment Holiday to be defined for a repayment scheduled on loan takeover or migration date.

Consider a scenario where the loan takeover or migration date - May 1, 2021, as per the original schedule, and last repayment date is Nov 1, 2021

The user triggers Payment Holiday on May 1, 2021 for the repayment scheduled on the same day (May 1, 2021) with recalculation option as Term. The repayment due for May 1 is considered as a holiday by the system and extends the schedule to Dec 1, 2021 (as term is recalculated).

| Month 2 (Holiday) | PHINT – 30 MIGRPHINT -30 | NA |
| Month 3 (Holiday) | PHINT – 60 MIGRPHINT -30 | NA |

The overall pre migrated holiday interest (MIGRPHINT) is split across 4 cycles at 30/4=7.50 The overall post migrated holiday interest (PHINT) is split across 4 cycles at 60/4 = 15 |  |  |

### 1.43  Renegotiate


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**

> **Purpose:** *The AA module allows renegotiation of a loan during its lifecycle. This feature allows the users to modify the existing arrangement conditions that are negotiable as per the terms and conditions of the product.*

#### 📖 Introduction

The AA module allows renegotiation of a loan during its lifecycle. This feature allows the users to modify the existing arrangement conditions that are negotiable as per the terms and conditions of the product.

> **⚠️ Note:** For the Risk Free Rates (RFR) functionality, renegotiation of attributes is allowed only at the start or the capitalisation date of the interest periods.

There are no specific limitations for renegotiation of loan contracts in TBC. The functionality related to risk free rates is not applicable for loans in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The LENDING-RENEGOTIATE-ARRANGEMENT Activity can be used to negotiate the conditions of the arrangement.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Renegotiation Activity allows the user to update all the attributes (based on the negotiation rules for the Product) available for user input during the arrangement creation.

In the below example, the Term and the Principal Interest fields are modified in the arrangement using the Renegotiation Activity.

The original arrangement information is displayed in the below screenshots.

The user can link the interest rate of a loan arrangement to the interest rate of another arrangement (such as a deposit) using the Linked Rate functionality in the Interest condition. In this case, any change or renegotiation of the loan's interest rate results in the scheduling of a Change Interest activity in the target arrangement to process the rate change during COB.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Manage And Decide On Amendments (AA)

This option allows the user to change the arrangement conditions of different properties at one stretch at an arrangement level.

### 1.44  Repayment Order


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Payment Rules Condition is used to manage repayments towards the outstanding components in the loan. The repayment towards the loan can prioritise the settlement of outstanding bills based on financial status, date of bill generation and more.*
> 
> **Applications:** `FUNDS.TRANSFER`, `PAYMENT.ORDERS`, `TELLER`, `TXN.ACTIVITY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Activity*, *Property*, *Settle Activity*, *Tax Settlement*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Payment Rules Condition is used to manage repayments towards the outstanding components in the loan. The repayment towards the loan can prioritise the settlement of outstanding bills based on financial status, date of bill generation and more.

There are no specific limitations in Repayment Order for loans in TBC.

When a payment is received, an API is triggered to credit the funds using the required repayment activity. The funds are apportioned to the balances based on the repayment rules of this Activity triggered.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Repayment Order for the loans is defined using the Payment Rules Condition. The key features of Payment Rule conditions are:

- It provides different repayment rules based on the financial status of the arrangement
- The repayment rule type can be defined to allow repayments for: Billed balances based on: Bill date only Components in bill Advance payments. Live balances like accrued interest, live principal or outstanding principal (CUR )
- When there are multiple bills to be settled, the payment rules can decide if the oldest or latest bills should be settled first.
- When there are multiple bills due on the same date, the payment rules can decide if the highest outstanding first or the lowest first. This choice defines the repayment order for settlement of bills with the same due date can be based on total bill amount namely the highest or lowest amount first. When the bills are partially settled, the prioritisation is based on the outstanding bill amount and sorts them as the highest or lowest amount first.
- The outstanding items can be repaid in bill type-wise or property wise. The sequencing order for repayment of properties can be decided.
- Tax properties can be settled separately and can be chosen as the first item in the sequencing of properties. This option does not apply to advance payments and principal decrease type of repayment.
- The Tax Settlement attribute can be set as: Prorate - This is the default option when this field is not set. The tax component is settled alongside the interest and charge settlement. For a partial payment, the tax is calculated and collected on a pro-rated method based on the repaid amount.
- During overdue settlements, banks might want to settle the tax component first. During the partial settlement of bills, this setup gives the opportunity to settle the tax components first.
- After the settlement of the outstanding bills, repayment rules can make the deferred charges due.
- Advance payment option can be used to settle the repaid amount on the future scheduled bills and settle them in advance. It can allow advance settlement fully or partially on those future bills.
- The restrictions on advance payments can be defined. By default, the system doesn’t control the number of bills that can be settled in advance. Based on the requirement, the restrictions can be made to specify if advance payments can be made only to the already issued bills or current bills or specified number of future bills.
- After settling the overdue, due and advance bills based on the setup, any excess funds can be used to repay based on the reminder activity defined. The option to settle unearned interest is available only for Islamic contracts.

An illustration of Mortgage Product’s Product Condition is shown below.

The key features of this repayment rule are:

- It is the same for both regular and delinquent loans.
- It sorts the outstanding bills by date and settles each component within that bill.
- The bills are sorted to settle the oldest bill first.
- If there are two bills generated on the same day, they are sorted to have the highest bill amount first.
- The tax component on interest and charges have to be settled separately.
- The tax properties in the product should be given separately in the sequence. The sequence of properties to be settled are: Tax Property VAT Property Penalty Interest Principal Interest Loan Principal – Account Property Principal Decrease Fee New arrangement Fee
- No deferred charge bills are made due at the end of this repayment.
- Any remaining funds after settling the bills are applied towards a principal decrease activity.


#### 🔧 Working With

The loans can have repayments from:

- An automatic settlement from the settlement condition The repayment received from the settlement account is apportioned according to the payment rule condition attached to the Applypayment activity configured. The Applypayment activity is specified in the Settle Activity (PAYIN.SETTLE.ACTIVITY) of Settlement Condition. The repayment rule attached to this Activity is used for referring to the repayment rule.
- Manual payments using the payment channels like TELLER , FUNDS.TRANSFER , PAYMENT.ORDERS and such applications. The repayment received from external payment applications like Teller, FT, Payment order and more is mapped to an Applypayment activity in the Activity Mapping using the Activity field ( TXN.ACTIVITY ). The repayment rule attached to this Activity is used for referring to the repayment rule.

- The features related to automatic settlement of bills are not applicable for loans in TBC.
- In case of manual settlement of the due bills for a loan in TBC, the customer or user initiates a repayment transaction in the external payment system (which is outside the TBC). When a payment is received, an API is triggered to credit the funds using the required repayment activity. The funds are apportioned to the balances based on the repayment rules of this Activity triggered.

Consider a mortgage product with the repayment rule configuration to settle oldest bills first with tax as a separate component. This setup is illustrated in the configuration page.

In this mortgage product, there are three bills outstanding:

The breakup of the bills are:

The repayment order according to the payment rule is the oldest bill first. So the bills are sorted as:

- The oldest bill is the charge bill for new arrangement fee dated 01 Feb 20
- The next is the instalment bill without taxes dated 01 Mar 20
- The third is the instalment bill with taxes dated 01 Apr 20

When there is payment for 1000 made using a payment system, the corresponding activity is triggered. Here the repayment triggers the default LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.REPAYMENT credit activity. The corresponding payment rule is described in the configuration page.

The repayment of 1000 settles:

1. New arrangement fee first, fully
2. Instalment bill due in March, partially with repayment order to settle Penalty interest first fully. Principal interest next but partially. There are no funds available to be allocated to the principal.

Now the outstanding bills and their components are:

When there is payment for 8450 made using a payment system, the repayment settles:

1. Instalment bill due in March: The remaining amount of principal interest The principal component in the bill.
2. Instalment bill with taxes partially with repayment order to settle Tax property first VAT property next but partially

In the April bill, the Tax property is settled fully but the next component VAT is settled partially. The remaining VAT, penalty interest, principal interest and principal are settled only when further payments are done by the customer.

### 1.45  Rescheduling Payment Dates


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Loan rescheduling refers to amending the terms of an existing loan in order to extend, change, repayment period, frequency, mode, etc. It can mean a delay in the due date(s) of required payments or reducing payment amounts by extending the payment period and increasing the number of payments.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *GB Narrative*, *PayFreq*, *Payment Limit Revolving*, *Recurrence Pattern*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Loan rescheduling refers to amending the terms of an existing loan in order to extend, change, repayment period, frequency, mode, etc. It can mean a delay in the due date(s) of required payments or reducing payment amounts by extending the payment period and increasing the number of payments.

The system allows the rescheduling a loan in terms of changing the loan repayment date, repayment holiday and frequency of repayment.

There are no specific limitations for rescheduling payment dates of loan contracts in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Payment Schedule Property Class is used to define parameters for rescheduling loans. In order to reschedule a Lending Arrangement, the attributes eligible for negotiation at the Arrangement level must be defined as negotiable in the Payment Schedule Property.

In the below screenshot, the Payment Limit Revolving attribute is defined as negotiable.


#### 🔧 Working With

When the attributes in the Payment Schedule Property Class are defined as negotiable, the user can amend the below loan parameters:

- Change in Repayment Frequency
- Repayment Holiday
- Change Loan Repayment Date


##### Change in Repayment Frequency

The user can change the frequency of repayment using the Payment Schedule Property Condition. The below screenshot displays the repayment frequency of the mortgage loan, which is changed from 1M to 2M as part of the loan rescheduling process.

The below screenshot displays the repayment frequency defined on monthly basis before rescheduling the payment.

The below screenshot displays the change in repayment frequency from 1 month to 2 months.

The below screenshots display the repayment frequency changed to alternate months after rescheduling the payment.


##### Repayment Holiday

Payment Holiday is a feature offered by banks with which the customer can opt to take an installment break to skip repayments for any reason. The system stops generating bills during the holiday period.

The below screenshots display the payment holiday applied on a Mortgage loan for six installments.

The user can place a holiday request using the Request Payment Holidays option as displayed in the below screenshot.

Post authorisation of the holiday request, the Activity Log, Payment Holiday Menu, Payment Schedule and AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS table are updated as displayed in the below screenshots.

The below sample screenshot displays the repayment that is skipped for six installments from the month of April to November.

The below screenshot displays the payment holiday details that is updated in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS record.


##### Change Loan Repayment Date

The user can amend the repayment date of an arrangement. In the following example, the repayment date of the arrangement is changed from 21st of every month to every second Monday of the month using the Change Activity for schedule.

The below screenshot displays the payment date as 21st of every month.

Amendment of repayment date can be done by updating the Recurrence Pattern fields as displayed in the below screenshot.

The below screenshot displays the updated repayment dates of the arrangement.

> **⚠️ Note:** In this arrangement, the monthly repayable amount is updated due to the change in repayment date.

### 1.46  Risk Free Rates


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Risk Free Rates(RFR) feature supports any RFR irrespective of currency and publication time. They are not equal to IBOR and have to be processed in a different way. RFRs are published with a lag, that is, the rate that is published today is applied for a date in the past. This means that transac...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AC.RFR.DETAILS`, `EB.CASHFLOW`, `PERIODIC.INTEREST`, `ST.RFR.DETAILS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Apr Type*, *Arrangement*, *Arrangement
 Date*, *Base Min Rate*, *Contract ID*, *Date Convention*, *Initial
 Payment Projected*, *Loan
 Amount* ... +30 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Risk Free Rates(RFR) feature supports any RFR irrespective of currency and publication time. They are not equal to IBOR and have to be processed in a different way. RFRs are published with a lag, that is, the rate that is published today is applied for a date in the past. This means that transactions, which use RFRs must reference new rates each business day for compounding interests. Banks can choose from multiple ways of compounding interest.

The features related to Risk Free Rates are not applicable for loans in TBC. Read Introduction to TBC for Lending for more information about TBC for loans.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The RFRs stored in the PERIODIC.INTEREST application are only published rates and are compounded on a daily basis to arrive at a final interest rate for the period.

- The user enters the RFRs index in the Periodic Index field.
- Along with periodic index, market convention and spread treatment parameters are passed to call the rate calculation routine to arrive at the daily compounding interest rate for the contract.
- The calculation method defined in the Rfr Calc Method attribute is used to calculate the total accrual amount for the current interest period.
- The market convention ( Rfr Convention attribute) that AA follows is the use of historical RFRs for daily compounding and is called as Lookback.

Whenever a spread is input in a contract which is on top of the rate, there are spread treatment options that can be defined in the Rfr Spread Treatment attribute.

If the rate applies till a date in excess of the Period End Date , that is, when the interest period ends is a weekend and contains a real month end date, then the business day’s ( Date Convention attribute) convention from the Account Property conditions takes precedence in calculating the day count.

|  | Day 1 | Day 2 | Day 3 | Day 4 | Day 5 | Effective Rate (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Periodic Index Rate | -0.023 | -0.016 | 0.012 | 0.015 | -0.009 |  |
| Rate Used | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.012 | 0.015 | 0.00 |  |
| Day Count | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 3 | 0.003857 |


##### Payment Schedule Projections

For the Risk Free Rates functionality, schedule projection is calculated dynamically using the respective day’s interest rate for the rest of the term from the Overview screen and the values are not stored. This is because of daily rate change during the interest period and the accurate payment amount can be calculated only at the end of the interest period.

Consider the following example scenario:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Loan Amount | USD 10,000 |
| Arrangement Date | 02 January 2020 |
| Maturity Date | 31 March 2020 |
| Payment Type | Annuity |
| Payment Date – 31st of every month | 31st of every month |
| Payment Frequency | Monthly |
| Initial Payment Projected | USD 550 (approximately) |
| RFR Convention | Lookback |
| RFR Look Back Days | 5 |
| RFR Look Back Type | Narrow Definition |
| ISSUE BILL | 28 January 2020 |

In this case, the accurate payment to be paid on 31 January can only be calculated on or after 24 January based on the Lookback days and Issue bill activity.

> **⚠️ Note:** All RFR properties have to be scheduled and should have the same Payment Frequency. The execution days cannot be more than the Lookback days defined in Interest Property conditions, and if defined, an error message is displayed.


##### IFRS Processing

IFRS has the following rules for the RFR cashflow update:

- Initial transition from IBOR to RFR updates the EIR (Effective Interest Rate) in EB.CASHFLOW using the LENDING-UPDATE.CASHFLOW-REPORTING Activity.
- Ongoing daily changes in cashflow are updated in EB.CASHFLOW using the INTEREST-CHANGE event type during the RFR rate revision process.

> **⚠️ Note:** Apr Type in Reporting Property Condition with Source Type as INTEREST is restricted for RFR contracts, as it is relevant only for deposits with fixed rate.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes the working of RFR using multiple ways of compounding calculation with examples. When the RFR Calc Method attribute is:

According to regulatory papers by the Bank of England and ARRC the rate compounding can be of two types - cumulative and non-cumulative (NCCR):

- Cumulative Compounded Rate (Rate Compounding) method is based on the ISDA’s formula for compounded RFRs in arrears.
- Non-Cumulative Compounded Rate (NCCR) method is a variation of the Cumulative method in which daily compounded rates (instead of cumulative rates) are calculated.

The system records the risk-free rate calculated for each working day of the arrangement in the ST.RFR.DETAILS application along with the details such as daily accrual, principal balance on which the accrual amount is calculated, and so on. In case of any discrepancy between the system-calculated risk-free rate and the expected value for a specific day, the user can validate the calculation details from the ST.RFR.DETAILS application.

The record in ST.RFR.DETAILS for the interest period from Dec 18, 2009 to Dec 21, 2009, where the Non-Cumulative Compounded Rate (NCCR) calculated for Dec 18, 2009, with the related details are displayed as shown in the below screenshot.

The record in ST.RFR.DETAILS for the interest period from Dec 23, 2009 to Dec 26, 2009, where the risk-free rate calculated (using amount compounding) for the 23rd and 24th of December 2009, along with the related details, are displayed as shown in the below screenshot.

The Non-Cumulative Compounded Rate (NCCR) calculated for December 18, 2009, is reflected in ST.RFR.DETAILS for the interest period from December 18, 2009 to December 21, 2009, as shown in the below screenshot.

The risk-free rate calculated (using amount compounding) for December 23, 2009, and December 24, 2009, is reflected in ST.RFR.DETAILS for the interest period from December 23, 2009 to December 26, 2009, as shown in the below screenshot.

##### Non-Cumulative Compounded Rate (NCCR)

Principal decrease is a common scenario where NCCR becomes more useful than the cumulative compounded rate approach. When there is a principal change, only the principal amount is used for interest calculations changes. All the steps for NCCR calculations remain the same.

The below illustration shows the regulatory text by the Bank of England with the steps to calculate NCCR.

- Step 1 shows the Cumulative compounded rate (ACR) which is used to calculate NCCR.
- Step 2 shows the formula to derive the unannualised cumulative compounded rate (UCR). The compounded rate is unannualised by multiplying with the business day convention, that is, the number of calendar days in the interest period divided by the market convention for quoting the number of days in the year (360, 365 and so on).
- Step 3 shows the formula for the calculation of the NCCR. The UCR for that given business day is subtracted from the UCR of the previous business day and multiplied with the market convention for quoting the number of days in a year (360, 365 and so on). Further this answer is divided by the day count for the given business day.
- Step 4 is the formula for interest accrual calculation with NCCR - Simple Interest.

Consider a loan with Rfr Lookback Days set as five business days, Narrow Definition with monthly payment schedules. There is no spread on the contract. The principal is USD 100,000,000.00 and interest is for one month (Jul 1 to 31). If there is a principal decrease on Jul 17 and new principal is USD 90,000,000.00 (a decrease of USD 10,000,000.00), the calculations are tabulated as shown below:

| Interest Period Date | RFR Observation Date | Daily RFR Rate | Day Count - Narrow | Cumulative Compounded (Step 1) | Calculation of UCR (Step 2) | NCCR (Step 3) | Daily Interest Accrual with NCCR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15-Jul-19 | 8-Jul-19 | 2.4800% | 1 | 2.4800% | 0.00689% | 2.4800% | $6,888.89 |
| 16-Jul-19 | 9-Jul-19 | 2.4500% | 1 | 2.4651% | 0.01369% | 2.4502% | $6,806.02 |
| 17-Jul-19 | 10-Jul-19 | 2.4600% | 1 | 2.4635% | 0.02053% | 2.4603% | $6,150.84 |
| 18-Jul-19 | 11-Jul-19 | 2.4100% | 1 | 2.4503% | 0.02723% | 2.4105% | $6,026.24 |
| 19-Jul-19 | 12-Jul-19 | 2.3600% | 3 | 2.4118% | 0.04690% | 2.3606% | $17,704.82 |
| 20-Jul-19 | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend |
| 21-Jul-19 | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend | Weekend |
| 22-Jul-19 | 15-Jul-19 | 2.4600% | 1 | 2.4180% | 0.05373% | 2.4612% | $6,152.88 |

### 1.47  Risk Participation for Bilateral Loans


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A loan is associated with a credit risk as there is a chance for the borrower to default on the repayments. The banks need to ensure that the borrower repay the loans without fail.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.BILL.DETAILS`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Buy Back*, *Fixed*, *Margin Operand*, *Own Bank*, *Participant Role*, *Participant role*, *Participation Type* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A loan is associated with a credit risk as there is a chance for the borrower to default on the repayments. The banks need to ensure that the borrower repay the loans without fail.

The banks mitigate the risk exposure in the loan by selling the risk exposure to other banks. This helps them to diversify the Risk Portfolio. The banks that share the risk exposure from the owning bank are called Risk Participants.

The owning bank can sell the risk exposure (full or partial) to the risk participants, so that the risk exposure is shared between the banks accordingly.

Risk participants only share the risk and do not provide any funding to the borrower. In case of any default by the borrower, the risk participants pay the amount to the owning bank which then is decided based on the share of the Risk exposure which the Risk Participants hold.

The following are the two types of risk participants:

- Fixed Risk Participants - Risk exposure is based on a specific commitment amount of the Book commitment.
- Variable Risk Participants - Risk exposure is based on a certain percentage of the Book commitment. Though Variable Risk Participant comes with certain percentage of commitment, the system captures only the share amount of that participant and not the percentage.


##### Write-off for Loans

Bank can write-off a loan or a bill when it has not received the repayment due for a certain period and has to follow the regulatory compliance.

As risk participants cover a portion of the loan, the risk participants pay the written off amount proportionately. These settlements happen outside the loan contract. As the risk participants pay the portion of the loan amount, the corresponding amount should be reduced from their commitment.

A loan contract can be partially or fully written off.

- When the loan is written off completely, then all the risk participants balances are reduced to zero. The bank can write off the entire funding portion it holds irrespective of the risk exposure sold.
- When there is a principal write off, that is, either the outstanding principal amount or a specific bill is being written off, then the risk participant’s balances are reduced proportionately based on the principal amount that is being written off.

In both the cases, the adjusted or reduced amount is settled by the risk participant to the own bank outside the contract.

Bills such as risk fees and risk margin that the own bank needs to pay to risk participants cannot be written off, as it is the own bank’s responsibility to pay those bills.

The features related to Participant property class are not applicable in TBC. Therefore, the functionality pertaining to risk participation for bilateral loans are not applicable for loans in TBC. Read Introduction to TBC for Lending to know more for more information about TBC for loans.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

A Participant Property of property Type as Risk Participant is created to add risk participant to a loan contract and then add it to the product at the product designer level.

For adding the fund participants and risk participants, two separate properties need to be created and added to the product, that is, one property with property Type set as Participant and the other with Type as Risk Participant as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** A single Participant property cannot have both the Participant and Risk Participant property types.

The bank user creates separate properties for the fund participants and risk participants, and they are added to the Participant Property class at the product group level. At product designer level, both the properties have their respective product conditions attached to them.

> **⚠️ Note:** If property type is not selected the system defaults it to Participant.

The user configures the following property classes, to calculate the Risk fees, Risk Margin and Flat Fees for the bilateral contracts or club loan contracts.

Interest Property Class is used to define the risk fees and risk margin and it can accrued and paid to the Risk participant.

To differentiate the risk participant’s Risk Fee and Risk Margin property from the other regular interest properties, the Interest property, which is created for paying out risk fee or margin consists of the Risk Participant property type along with existing Non Customer property type.

The screenshot below shows the Non Customer Interest Properties created to pay the risk margin and risk fees to the risk participant.

Charge property class is used to define the flat fees that is to be paid to the risk participants. It can be configured as an activity charge or as a scheduled charge, which can be defined in the Payment schedule.

To differentiate the Charge property that is used for paying flat fees to the risk participants from the other regular charge properties, the Charge property created for paying out the flat fees consists of the ‘Risk Participant’ property type along with existing ‘Non Customer’ and ‘Credit’ property type.

The screenshot below shows the Non Customer Charge Property created to pay the flat fees to the risk participant.

The properties created are attached to the respective Property Class of the Product in the Product Group as can be seen below

In the Product Designer, appropriate Product Conditions are attached to the Interest and Charge Properties which are attached to the Product are shown below:

The screenshot below shows the calculation source balance is defined for the Interest properties.

Once the product is published, the bank uses the risk fees and risk margin at the arrangement level.

> **⚠️ Note:** Irrespective of the bilateral or club contract with risk participants, a syndication settlement account is created. The risk fees and margin to be paid out are initially credited to the syndication settlement account and then a payment order created to pay out the funds to the respective risk participants.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes the risk participation and the risk share transfer in bilateral loans.


##### Selling the Risk Participation

The owning banks can make changes to their existing risk portfolio through share transfer by selling or buying risk exposures from other risk participant banks during the life term of the loan.

##### Risk Share Transfer

When the owning bank sells the risk exposure to risk participants , the formulas to calculate the maximum amount that can be transferred, share transfer ratio and balances of risk participants after share transfer are:

1. Maximum Transferable Amount = Current Commitment of the Owning Bank - Current Commitment of all the Existing Risk Participants

where Current Commitment = CUR + UTL + OVD

1. Share Transfer Ratio= (Share Transfer Amount/Own Bank’s Current Commitment) *100
2. Total = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | Own Bank’s CUR +UTL +UTL )
3. UR of RP3 = Own Bank’s CUR * Share Transfer Ratio
4. UTL of RP3 = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
5. OVD of RP 3= Transfer Amount- (Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

When the share transfer is complete to an existing risk participant in the contract, the calculated balances are added to the existing balances of the risk participant to whom the share transfer is complete.

When the owning bank buys back its risk from risk participants, the formulas to calculate the maximum amount that can be bought by own bank, share transfer ratio and balances of risk participants after share transfer are:

1. Current Commitment = CUR + UTL + OVD
2. Share Transfer Ratio= (Share Transfer Amount/ Selling RP Current Commitment) *100
3. Total = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | selling RP CUR +UTL
4. CUR = Selling RP CUR * Share Transfer Ratio
5. UTL = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
6. OVD = Transfer Amount- (Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

The balances derived are subtracted from the existing balances of the risk participants.

##### Risk Margin and Risk Fees Operands

Risk Margin or Risk Fees Operands are available under Risk Participant Property. Default values of Risk fees and Risk margin for the contract can be entered in the respective properties. Banks can alter the default risk fees or margin for a particular risk participant by adding or reducing a margin for that particular risk participant using the Operand field in the risk participant tab.

The following Margin Operand are applicable for Risk Participants.

The Bank reduces the Risk Margin and Risk fees for a specific risk participant using Operand. The value entered in the Margin Rate field is subtracted from the default risk margin and risk fees of the contract to obtain the effective risk margin rate.

If the default risk fees defined in the contract is 0.5% and below definition is given for a risk participant, then the Risk fees paid for the risk participant becomes 0.3%.

It is used to increase the default risk margin or risk fees. The value entered in the Margin rate field add up to the default risk margin or risk fees of the contract. Example: When the default risk fees defined in the contract is 0.5% and below definition is given for a risk participant, then the Risk fees to be paid for the risk participant becomes 1.3%.

It is used to override the default risk margin or risk fees. The value entered by the user replaces the default risk margin or risk fees of the contract. Example: When the default risk fees defined in the contract is 0.5% and below definition is given for a risk participant, then the Risk fees to be paid for the risk participant becomes 1%.


###### Calculating Risk Margin and Risk Fees for Bilateral Contracts

A contract with two risk participants ABC Bank (100112) and XYZ bank (100369) is created as a Bilateral Facility on May 24, 2021, for USD 1 million.

When the bank collects the risk fees and risk margin at the facility level , that is in facility arrangement,

- Risk fees is 0.7% (In Risk Fees Interest Property defined at Arrangement level)
- Risk Margin is 0.5% (In Risk Margin Interest Property defined at Arrangement level)
- Risk Margin and Risk fees due once a month
- Payment Schedule defines the frequency of risk margin and risk fees to be paid. Bill type defined in the payment schedule condition must be ‘Internal’.

ABC Bank Risk Participant

When the bank customises the default risk fees or risk margin in the contract specific to Nomura, then it uses the operands in the risk participant property.

- The bank pays an extra 0.8% in addition to the default risk fees(0.7%) defined in the contract as shown in the screenshot below and the risk fees paid to ABC Bank becomes 1.5%.

- The bank pays 1.3% as the risk margin instead of the default 0.5% and so the bank user uses the Operand ‘Override’ as shown in the screenshot below .

###### Calculating Flat Fees for the Bilateral Contracts

If the customer draws USD 600,000 under the facility and the bank pays a flat fee (Non Customer Charge) of USD 5,000 to all the risk participants in the contract for every new drawing taken by the customer under the facility, then the bank makes use of the activity charge to pay this flat fee to the Risk Participant.

Charge payment method in the activity charge condition should be pay . Each risk participant added to the contract is paid out a charge of USD 5,000 which is defined in the charge product condition. On the contrary, in the funded participation, flat fee is paid out pro-rata to the participant banks.

If the bank wants to customise this noncustomer charge for Nomura in the contract, then the bank pays USD 7,000 instead of USD 5,000 to Nomura and USD 5,000 to JP Morgan. For JP Morgan, the charge amount defined in the charge condition is taken by default. For Nomura, changes to the default charge definition is done in the Charges tab under the Risk Participant Property as shown in the screenshot given below.

Flat fees bills that are paid are displayed in the Drawing Overview screen as shown in the screenshot below. The bills are auto settled .


##### Activities for Loan Write-Off

Following are activities for loan write-off:

- LENDING-WRITE.OFF.BILL-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE - Use to write off only the bills of the loan.
- LENDING-WRITE.OFF.BALANCE-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE - Use to write off specific balances of the loan like outstanding principal (partial write off)
- LENDING-WRITE.OFF-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE - Use to write off the entire loan (full write off)
