## Chapter 2: lending - CL


lending - CL module of Temenos Transact


### 2.1  Collections features


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The functionality of Temenos Transact Collections is based principally on the overdue debt records held in the Past Due or AA overdue component in Temenos Transact . The debt collection is available for all loan products in Temenos Transact Lending Suite, handled through the Arrangement Architecture...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AC.BALANCE.TYPE`, `ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN`, `CATEGORY`, `CL. ACTIVITY`, `CL.ACTION`, `CL.ACTIVITY`, `CL.COLLECTION.ITEM` ... +12 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Aa*, *Account No*, *Act*, *Action*, *Action Code*, *Agency*, *Amount Exchange Rate*, *Amt* ... +127 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

The functionality of Temenos Transact Collections is based principally on the overdue debt records held in the Past Due or AA overdue component in Temenos Transact . The debt collection is available for all loan products in Temenos Transact Lending Suite, handled through the Arrangement Architecture (AA) or Loans and Deposits (LD)module.

When a borrower defaults on a due payment, the unpaid item is taken over by the overdue processing component (in AA or PD) and follows an aging process (buckets). These buckets segment collection items in different stages of case-handling.

Irrespective of the number of products and overdue payments and amounts, a delinquent customer has to be classified in one class. Any collection or recovery action should be based on the global customer position and not by product or payment. Therefore, collection items (records generated by the system when a customer defaults on a loan) are based on the customer’s ID, and not on individual AA or LD contracts. For a given customer, all accounts in arrears are placed under the same collection item collectively and are dealt with as such.

When a collector pulls a customer from a queue for follow up (no other collector should work on the same customer before it is released by the first collector), the worked record has to be stamped with a pre-defined action code (how communication was established) and an outcome code (the item’s status) describing the activity of the collector and the result of the action respectively. Some outcome codes can generate an automatic future outcome code.

A Promise To Pay (PTP) can generate a Kept Promise To Pay (KPTP) or Broken Promise To Pay (BPTP) outcome code. This is based on the customer’s actions from the date the collection item was updated to the outcome due date agreed upon.

Based on the outcome code, the worked record must either be re-queued in the same queue but with different priority or to be transferred to another queue for further action, that is, PTP, transfer to field collection, external agencies or no further action to be taken status. This is dependent on the criterion of the queues defined.

Once the customer has no leftover items in arrears, the items would disappear from the collections queues until the customer defaults again, at which point they will be again placed into an appropriate queue to be worked.


##### Challenges of Banks and Financial Institutions

Non-recovery of loans is one of the major risk areas that banks face, which impacts the bank’s overall balance sheet and profitability in an adverse manner. The NPAs (Non-Performing Assets) or not recovered debt is a major concern for every financial institution, thus every bank across the globe is spending considerate amount of time, money and effort on the recovery and collection of overdue debt.

It is for this reason that the Collections module is introduced in Temenos Transact to facilitate the debt collection process.


##### Collections for Overdue Items

Temenos Transact Collections is based on the overdue debt records held in the Past Due or AA Overdue component in Temenos Transact . The debt collection is available for all loan products in Temenos Transact lending suite, handled through the AA (Arrangement Architecture) or LD (Loans and Deposits) module.The collection module also handles debt collection for an overdraft current account. Overdraft accounts are monitored and tracked till the settlement of the overdue is actioned.


##### Monitoring Multi-Currency Collections

The Collections module supports monitoring and management of foreign currency overdues and records customer discussion outcomes in all currencies.

The collector can view the customer’s delinquent foreign currency loans, overdue amounts and subsequently record meeting outcomes in any currency.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section helps the user to configure the parameters required to process Collections.


##### Prerequisites of Configuration and Table Parameterisation

There are certain parameters for Collections that need to be defined to allow the Loan Collection process to initiate correctly. The module comes with a pre-defined configuration. However, the user can alter the values. The default configuration is shown below.

| S.No | Parameter Table | Live File | Dependent Records |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CL.PARAMETER | No | CL.OUTCOME CL.ACTION CATEGORY COMPANY AC.BALANCE.TYPE |
| 2 | CL.BUCKET.PARAM | No | No dependent records |
| 3 | CL.ITEM.WEIGHT | No | No dependent records |
| 4 | CL.QUEUE.TYPE | No | No dependent records |
| 5 | CL.QUEUE | No | CL.QUEUE.TYPE |
| 6 | CL.ACTION | No | No dependent records |
| 7 | CL.OUTCOME | No | CL.ACTION CL.QUEUE.TYPE |
| 8 | CL.COLLECTOR.TYPE | No | CL.ACTION CL.QUEUE.TYPE |
| 9 | CL.COLLECTOR | No | CL.INCENTIVE.STRATEGY CL.COLLECTOR.USER CL.QUEUE.TYPE |
| 10 | CL.COLLECTION.ITEM | No | No dependent records |
| 11 | CL.COLLECTOR.USER | Yes | No dependent records |
| 12 | CL.AGENCY.COMMISSION | Yes | No dependent records |
| 13 | CL.COLLECTOR.ACTIVITY | Yes | No dependent records |
| 14 | CL.ITEM.BUCKET | Yes | No dependent records |
| 15 | CL.ACTIVITY | Yes | No dependent records |
| 16 | CL.QUEUE.COLL | No | No dependent records |
| 17 | CL.EXTERNAL.AGENCY | No | No dependent records |
| 18 | CL.INCENTIVE.STRATEGY | No | No dependent records |

The loan collection parameter tables and dependencies are illustrated below:

It defines the types of queue like tele-collection, field collection, supervisor or external agency queue. This queue type is updated in the CL.QUEUE .

It is used to allocate the queue in collection item. The collection items are assigned to different queues based on the conditions here. CL.QUEUE.TYPE indicates the type of queue like tele-calling. Based on the selection criteria, when an item fits into different queues, PRIORITY decides which queue has to be chosen.

- Item Field - Indicates the name or number of the field in the file CL.COLLECTION.ITEM to be used as a selection criterion for this queue.
- Operator - Any valid operator.
- Value From and Value To - Indicates the From and To conditions for selection.
- Logic Oper - And/or operator (selection can be based on many fields).

When the queue is handled by external agents the information can be filled in the below fields:

- Agency - Indicates the external agency who handles the queue and AGENCY.BRANCH: Branch of the agency that handles the queue.
- Inactivity Days - Indicates the number of days without any action for any item in this queue to be considered as inactive.
- Inactivity Outcome - Indicates the outcome to be applied to items falling under the condition specified in the previous field.
- Selection - Decides if a queue can be inactive for a certain period.

It stores the loan collection agency name and contract date of the bank with that agency. The complete information of the agency like owner name, branch address and contact number. Commission percentage for agency is indicated. Also if there is a target amount to be achieved it is indicated along with the commission point for that target.

It defines the action done by the collector. The record ID indicates the action code and Action Code indicates the cost of the action used for statistical reports.

Some of the standard actions that are stored in the CL.ACTION table are:

- Call From Customers
- Call To Customers
- Filed Complaint
- Non-Cooperative Customer
- Issue Notice
- System Updates
- Visiting Customers

It stores the outcome of collections and this notifies the results of the actions performed by various collectors.

Records here indicate different types of outcomes, some of which are used to stamp the item (customer) in the queue for information only; others cause a re-queuing action (change priority in the same queue or transfer to another queue). Hence, an outcome can be productive or non-productive.

When the collector processes a collection item and manages to secure a commitment from a customer to pay part or all of their outstanding debt on a given date, the PTP outcome code is used. It is a productive outcome since it is followed by an Activity and another outcome ensues as a result of this activity (for example, KPTP, PPTP or BPTP).

- Productivity Flg - Indicates whether the outcome is productive or not
- ID - Indicates the action code that can trigger this outcome is indicated here
- Qtype Queue - Indicates is the control queue type or queue for which this outcome code is available
- Outcome Due Date indicates if a date is to be entered with outcome code
- Max Future Date - Indicates the maximum gap that can be between current date and the outcome due date
- Outcome Due Amt - Indicates if outcome code should have an amount entered with it
- Src Queue and Dest Queue - Specifies the source queue and destination queue . Used to transfer an item from a queue to another queue based on the outcome code
- Notes - Indicates the notes to be displayed when the collector enters the output code
- The Collector and New Queue - Enables reassigning the collector to a new queue

- It defines the ageing bucket for the overdue items based on the number of days the record (both contract and arrangement) is overdue. When the collection items are created, they fall into the respective buckets based on this configuration. Company specific records contain the number of days in the No From and No To fields and Bucket No that range should be allotted to.
- Based on the bucket in which the collection item belongs to the incentive, the bank derives the strategy.
- For PD records, the buckets are based on the Start Date field in PD.PAYMENT.DUE .
- For arrangement records that go overdue, the Bill Pay Date from AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS for the bills are being used for aging buckets.

- It defines the type of collector like tele-collectors, field collectors, supervisors and external agency.
- Supervisors can reassign collection items between the collectors and the queues. Valid queue type is indicated from CL.QUEUE.TYPE table to indicate the type of collectors who can work on this queue. Int Ext Flg - Indicates if the collector is internal or external type. The main action of the collector is like, calling the customer or making a personal visit, etc. This has to be a valid field in CL.ACTION .

It contains the information of the collector like:

- Collector Type - Indicates a valid type defined earlier
- Collector User - Indicates a system user ID
- Assigned Queue - Indicates the queue this user should work on
- Incentive Strategy - Indicates the strategy to be applied for this collector (valid record in CL.INCENTIVE.STRATEGY )

Along with these details, the home phone and mobile phone numbers are stored.

- It contains parameters for sorting the CL.COLLECTION.ITEMS based on financial impact and priority. (Outstanding loan amount and No of Days in Overdue for payment). The SYSTEM record is a mandatory record. A sorting record can be created for each record defined in CL.QUEUE application to customise the values.
- Outstd Amt Upto and Ots Weight - Assigns weightage to the outstanding amount of the CL.COLLECTION.ITEM based on the amount.
- Odue Amt Upto and Odue Wgt - Assigns weightage to overdue amount of the CL.COLLECTION.ITEM based on the amount.
- Bptp Upto No and Bptp Weight - Assigns weightage based on number of BPTP (Broken Promise To Pay) in the CL.COLLECTION.ITEM.
- Pd Days Upto and Pd Days Weight - Assigns weightage based on the number of days the CL.COLLECTION.ITEM in is Past Due.
- Dno Act Upto and Dno Act Wgt - Assigns weightage based on number of days elapsed since last action performed on the CL.COLLECTION.ITEM .
- Last Outcome and Last Ocome Wgt - Assigns the weight to be given for the Last Outcome attribute of each item
- Black List Wgt - Assigns weight to be given to items with black-list field is Y.
- Ul Loan Secured - Decides if loan is secured or not to be considered in weight calculations.
- Security Wgt - Assigns weight to be given to the loan secured based on UL.LOAN.SECURED .

Company specific records to specify general parameters of Collections module.

- Cl Outcome - Indicates calid values to be assigned to Promise to pay, Kept promise to pay, Broken promise to pay, partial kept promise to pay under PTP.CODE, KPTP.CODE, BPTP.CODE and PPTP.CODE respectively.
- Ptp Percentage - Gives the percentage of a promise to pay amount if paid it can be considered as promise to pay kept up.
- Ptp Grace Prd - Indicates the grace period given for a customer before a promise to pay (PTP) is considered as broken (BPTP).
- Pptpb Code - Indicates the outcome code indicating partial kept promise to pay when a partial repayment is done before the PTP end of the grace period.
- Spay Code - Indicates the outcome code to be populated automatically if customer pays without any promise to pay.
- Apay Code -Indicates the outcome code used for payments obtained by external agencies and it is used to calculate the commission to pay to external agencies.
- Asal Code - Indicates the Outcome code used for salary assignment obtained by external agencies and it is used to calculate the commission to pay to external agencies.
- Category From and Category To fields - Indictaes the products to be handled by loan collections module (for LD/PD/AA)
- Inactives Notes - Gives a free text filed definition to enter the reason for a collection item becoming inactive and this will be updated on the Collection Item after the inactivity period has passed.
- Hist Notes - Holds any note on collection Items that have moved to History. It is a free-text field.
- Aa Od Balance and Aa Os Balance - Indicates the virtual balance type used to calculate the total outstanding overdue amount of AA Loan and the total outstanding Loan balance amount of AA loan respectively.
- Category code for the overdraft current account to be selected for the overdue processing is defined in the Category From field in CL.PARAMETER .
- Cat Ovd Bal Type - The value in this field has to be a valid record from AC.BALANCE.TYPE or can be blank. This balance type is used to calculate the total outstanding overdue amount of contracts defined within Category From – To range
- Cat Os Bal Type - The value in this field has to be a valid record from AC.BALANCE.TYPE or can be blank. This balance type is used to calculate the total outstanding balance amount of contracts defined within Category From – To range The balance types defined in the fields have to be applicable for the category range defined. There are validations to make sure that the Category From and Category To fields are input and are in range.
- Currency Conversion Rate Type - Indicates the rate which the system has to pick from the currency table for conversion purposes. It can be BUY.RATE or SELL.RATE or MID.RATE (default value). This is used in the collection application for arriving at the local currency equivalent amounts in case of delinquent or past due foreign currency contracts. The exchange rate in CL.COLLECTION.ITEM is updated for new contracts only. This does not work for existing contracts.

The collectors are given incentives (in form of points which can be transformed to cash) based on their performance and achievement of predefined targets.

External agencies are given commission based on amounts recovered and pulled out items against salary assignment.

Incentive calculation for the collectors’ activity is done only if collection activities exceed more than mentioned for each collector.

The incentive strategy can be set separately for each by assigning it to in CL.COLLECTOR table’s Incentive Strategy field.

- Trgt Main Act - Gives the number of main actions required as target for the collector and Trgt Pts Mact gives number of incentive points allocated to collector if the target main actions are exceeded.
- Factor Main Act - Indicates the number of main actions over the target to be considered as an extra unit. Points Maction is number of points to allocate to collector per extra unit of main actions.
- Trgt Prod Maction - Indicates the number of productive outcomes related to main actions required as target for the collector.
- Trgt Pts Pro Mact - Indicates the number of incentive points allocated to collector if the target productive outcomes related to main actions is reached.
- Prod Maction - Indicates the number of productive outcomes related to main actions over the target to be considered as an extra unit.
- Prod Mact Points - Indicates the number of points to allocate to the collector per extra unit of productive outcomes related to main actions.
- Number of other actions (other than main action) required as target for the collector is Trgt Others Act which has incentive points if achieved as in Trgt Pts Oaction . The number of other actions over target for additional unit is Factor Other Act .
- Pts Other Action gives number of points to allocate to collector per extra unit of other actions.
- Trgt Prod Oact gives number of productive outcomes related to other actions (other than main action) required as target for the collector , incentive points if target achieved is Trgt Pts Pro Oact . For extra units over target number of productive outcome is indicated as Factor Pro Oact .
- Pts Prod Oaction gives number of points to allocate to collector per extra unit of productive outcomes related to other actions.
- Target points for Promise to pay is given in Trgt No Ptp and the incentive points if target achieved is indicated in Trgt Pts Ptp . Factor Ptp gives number of PTP over the target to be considered as an extra unit. Pts Unit Ptp number of points to allocate to collector per extra unit of PTP
- Trgt Ptp Amt for Total PTP amount target and incentive points as given in Trgt Ptp Amt Pts ; Factor for extra points Factor Ptp Amt and additional points for extra units Pts Unit Ptp Amt.
- Trgt No Kptp gives Target for collectors number of KPTP (kept promise to pay) and incentive points that would be allocated on achieving it Trgt Pts Kptp .
- Factor Kptp gives Number of KPTP over the target to be considered as an extra unit with Pts Unit Kptp number of points to allocate to collector per extra unit of KPTP. Trgt Kptp Amt is Total KPTP amount to be achieved by collector as target. Trgt Kptp Amt Pts is number of incentive points allocated to collector if the target KPTP amount is reached. Factor Kptp Amt gives KPTP amount over the target to be considered as an extra unit and Pts Unit Kptp Amt number of points to allocate to collector per extra unit of KPTP amount

The record is used for reporting purposes and calculating incentive points.

It stores bucket information of a customer. This record is updated automatically online for each action performed by the collector and during end of day batch for actions generated by the system. The details of this record are as follows.

The records of CL.COLLECTION.ITEM get updated during online and COB processing. It contains the details of collection items, including due details, customer details and loan details. The table is also used to capture the required details for loan collection.

The CL.COLLECTION.ITEM table gets updated when a borrower defaults on his scheduled loan repayment(s). In the latter event, the Queue field is allotted in accordance with the CL.QUEUE parameterisation on a first come, first serve basis.

The attributes below to support collections of foreign currency loans in AA and PD and record outcomes in foreign currencies.

- Lcy OS Amount - Represents the outstanding amount in local currency.
- Amount Exchange Rate - Converts the amount to local currency.
- Out Due Ccy - Specifies the outcome currency.

- Out Ex Rate - Denotes the exchange rate which converts the outcome amount in local currency.

- Ptp Paid Amt Lcy - Represents the PTP paid amount in local currency.

##### Key Tables and Files

The Key Tables and Files for the collection process are as follows:


##### Collection and Recovery

Collections and Recovery are two terms, which are used interchangeably.

It includes collecting payments from those who are delinquent or who have defaulted on their contractual commitments, that is, those who make payments later than their contractual due date.

It involves the collection of money owed on accounts after the financial institution has classified the account as non-performing or has written off the debt as a loss. The recovery or collection processes help banks to preserve the quality of customer loan portfolio and prevent loss of revenue.

The detailed navigational steps are shown below.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic helps the user to understand the Collections process in Temenos Transact .


##### Collection Processing in Temenos Transact

When a borrower defaults on his scheduled repayment of a loan, the unpaid items follows an overdue ageing process. A collection item record is created for each customer and contains all overdue loans of the given customer, irrespective of the type of loan. Collection cases are assigned to different collection queues and the user with supervisory permissions can assign the collection cases to Callers or Field Executives working for the queue. Collectors can act upon their work list and record their activities for further follow up or resolution.


##### Collection Strategies

A universal collection strategy cannot be applied to all customers. Collection strategies can be devised considering the customer and debt classifications. The criteria may be customer’s occupation, age, gender, residential status, overdue status of loan, overdue amount, and total loan outstanding, bucket classification, etc.

When a collector pulls an item from a queue for follow up (no other collector should work on the same customer before it is released by the first collector), the worked record has to be stamped with a pre-defined action code and an outcome code describing the activity of the collector and the result of the action respectively. Some outcome codes can automatically generate an outcome code at a future point; for example a PTP can generate a KPTP or BPTP outcome code.

Based on the outcome code, the worked record has to be re-queued in the same queue but with different priority or to be transferred to another queue for further action, that is, PTP , transfer to field collection, external agencies or no further action to be taken status.


##### Collection Teams

Temenos Transact terms collections teams as Queue Types. For example, tele-collection, field-collection and external agency can be queue types of the bank’s collection department. These teams can be internal or external to the bank.


##### Collection Groups

Collection groups can be formed within collection teams. The criteria for forming these homogeneous groups can be defined as per the bank’s policy. For instance, the bank can form a tele-collection queue for staff, tele-collection queue for retail customers, and tele-collection queue for corporate employees, etc. If a collection case matches the criteria set for more than one queue, it is assigned to the queue that has the top priority.


##### External Agencies

A master for external collection can be maintained within Temenos Transact . The following details of the agency can be recorded in the master.

- Agency owner’s name
- Date of contract
- Branch details
- Commission scale

Commission to agencies can be a fixed percentage of the payment obtained for the month. A scale of commission can be applied to salary assignments obtained by the agencies.


##### Collector Types and Collectors

Tele-collectors and field-executives working for collections or recoveries department of the bank and external agencies, can be recorded as collector types in Temenos Transact . The follow-up actions permitted and the queues on which each type of collector can work are user-definable.

Individual collectors are mapped to the broad classification (Collector Types). The collectors can be associated with multiple queues and may be internal or external to the bank. The contact details of the collector and incentive strategy applicable can be specified.


##### Incentive Strategy

Different incentive strategies can be framed for different collection queues and linked to the collectors working for the queue. Incentives can be based on the collection efforts and results (outcome) achieved by the collectors for the month. In Temenos Transact collections, this serves to encourage positive outcomes for collection cases and minimise non-repayment of loans.


##### Dunning and Possible Results

Dunning or collection activities can be defined for each type of collector. In Temenos Transact , these are termed as Main Actions. A few sample main actions are:

- Inward Telephone Calls (CALLI)
- Outward Telephone Calls (CALLO)
- Field Visits (VISIT)
- Dunning Letters

Possible results of dunning process are defined as Outcome in Temenos Transact . Sample outcomes are:

- Promise to pay (PTP)
- Consent to negotiate
- Consent to meet in person
- Next call scheduled
- Salary assignment (ASAL)

These are the result of actions performed by the collectors. Hence, the actions which can result in an outcome are parameterised for each outcome. For instance, Promise to Pay may be a result of inward or outward telephone calls, field visits or dunning letters. The outcomes are also linked to the collection queues. For instance, Settlement is a result of the Visit action and it can be associated to the Field Collection queue.

The Temenos Transact Collections hierarchy is depicted below.

The collector's activities and outcomes are shown below.

Where,

- PTP – Promise to Pay
- MS – Meeting Scheduled
- PPTP – Partially Kept Promise to Pay

When the collector contacts the customer through an outward telephone call, the customer’s response is recorded in the CL.COLLECTION.ITEM application. So, to clear the due bills the customer promises to pay (PTP) a specific amount which can be an amount equal to, less than or greater than Tot Overdue Amt .

When the customer promises to pay an excess amount greater than the Tot Overdue Amt , the system allows them to do so. It also indicates this by raising suitable overrides. The related OVERRIDE application’s records are:

CL-OUT.DUE.AMT.LCY.GT.TOT.DUE.AMT - When the outcome due amount local currency is greater than the total overdue amount, the system fetches the override message from this record. CL-PTP.AMT.GT.OD.AMT - When the PTP amount is greater than the overdue amount, the system fetches the override message from this record. CL-PTP.AMT.LCY.GT.OD.AMT.LCY - When the local currency PTP amount is greater than the local currency overdue amount, the system fetches the override message from this record.

If the user prefers to restrict the excess PTP amount and allow it to be only up to Tot Overdue Amt , then these overrides can be set as Type = Error in the OVERRIDE application.

The below screenshot shows the override displayed when the PTP Outcome Due Amt Lcy amount captured is greater than Tot Overdue Amt .

When a PTP is recorded in the system with a due date and amount, the module automatically tracks the payment and updates the status as Kept Promise to Pay, if the payment is received in full; PPTP if the payment is partially received; BPTP if not paid.

There are further actions that can be taken once the PTP has been done. If the customer calls the bank and wants to arrange an increase or a decrease in his or her promise to pay this option is also available:

Where,

- IPTP - Increased Promise to Pay
- RPTP - Reduced Promise to Pay


##### Non-PTP Related Outcomes

There are outcomes that generate automatically if no PTP has been entered for a collection. These are titled SPAY and IDLE.

It refers to Self-Payment, which is when a customer has a delinquent contract but chooses to make a payment towards that contract before (or without) any contact was made to arrange a PTP. The system updates the amount they repaid automatically in the collection item, with the outcome being SPAY. When the customer pays the entire amount, the collection item disappears from the collections work list. When they pay a partial amount, the item is still shown as outstanding and is deemed workable.

It refers to an Inactive collection item. This outcome code displays for the item when it has not been worked for a certain number of days (the amount of days is configurable). This allows the collection items that have possibly been overlooked or left dormant to display the IDLE outcome. This allows the supervisor or collector to sort through their work list and highlight items that have been left un-worked.

#### 📖 Introduction

The LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS application enables the user to set-up bills, which the bank has discounted or passed on to a third party for rediscounting.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

On the LD transaction, the Bill Number In multi-value field is used to record one or more bills, which have been accepted for discounting or offered for rediscounting. Before the user can use this facility, one or more bills must exist on the BILL.REGISTER file.


##### Bills - Use in Loans and Deposits

Discounting and Re-discounting of bills is performed in the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS application. Before transactions involving bills can be entered, two LMM.CHARGE.CONDITIONS codes should be defined for the booking of profit and loss from re-discounting.

These codes must be added to the LMM.INSTALL.CONDS record in the Bill Chg Code field. The profit code must be value 1 and the loss code must be value 2.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section details the process of discounting and re-discounting bills.


##### Bill Register

Before the user can record a bill with the LD application, the basic details of the bill must exist within the BILL.REGISTER . The following screenshot illustrates how a bill may be recorded:

The above screenshot indicates that Keizo Saji expects to receive a sum of USD 1,000,000 from Hiroshi Yamauchi on 16th August 2004.

Once the bill has been entered and authorised, it becomes eligible for acceptance by either a third party or a particular organisation. Entering a valid customer ID into the Acceptor field indicates acceptance by a third party. Leaving that field blank indicates that the bill is eligible for acceptance by the organisation.

Read the Miscellaneous Deals user guide to know details on how to accept a bill.


##### Bills Discounting

The LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS application enables the user to record details of bills, which the organisation has agreed to discount on behalf of a customer. This option is available whether or not the organisation or a third party has accepted a bill. However the bill must exist on the BILL.REGISTER .

A separate version in LD is provided to enable the setting-up of a bill, which has been accepted for discount.

The above screenshot illustrates the means by which the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS application records the details of bills, which have been accepted for discount.

The Bill Number field is used to record the ID of a bill, which must exist on the BILL.REGISTER file. The user may enter the ID directly into that field or may invoke the drop-down list facility while in the Bill Number field of the version. Select the bill, which is to be discounted, complete the LD and enter it into the system in the normal way.

However, the process of selecting bills for discount has been designed to run from an enquiry. The enquiry is used to obtain a selection of like bills, which can be bundled together for discounting collectively. Once the selection is on view, the bills can be selected and loaded into an appropriate LD contract for the user.

This is achieved by first invoking the BILLS.DISCOUNT enquiry. When the required selection criteria has been made, running the enquiry presents with a list of those bills which are recorded on the BILL.REGISTER file and are available for discount by the organisation. A bill must first be flagged Y in the Discount field before it can be selected for discounting.

The BILLS.DISCOUNT enquiry checks for these values and only displays those bills, which meet the correct criteria as illustrated in the screenshot below:

Having obtained the list of those bills, which are available for discounting, there is a need to select the particular record for which the user may prefer to view or record the discount rate within the LD application.

Select the particular bill for viewing, which has been accepted for discounting. Do this by clicking the VIEW button over the particular item on the list.

However, if this particular bill is to be discounted, then clicking the Discount Bill button automatically invokes the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS application and add the bill to the Bill Number field.

The enquiry then populates the LD transaction with the Bill Register details, leaving the user to complete the transaction. How much the user needs to complete here depends upon whether the user tailored the version (as shown above) to default such information as category, interest rate (that is, the discount rate) and grace period.

A bill discounting transaction is recorded in the same way as a discounted loan; the amount paid for the discount is the sum of the bill amount less a discount amount. The discount amount is the sum of the bills multiplied by the discount rate for the remaining term of the bill.

The discount amount is amortised over the remaining term of the bill.

The LD module provides bill-bundling facilities so the user can select a parcel of bills all having the same currency and the same liability customer so that they can be discounted collectively under one single LD contract. A batch of bills can be assigned a batch number through input of the Batch No field. If NEW is entered into this field, a batch number gets automatically assigned.

The following screenshot illustrates how a typical bundle of bills are recorded within the LD application:

These particular bills all share the same maturity date, currency and customer and therefore may be bundled into a single LD contract so that they are discounted collectively.

A bill discounting transaction may be terminated prematurely by changing the maturity date of the loan transaction. The maturity date of the bill is updated in the BILL.REGISTER by the system.


##### Bills Re-discounting

The LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS module is also able to process bills which, having already been accepted for discounting, and then offered to another third party for re-discounting.

A separate LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS version for re-discounting is provided for processing the re-discount of a bill, or bundles of bills.

The various steps that the user should perform are exactly the same as those he must carry out in order to record a bill accepted for discount. The only exception being that the user has to use the BILLS.REDISCOUNT enquiry.

This enquiry locates those bills that have already been discounted and are therefore available for re-discounting.

These too may be selected and placed into an LD contract in the normal way, thereby creating a deposit taken as the re-discount proceeds are received.

When the bills are re-discounted, the transaction is booked as a deposit with a zero interest rate. A re-discount rate must be supplied, which is used to calculate the amount to receive for the discount. The amount to receive is calculated as the sum of bills less the sum of the bills multiplied by the re-discount rate for the remaining life of the bills.

The action of re-discounting a bill results in a profit or loss on the original discount, this is calculated as the sum of the bill multiplied by the difference between the discount rate and the re-discount rate for the remaining period of the bill. This amount is taken as a charge or fee in the Chrg Amount fields, together with a CHRG.CODE identified in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS in the Bill Chg Code field.

Even after the bill is re-discounted and profit or loss crystallised, both the loan (discount) and the deposit (re-discount) transactions continue to be accounted for until the maturity of the bill. However, there may be cases where the re-discounting is done on a without recourse basis, that is, the bank may want the loan and the deposit transactions to be removed from its books on the date of re-discount. For this purpose, the Red Recourse field is set to YES or NO.

- If flagged to YES, the re-discount transaction is treated as with recourse and both the loan and deposit continue in the books of the bank till maturity of the bill.
- If flagged to NO on the value date of re-discounting, both the asset and liability contracts are matured.


##### Impact of Limits by Re-discounting a Bill

When a bill is re-discounted, there is no longer any risk to the bank. In order to reflect this, the limit updated by the original discount of the bill(s) should be backed out. A BILL.LIMIT.AMOUNT subroutine, has been provided which recalculates the exposure for a bundle of discounted bills so that only those, which have not been re-discounted, are included.

This routine should be added to the LIMIT.REFERENCE record as the reference of discounted bills in the Limit Subroutine field.


##### Bill History

The results of discounting and re-discounting a bill can be seen in the BILL.REGISTER record.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Bills Discounted and Rediscounted feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Bills Discounted and Rediscounted feature.

### 3.3  Interest Assessment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Loans can have two interest calculation methods, interest bearing payable in arrears and discounted type payable upfront. The former is a standard method of interest payment, where interest is receivable at the end of an interest period. The latter, discounted type, is interest paid at the start of ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accrual Parameter*, *Capitalisation*, *Interest Basis*, *Interest Rate*, *Interest Spread*, *Liquidation Mode*, *Nab Start Date*, *Negative Rates* ... +10 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Loans can have two interest calculation methods, interest bearing payable in arrears and discounted type payable upfront. The former is a standard method of interest payment, where interest is receivable at the end of an interest period. The latter, discounted type, is interest paid at the start of the interest period. The interest calculation is the same as for an arrears interest type, and is not calculated using yield style calculation. Negative rates are also supported.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

For discount interest calculation using yield method, by flagging the Yield Method field in LD to YES, the interest is calculated using the yield method in place of a straight discount. The amortisation of such discount is done based on an effective rate for the respective period over the life of the deal, and also taking into account the grace period.


##### Negative Interest Rates

For both loans and deposits, if the Negative Rates field is flagged to YES, a negative rate can be input in the Interest Rate field. It accepts values YES, NO or Null and is an input field after first authorisation. The default value is Null (with the same meaning as NO). YES is not permitted in the following cases:

- Discounted contract ( Payment Method For Interest is set to 2)
- The Interest Basis field set to S (special) that is, direct input of interest amounts
- Annuity type contracts
- The Capitalisation field set to YES
- Contract with a value in Tax Interest Key field, that is, contracts with interest tax
- Rediscount contracts
- Commitment contracts (category range 21095-21099)

If set to YES, input of positive, zero and negative rates are allowed with the following restrictions:

Negative interest rates can be input in the following fields:

- Interest Rate (Fixed)
- Interest Rate
- New Interest Rate (during amendments)
- Negative interest rates can be input in the Interest Rate field of LD.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION .
- Negative interest rates can be input when defining type R schedules.

During amendments, the New Spread field can accept a negative value even if the resulting interest rate is negative.

For floating rate contracts, where the rate from PERIODIC.INTEREST or BASIC.INTEREST plus the value input in the Interest Spread field gives a negative rate, results in an error where, negative rates is set to NO. PERIODIC.INTEREST and BASIC.INTEREST may not allow the direct input of negative rates, but negative contract rates can occur as the result of adding a negative spread. For the YES option, Liquidation Mode field can only be set to AUTOMATIC.

Interest that is accrued till date from the previous capitalisation or interest schedule date can be repaid by the customer on an ad-hoc basis. In this case, the user has to enter the date (not prior to last capitalisation date or the value set in the Nab Start Date field) in the Online Eff Date field . The Online Rpy Type field should be set to I and the Online Rpy Amt is automatically populated by the system and is a display-only field. The system defaults the accrued interest as of the date specified in the Online Eff Date field.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes the topics related to interest assessment.


##### Interest Accruals

Interest on an LD deal is calculated for the period of the deal, from value date to maturity date.

Normal interest calculation includes the first and not the last date. However, the user can override the normal interest calculation and accruals by setting the Accrual Parameter field. This field is available in the LD.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION table and LD transaction to define different rules for loans and deposits (if so desired), which the system defaults on to the deal. The system defaults the changeable value at the deal level and generates an override in case of any change.

The values in the field should be a valid record from the EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM table, which is shown below.

The above example shows the interest accrual rules for the Japanese RYOHA style of interest. This particular parameter defines that the number of days of interest should include both the first and the last days. If any repayment is done, then the next interest period starts from Repayment Date + 1.

The EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM table allows the user to also define whether a routine is to be used, include Start Date or not, include Last Day or not. Furthermore, + or - adjustment of no days can be specified for principal increase or decrease.

The Rounding Rule field at contract level allows the user to define the rule used in rounding underwriting fee, facility fee, interest and charge amounts calculations apart from rounding rules specified at currency level. This, the system can be default from the LD.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION for the category. However if no rounding rule is specified by the user or the system, then the rounding rule given in EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM , if exists, is used. Else, the rules at currency level takes precedence.

When a contract follows the RFR compound or simple rate calculation method, RFR requires a daily interest rate reset. Each business day contract receives or calculates the new rate for the current interest period, and the daily interest accrual amount is calculated using the below formulae.


##### Online Repayment of Interest

For the below LD contract, interest has been accrued from 15th Dec till date. (Current date being 24th Dec 2010).

On 24th Dec 2010, the user has provided online principal repayment and the system has calculated the payment amount as $ 4.50.

The enquiry schedule displays repayment of accrued interest on 24th Dec and adjusted the next payment amount.


##### Interest Settlement during Extension of Loan

For example, a one-month contract is due to mature in three days and the client wishes to extend it for a further month.

The bank provides a new rate for the extension; settle the interest from the clients’ account and advise the client of the extension.

To adjust the contract to meet this criteria, the amendment fields on the LD contract are used to set the new rate; change the maturity date to the new date, and specify the settlement of interest on the old maturity date as well as on the new maturity (on the Schedule Define screen).

> **⚠️ Note:** If the contract is extended without defining an interest schedule for the old maturity date, then the committed interest changes and settle on the new maturity date.


##### Capitalising Interest

If interest is to be capitalised for all future interest settlements (apart from at Maturity), then the user can set the Capitalisation field to Y. In this case, there is no need to effect a principal increase for the interest amount.

The user can modify the Capitalisation field at a later stage following initial input. This allows greater flexibility in the case of any necessary future amendments to the contract, any mistakes on input to this field, or LD contract was first entered.

### 3.4  Lease


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Leasing functionality involves hiring out an equipment or vehicle between two parties. The contract involves a fixed rental value to be paid over the tenor of the lease. The lease rentals are repaid as annuity type payment amounts over a specified period. This can be either Begin (payable at the beg...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Annuity Pay Method*, *Annuity Repayment*, *Residual Value*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Leasing functionality involves hiring out an equipment or vehicle between two parties. The contract involves a fixed rental value to be paid over the tenor of the lease. The lease rentals are repaid as annuity type payment amounts over a specified period. This can be either Begin (payable at the beginning of the payment period) or End (payable at the end of the payment period) type. The Loans and Deposits (LD) module supports creating and maintaining above lease contracts. The system supports recording of any associated charges or insurance premium payments.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There are three fields available in the LD contract, which support the Leasing functionality:

- Annuity Pay Method – This field specifies the annuity payment method. The valid values are: BEGIN – Payment is due at the beginning of the period. END – Payment is due at the end of the period.
- Residual Value – This field specifies, if applicable, the residual value of a leasing contract. If a residual value applies, then it must be greater than zero, (less than zero for a deposit) and less than the amount to be financed.
- Annuity Repayment – This field records the annuity repayment amount. It is a no-input field and is completed by the system.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following screenshot illustrates how an LD version can be written to enable the input and recording of a 12-month automobile lease having no residual value at the end of the lease term.


##### Leasing Schedule Types

A schedule type A indicates that the underlying transaction is an annuity type agreement in the LD.SCHEDULE.DEFINE schedule definition screen.

The A schedule defines the regular annuity repayment amount. The associated amount may be entered or calculated using the standard annuity repayment calculation if entered. The amount of principal and interest to be repaid for each monthly repayment is calculated by Temenos Transact . Only one A schedule may be specified. For a begin type lease contract, the first repayment has to be the same as the contract value (start) date.

The schedule definition screen enables the recording of any associated charges or insurance leasing. Read detailing charges and fees for more information. Once the lease details have been entered into Temenos Transact ; the user can use the supplied LD.BALANCES.SUM enquiry to view the amounts that have been calculated, whether the underlying transaction has been authorised or not.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Lease feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Lease feature.

### 3.5  Loan Commitment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks record the terms and conditions of the agreement between them and the customers, relating to the loan sanctioned as part of the Commitment.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Available Amount*, *Calculation Basis*, *Commitment Type*, *Drawdown End Date*, *Drawdown Start Date*, *Drawings Allowed*, *Reinitiate Commitment Amount*, *Tranche Amount*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks record the terms and conditions of the agreement between them and the customers, relating to the loan sanctioned as part of the Commitment.

- The commitment product can be revolving or non-revolving.
- Fee calculation can be based on the original or unused amount of the commitment amount.
- There can be a grace period at the start and end of the commitment and drawdown amounts against the commitment can be specified.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The category code for Commitment type of contract must be within the following ranges in the Loans and Deposits application:

| Contract Type | Description | Category Range |
|---|---|---|
| COMMITMENT | Commitment | 21095–21099 |

Based on the commitment contracts opened within the range of above categories, drawings (or disbursement of) under the commitment can be effected. There can be single or multiple drawings.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section orients the user on working on a commitment contract.

The following screen shot displays a commitment contract and a drawdown against it as an example loan contract.

> **⚠️ Note:** The start and end dates for fee calculations differ from the contract start and end dates.

The Calculation Basis field can display the following new values:

- TO (Tranche Original)
- TU (Tranche Unused)
- O (Original)
- U (Unused).

If this field is set to TO or TU, then the Drawdown Start Date and Drawdown End Date fields can be multi-valued and individual tranche amount and its validity may be defined. Tranche Amount field defines the amount of each tranche, which is associated to the start and end date fields.

The Commitment Type field displays NC and RC as values. These values determine whether the undrawn residual balance is allowed to be carried forward or not after the expiry of the Drawdown End Date.

If the Calculation Basis field is set to TO, the Available Amount field is updated only on the first Drawdown Start Date and not on Value Date. Loan withdrawal before this date is not possible under the commitment (unless the dates are re-defined in the commitment record). Fee on commitment is based on the value in Available Amount .

If the Calculation Basis field is set to T and the Commitment Type field has a value of either R or N, withdrawal of loan after the expiry of the last Drawdown End Date in the commitment record is not permitted.


##### Commitment Available Amount in LD Revolving

When LD loan under LD revolving commitment contract goes to PD in PR amount type during batch or online, the commitment available amount is not increased.

The commitment available is increased only when LD loan is paid by debiting account or PD, the principal component (PR) has been paid in PD module.

The Reinitiate Commitment Amount field is to be set to YES to enable this functionality.

This field is available to re-initiate commitment when PD repayment is made. This is a display-only field and can be enabled for revolving commitment contract only.

- When this field is set to null and a drawing under a revolving commitment contract is moved to PD, then the commitment amount is reinstated.
- When this field is set to YES, then when a drawing under a revolving commitment contract is moved to PD, the commitment amount is not reinstated. However, when there is a repayment in PD for the Principal amount, then the commitment amount is reinstated.

Following are the features of this field:

- This field can be set as YES or NULL only.
- This field is display-only field.
- This field can be input only for commitment revolving contract.
- For other type of contracts, when input is tried, suitable error message is given by the system.


###### Schedules

If the commitment contract is not drawn against, it is possible to define a series of P schedules using the LD.SCHEDULE.DEFINE screen to,

- Reduce the notional principal amount
- Repay capitalised interest

A commitment can be flagged as a non-drawable commitment by setting the Drawings Allowed field to NO. This can be used where the commitment is updated manually to mirror the effect of contracts, which are associated with the commitment, though are not linked through the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS application.

When LD loan under LD revolving commitment contract goes to PD in PR amount type during batch or online, the commitment available amount is not increased.

The commitment available is increased only when LD loan is paid by debiting account or PD, PR has been paid in PD module.

Whenever PRIN.INCREASE is done in LD LOAN contract, the balance in the account is checked and depending upon the availability of funds, appropriate override message is generated. Under no circumstances, PD record is created or updated for PRIN.INCREASE operation.

The principal decrease in LD contract does not generate or update PD contract. Instead, irrespective of the liquidation mode, if balance is available in the liquidation account STMT.ENTRY is generated. If not, suitable override message is given by the system.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Define Commitments

A new loan arrangement can be created as a commitment to the customer. The loan commitment is a contingent arrangement with the customer and becomes non-contingent upon disbursal. The term and amount of loan sanctioned can be updated in the Term Amount Property Class of the loan arrangement to indicate the loan commitment.

In the Loan Commitment Feature, the user can perform the below activities:

|  | Authorise/Delete Commitment . |
| List of Unauthorised Commitments | Click the Authorise icon corresponding to a record. |
| Authorise/Delete Commitment | Click the Authorise icon. |

### 3.6  Loan Creation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The LD module caters to the different types of loans that each bank can offer to its customers. Alternative VERSION records and advices allows the user to set specific loan types using the category codes on the system to reflect the different products.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Comm Fee Liq Acct*, *Int Payment Method*, *Int Rate Type*, *Interest Rate*, *Prin Ben Bank*, *RFR Convention*, *RFR Decimals* ... +7 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The LD module caters to the different types of loans that each bank can offer to its customers. Alternative VERSION records and advices allows the user to set specific loan types using the category codes on the system to reflect the different products.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The bank can create specific loan types using the category codes on the system to reflect different products. These can be reported by the category code in the bank’s General Ledger.


##### Configuring Risk Free Rates Contracts

Temenos Transact supports various risk-free rates irrespective of currency and publication time. To enable the processing of Risk-Free Rates (RFRs), the bank must configure the following tables.


###### LMM.INSTALL.CONDS

The user has to configure the following RFR related fields in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS for accurate rate calculation, according to the bank’s preferences.

| Field | Function |
|---|---|
| RFR Convention | Specifies the market convention for rate compounding or averaging. The LD application follows the lookback convention. |
| RFR Lookback Type | Specifies the type of lookback method applied for rate compounding or averaging. Types for rate calculations are: Narrow Definition - Uses the original interest period day count with lookback rate. If the Wednesday's rate is used for Friday, apply Friday’s weight (three days) to Wednesday’s rate. Observation Shift - Uses the original day count of the lookback rate. If the Wednesday's rate is used for Friday, apply Wednesday’s weight (one day) to Wednesday’s rate. |
| RFR Calc Method | Specifies the calculation method for RFR averaging. It can be: Compound Simple |
| RFR Spread Treatment | Specifies the spread treatment method during the RFR averaging: Spread-Inclusive - Uses the spread within the averaging calculation along with daily rates. Spread-Exclusive - Adds the spread separately after RFR averaging is done. |
| RFR Period Day Count | Specifies the treatment of the last available RFR in the rate averaging process. It allows the following values: Full - Last RFR with day weightage, which is applicable for the entire current interest period. Today - Last RFR with its original day weightage, which is applicable till the current business day. |
| RFR Decimals | Specifies the rounding value applied for RFR |


###### LD.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION

The LD application also allows defining RFR related fields for a specific product category. Thesystem defaulte the values on to the LD contract and are changeable at the contract level. Banks can configure the additional RFR Lookback Days field along with other RFR fields defined in LMM.INSTALL.CONDS table for rate calculation.

| Field | Function |
|---|---|
| RFR Lookback Days | Specifies the number of lookback days considered for RFR calculations. |


#### 🔧 Working With

The example below illustrates a simple loan contract using the drawdown against a commitment. The LD module allows for much more complex stand-alone loans, which can display payment schedules, interest settlement frequencies, rate change frequencies, LIBOR or base rate options as well as discounted product types.

The above screenshot displays the drawing under a commitment using the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS,DRW version.

The above screenshot displays the discounted loan input using the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSIT version, ADL with Yield Method field as No.

The above screenshot displays discounted loan input using the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS,ADL with the Yield Method field as Yes.

Examples of a discounted loan with different Yield Method are also displayed, which highlights the different version records accommodate the banks differing requirements.

> **⚠️ Note:** The calculation of interest is performed different manner, which is due to grace period considered during yield computation.

When the Yield Method field is set to Yes, the value in the Amount field is taken as the repayment amount (or the bill face value, if a bill is discounted). The amount to be disbursed to the customer (net amount) is arrived at using the following formula,

- I = rate entered in the Interest Rate field
- N = number of days between the Value Date and the FIN.MATE.DATE (grace period does not form part of this period)
- X = the denominator of the interest basis used

- Amount = 1,000,000
- Value date = June1st, 2003
- Final maturity date = July 1st, 2003
- Interest rate = 10%
- Interest basis = B (366/360)
- Grace period = 5 days
- Yield method = YES
- N = 30 days (exclusive of grace period) but 35 with grace period

Using the formula given above, the net amount (inclusive of grace amount) is

- =1,000,000 / (1+ (10 * 35)/(360 * 100)) = 990, 371.39
- The total interest amount is 1,000,000 less 990,371.39 = 9628.61 (inclusive of grace period interest)

The effective rate is calculated using 35 days =

- 9628.61 * 360 * 100 / 1000000 * 35 * 10 = 9.90371%

The grace period interest is therefore = 1,000,000 * 9.90371 * 5 / 360 = 1,375.52

Therefore the total interest ( Tot Interest Amt field) after factoring in the grace period works out to 8264.46 + 1377.41, which is 9,641.87


##### Draw down in a Currency other than Deal Currency

Draw down can be made from or to an account, which can be denominated in a currency other than the deal currency. While inputting a discounted LD deal, interest or commission can be collected or paid upfront in a currency other than the deal currency. Similarly, charges can be collected in any currency.


##### Liquidation in a Currency other than Deal Currency

The liquidation amount can flow from or to an account, which can be denominated in a currency other than the deal currency. A facility is also available in the Settlement Rates table for the user to define an exchange rate to be used for conversion while handling liquidation in a different currency.


##### Increasing or Decreasing the Principal

As described in the Capitalising Interest section, it is possible to affect an increase in conjunction with the rollover. It is also possible to affect a decrease instead of an increase if the client only wished to roll part of the outstanding principal. The decrease must be entered as a repayment schedule on the Schedule Define screen.

The above screenshot displays the Increasing principle using the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSIT,CEMAL version.


##### Creating Risk Free Rate Contracts

At the time of RFR contract creation, risk-free related field values default to loan contracts from the RFR fields specified in LD.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION or LMM.INSTALL.CONDS tables. The system allows changing the default values at the contract level.

The LD application follows the Lookback market convention to arrive at the RFR applicable for the interest period. Hence, each business day, the contract receives a new rate for the interest period. The accrual amounts for each working day are calculated based on the latest rate.

The LMM.ACCOUNT.BALANCES table stores the accrual ladder for the current interest period with the amount accrued and rate applied for each accrual cycle. Average RFR changes every business day once a new rate is available.

An RFR contract can be created only when the below conditions are fulfilled.

- Int Payment Method = 1 ( Interest Bearing Contracts)
- Int Rate Type = 2 (Periodic Automatic)


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Set Up Project Loan
- Manage Early Maturity (LD)

This feature is used to enter Loan deals, usually specifies the principal amount of money borrowed, the interest rate the lender is charging, date of repayment, settlement accounts for settling the dues of installment and charges. Most of the values are defaulted from the relevant product conditions.


##### Workflow

In the Loan Creation feature, the user can perform the below activities:

A Corporate Loan provides an extensive range of processing in relation to the physical extension of credit to a borrower. This type of loan contract can be either a BULLET or AMORTising contract. For a BULLET contract ,the only events are initial draw-down and maturity. There are no other scheduled events (apart from payments linked to the draw-down and maturity). A contract of this type can be entered using Auto Schedules set to YES. An AMORTising contract has other scheduled events apart from initial draw-down and maturity.

Other features of Corporate Loan is listed below:

- Interest rate can be fixed or floating
- Interest is collected at the end of the period
- For loans other than with annuity repayment, it is possible to specify that interest can be collected only to the extent of the principal amount repaid.
- Charges, Fees and Commissions can be collected on the contract at different time periods.

To create a Corporate Loan, follow the below steps:

1. Corporate Loans .
2. In the Corporate Loans screen, enter values in the following fields: Customer Id Currency Loan Amount Loan Start Date Loan Maturity Date Loan Product Interest Rate (Fixed)
3. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
4. Click the Commit icon.

A Discounted Loan is one in which the interest is collected from the customer upfront and hence the amount disbursed is less the total interest due. This type of loan can be used to record discounting of bills and acceptances.

Other features Discounted Loan is listed below:

- Interest rate is normally fixed. Floating interest rate can be specified, if required.
- Discount (Interest) to be deducted upfront is normally calculated on a straight line basis. By flagging the Yield Method field to YES, interest may be calculated on Yield basis in place of a straight discount.
- Normally, these are bullet type of loans, that is, the principal amount is payable at maturity. Temenos Transact allows specification of schedules on these loans, if required.
- Charges and Commissions can be collected on these loans.

To create a Discounted Loan (Acceptance, Bills), follow the below steps:

1. Discounted Loan (Bills, Acceptances, etc.) .
2. In the Input Discounted Loan screen, enter values in the following fields: Customer ID Currency Loan Amount Business Day Def Loan Start Date Loan Maturity Date Interest Rate (Fixed)
3. Click the Account Details tab and enter a value in the Prin Ben Bank field.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

Commitment loan product is used to record a Credit Line where the drawdown has to be done within a fixed period and/or in tranches and a fee is charged for the commitment amount.

Features of this type of loan product is listed below:

- It can be either revolving or non-revolving, that is, may or may not allow amounts that have been repaid to be re-drawn.
- Fee calculation can be based on the original or the unused amount of the committed amount.
- Draw-down can be in tranches and the multiples in which draw-down is allowed, can be stipulated.
- There can be a grace period at the start and end of the commitment.

To create an Input Commitment, follow the below steps:

1. Input Commitment .
2. In the Input of Commitment screen, enter values in the following fields: Customer ID Currency Commitment Amount Business Day Def Commitment Start Date Commitment End Date Commitment Fee Rate
3. In the Int, Schd and Tranche Dets tab, enter a value in the Comm Fee Liq Acct field.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

Loan under a Commitment is essentially the same as a Corporate Loan, the only difference is that the user has to enter the commitment contract number under which the loan is to be drawn.

To create a Loan under Commitment, follow the below steps:

1. Loan Under Commitment (Project Loans) .
2. In the Drawings under Commitment screen, enter values in the following fields: Customer ID Currency Loan Amount Loan Start Date Loan Maturity Date Loan Product Commitment Ref Interest Rate (Fixed)
3. Click the Account Details tab and enter a value in the Prin Ben Bank field.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

This section displays the following enquiries:

Model bank supports amendment and reversal (cancellation) of other loans, such as, Corporate loans, Discounted Loans and Loans under Commitment.

The following are allowed while amending these loans -

- Increase or decrease the Principal.
- Change the interest rate for a fixed interest loan and the spread for a floating rate loan.
- Extend or reduce the maturity date of the loan.
- Re-schedule Principal, Interest and Commission schedules.
- Modify the Principal, Interest and Charge Liquidation accounts.

There are specific exclusions to the above amendments depending on certain field settings, which is available in the field help text.

Partial repayments cannot be made in corporate loans, discounted loans and loans drawn under commitment. We can do the same only by using the principal decrease functionality. The reversal (cancellation) of a contract is possible only if no schedule is processed.

To amend a loan, follow the below steps:

1. Amend/ Reverse-Loans .
2. Click the Amend icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the Amend/Reverse Loans screen, enter values in the following fields: Business Day Def Loan Product Loan Maturity Date Interest Type
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

To reverse a loan, follow the below steps:

1. Amend/ Reverse-Loans .
2. Click the Reverse icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the Amend/Reverse Loans screen, click the Reverse icon.

Online Repayment is a new functionality whereby the borrower can make an online ad hoc repayment of principal or principal and interest at any time during the tenor of the loan. However, partial repayment of interest is not allowed. This functionality is available for both Fixed and Call or Notice type of loan contracts and is not supported for Annuity, Discounted, Commitments and deposit type of contracts.

To initiate an online repayment, follow the below steps:

1. Online Repayment .
2. Click the Amend icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the Online Loan Repayment screen, enter values in the following fields: Business Day Def Loan Maturity Date Interest Type
4. In the Account Details tab. enter values in the following fields: Drawdown Account Principal Liq Acct Intt Liq Acct
5. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit icon.

Model Bank supports Early Maturity of Corporate Loans, Discounted Loans and Loans drawn under commitment.

To perform an Early Maturity of a Loan, follow the below steps:

1. Early Maturity Of Loan .
2. Click the Preclose icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the Early Maturity of Loan screen, enter values in the following fields: Maturity Date Principal Liq Acct Interest Liq Acct
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.

Model bank supports manual provisioning on Other Loan types (Corporate loans, Discounted loans and Loans under commitment), if they have been defined in Asset Class Parameter.

If the user decides to maintain the provision manually, then they can use this option to change the provision method to manual. If the provision method is manual then the loan would be skipped for any automatic computation of provision until the field is switched back to AUTO.

To perform Loans under Provisioning, follow the below steps:

1. Loans under Provisioning .
2. Click the Manual Provisioning icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the Manual Provisioning on Loans screen, enter values in the following fields: Limit Reference Liquidation Mode Asset Class Provision %
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Commit icon.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Loan Creation feature.

### 3.7  Loan Maintenance


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The normal amendments or maintenance that the users wish to make on loan contracts, during its lifecycle, can be accommodated in the LD module. Pre-mature closure of contracts may require the change of the interest rate as well as the maturity date itself. Contracts can be extended or amended from, ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Maturity Date*, *Repayment Account*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The normal amendments or maintenance that the users wish to make on loan contracts, during its lifecycle, can be accommodated in the LD module. Pre-mature closure of contracts may require the change of the interest rate as well as the maturity date itself. Contracts can be extended or amended from, call or notice to fixed, or from fixed to call or notice. A number of version records exist to assist the user when making simple or specific changes to a contract, like amending the settlement accounts. The user is given the flexibility to make changes to accommodate the bank's needs, for example, the fact that a rate is fixed does not prevent the user from changing the rate.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

LD supports amendment and reversal (cancellation) of other loans such as Corporate loans, Discounted Loans and Loans under Commitment.

The following are allowed while amending these loans:

- Increasing or decreasing the principal.
- Change the interest rate for a fixed interest loan and the spread for a floating rate loan.
- Extend or reduce the maturity date of the loan.
- Reschedule Principal, Interest and Commission schedules.
- Modify the Principal, Interest and Charge Liquidation accounts.

Partial repayments cannot be made in corporate loans, discounted loans and loans drawn under commitment. This change can be done by using the principal decrease functionality.

The reversal (cancellation) of a contract is possible only if no schedule is processed.

Temenos Transact can make changes to commitment contracts. Also, it does not restrict the user from changing fee rates, maturity dates or amounts. The only exceptions are where drawdowns have been made. In these circumstances, the commitment amount and period cannot be less than the current drawdown amounts and dates.

The LD module allows the common changes users make on loan contracts . Pre-mature closure of contracts require change of the interest rate as well as the maturity date. Contracts can be extended or amended from call or notice to fixed, or from fixed to call or notice. A number of version records exist, which assist the user to make simple or specific changes to a contract (amending settlement accounts). The user has the flexibility to make changes to accommodate the bank's needs. (For example,a fixed rate does not prevent the user from changing the rate).

Using the Sundry Deposit example ,from the previous section, notifications are received confirming that the customer wants the money credited to his recently opened USD savings account. The repayment account and maturity date of the contract has to be changed. The same input version can be used since the only changes required are to the Maturity Date and the Repayment Account fields. The limitations for these changes are that the maturity date must be equal to or greater than today. Since there is no interest element, the effect of the maturity date on the contract is not important. If the bank considers that the credit to the clients account is important, either the FT or DC module should be used to correct the value date for interest purposes on the newly opened savings account.

When the client requires a further extension and the user only amends the Maturity Date field.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Set Up Corporate Loan

The amendments or maintenance of loan contracts can be carried out in LD module. Pre-mature closure of contracts may require a change in the rate of interest and maturity date.
