**Misc**

| S.NO | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account | The Account property class is used by all the products which are account based. This property class primarily controls the description of the account. The ACCOUNT property allows the user to define and control balance treatment, posting restriction, linked account number (for memo accounts), currency market, date convention related setup for the account. Although the account names are account specific, generic titles can be defaulted from the product and can be replaced or given additional detail at the arrangement level. Each product defined and processed in AA can have a single ACCOUNT Property defined. |
| 2 | Activity Charges | The Activity Charges property class defines the charges that have to be applied when a particular activity is triggered on the arrangement. The charges so applied can be made due, capitalised or deferred. The user can enable auto settle the charges made due from unallocated credit balance by setting this to Yes. In accounts, charges are enabled for dormancy, settle payoff and ageing. This property class is also extensively used for all AA related modules, charges are set for various other activities. |
| 3 | Activity Restriction | The Activity Restriction property class is used to specify a restriction on a particular transaction. The restriction rules including the relevant periodic attributes and activities are defined in the product condition. These rules are then used to define activity based or property based restrictions. A rule if broken can be set to result in an override or error. A charge can be attached for this and can be set to be made due, capitalised or deferred. For the AR module, activity restriction is extensively used for restricting transactions by number, type, and so on. This is also extensively used in other modules to restrict the user from doing various user activity based on the life cycle status of contracts. |
| 4 | Balance Availability | The Balance Availability property class allows the user to control the following features pertaining to AR module: Notice amount and period, which needs to be given by a customer for withdrawing money from his account. Default Credit Check and Available Balance update related set up. Activity class or Activity specific credit check, and NSF related fees pertaining to it Tolerance Amount or Tolerance Currency - To indicate the grace amount, which is the allowed overdraft before the bank imposes NSF or OD fees. Overdraft Grace Period - To waive the NSF fee levied on the account, if the customer clears the debit balance within the stipulated grace period. |
| 5 | Dormancy | The Dormancy property class allows the user to control the parameterisation of inactive or dormant accounts and movement of the same into various buckets at the arrangement or product level. The same can be controlled based on period, and some exceptions or rules also can be added for evaluation and movement. The user can include or exclude certain activity or activity class for the evaluation. It is possible to, Configure different Dormancy status based on the period of inactivity Specify different charges and charging frequency for each Dormancy status Apply some exception rule filtering at an individual arrangement level (for example, account is in debit balance) and such rules can either be an API or a rule created using the Rules Engine Specify notices and notice frequency for each Dormancy status Specify Activities or Activity Classes or Activity Initiation Types which are qualified to keep an account active. Auto Reset can be enabled based on status or on Activity Type. |
| 6 | Facility | The Facility is a service component for financial products designed using arrangement architecture. The Facility property class controls the list of available services for an arrangement account. When an external activity (financial or non-financial) is triggered and the corresponding service group is mapped to an activity through Activity Mapping and EB.EVENTS . And the same came allowed or restricted or charged corresponding error message is raised to stop the activity. |
| 7 | Inheritance | The Inheritance property class is used for BN pool structure for inheriting the product conditions set at Parent level arrangement to the Child level arrangement accounts. The product conditions that are set for inheritance are attached to Property records with type as Inheritance Only. The properties to be inherited can be controlled both at source and target level. |
| 8 | Interest | The Interest property class is used for all interest definition and processing in AA. A product defined and processed in AA can have multiple interest properties defined (for example, principal interest, penalty interest, commission, etc. Interest rates can be defined as fixed , floating , periodic or linked rate (referring an INTEREST property from other arrangement), routine based calculation. Tiered interest can also be defined. Further it is possible to define a negative rate, minimum interest amount and waive the interest. Interest adjustment can be done in run time, and adjustment related detail or values can be captured in adjustment related fields. |
| 9 | Limit | The Limit property class primarily controls the use of LIMIT module by the product. We can set up single or shared limit. We can define the LIMIT.REFERENCE applicable for a specific product such that the system defaults the same in an arrangement. For a new limit, at the arrangement level, the LIMIT.SERIAL has to be given as NEW. The AR module can have self-contained secondary limit without having actual limit attached to it. Overdraft status or notice for AR module is handled inside the Limit Property class. Further Limits can be set to use the LIMIT module (AL and AD) or it can be managed only within the arrangement architecture framework. |
| 10 | Payment Schedule | The Payment Schedule property class is used by all products which have amounts billed (that is,made due) or capitalised or Pay. A Payment Schedule can be comprised of one or more payment definitions with conditions such as payment Type and Method, arrangement properties, dates and amounts. The AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application is used to define the standard payment types such as constant, linear, actual and fixed equal and so on, that can be used by a product. This payment type is then attached to each payment schedule definition. The start and end date can be specified, the user can specify the repayment of arrangement to commence after ‘n’ months from the arrangement date or ‘n’ months before the maturity or ‘n’ months after the change product or reset and rollover has happened. |
| 11 | Periodic Charges | The Periodic Charges property class acts as a container to group different charge properties and calculate a periodic charge amount. The Payment Schedule property class drives this property class. A periodic charge property can be attached in payment schedule and on schedule date periodic charge amount is calculated. At the arrangement level adjustment can be done by the user on whole periodic charge. |
| 12 | Statement | The Statement property class is used to define the legacy ACCT.STATEMENT feature at the AA level. Statements may be produced daily (every working day), every 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or every 1-12 months on any day of the month. Up to nine statement cycles may be specified for each account, and each statement cycle is independent. In addition to this, special interim statements can be enabled. This property class also controls whether or not advices are to be produced when interest and charges are applied, and whether detailed interest statements (interest scale) should be produced. Within a statement cycle, it is possible to define multiple frequencies with a combination of weekly and monthly, such that statements are produced on the dates specified by both frequencies, but only contain details of entries since the last statement in that cycle. |

**LoanRestructuring**

| Restructuring Codes | Description |
|---|---|
| INPROG | Corresponds to the initial restructuring stage which commences from the moment the bank receives the Court Intimation Receipt. The intimation signifies that the customer or debt advisor or bank has approached the court with a request for restructuring of his debt. This stage implies that the court is in the process of reviewing the customer’s request, overall debt, and financial circumstances. |
| APPRVE | Corresponds to the restructuring stage during which Technical Loan (TL) booking should be available. This stage commences from the moment the bank receives the Court Order on Approval Decision for restructuring. It signifies that the customer’s request is approved, and the debt must be restructured as per the Court Decision by stating the new terms and conditions that will be applied. It is further implemented using the TL. |
| REJECT | Corresponds to the restructuring stage in one of the following situations: The customer’s request for restructuring is rejected by the court because he/she is being inconsistent or unreasonable as per his/her current financial circumstances. This stage commences when the bank receives the Court Rejection Decision for restructuring, which signifies that the customer’s request is rejected, and the loan must revert to its original parameters. The bank has concluded that the customer(s) is/are unable to pay towards the TL and has decided the reversion to REJECT stage. When reverting from APPRVE to REJECT, all TLs must be manually closed before the actual change of status. (The rejection does not exclude the bank from approaching the court again in the future). |

**LoanRestructuring**

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Restructure Status | Used to hold the restructure codes . The restructure status can take values defined in the restructure code like INPROG, APPRVE, and REJECT that denote restructure status of the loan. |
| Description | Used to display the restructure code’s short descriptions - business-wise description of the respective restructuring stage relating to the code. These can be amended even after the initial setup. |
| Previous Status | Used to display the allowed movements between the different restructure codes or stages. The system verifies the current restructuring status of the loan arrangement against this field in the AA.RESTRUCTURE.STATUS table on triggering the restructuring process as well as on moving between the different restructuring stages. It validates if the arrangement is eligible to move to the status corresponding to the restructuring activity triggered. |
| Book Memo Loan | Used to define the stage during which the Technical Loan (TLs) booking functionality is allowed. The Book Memo Loan field must be set to Yes only on that particular restructure stage where a technical loan can be booked. This field is not mandatory itself, as restructuring does not always make use of the memo loans functionality. Yet this can be set for one restructure stage only. There is no restriction on the number of memo loans that can be booked under a single OL. |
| Auto Terminate Memo Loan | Used to define a specific behavior of the TLs when the outstanding balances of the OL become zero. This is referred to as automatically terminating the Technical Loans (TL) and is the default behavior for the TLs when the OLs reach zero outstanding and/or fulfill the closure conditions. |
| Allocate as Per Ml | If set as Yes, it indicates that the same portions of payments applied to a TL should also be applied to the OL per property (if a due amount for the respective property is in place). This is a no-change field and cannot be amended once set. |

**Loan Creation**

| Field | Function |
|---|---|
| RFR Convention | Specifies the market convention for rate compounding or averaging. The LD application follows the lookback convention. |
| RFR Lookback Type | Specifies the type of lookback method applied for rate compounding or averaging. Types for rate calculations are: Narrow Definition - Uses the original interest period day count with lookback rate. If the Wednesday's rate is used for Friday, apply Friday’s weight (three days) to Wednesday’s rate. Observation Shift - Uses the original day count of the lookback rate. If the Wednesday's rate is used for Friday, apply Wednesday’s weight (one day) to Wednesday’s rate. |
| RFR Calc Method | Specifies the calculation method for RFR averaging. It can be: Compound Simple |
| RFR Spread Treatment | Specifies the spread treatment method during the RFR averaging: Spread-Inclusive - Uses the spread within the averaging calculation along with daily rates. Spread-Exclusive - Adds the spread separately after RFR averaging is done. |
| RFR Period Day Count | Specifies the treatment of the last available RFR in the rate averaging process. It allows the following values: Full - Last RFR with day weightage, which is applicable for the entire current interest period. Today - Last RFR with its original day weightage, which is applicable till the current business day. |
| RFR Decimals | Specifies the rounding value applied for RFR |

**Misc**

| Status | Description | Processing |
|---|---|---|
| CUR | Current | This is the status of a past due payment when it is fully up to date , that is, there is nothing outstanding. |
| PRE | Pre Grace | No penalties are applied whilst the payment is in pre-grace. Penalties are neither calculated, accrued nor posted. |
| GRA | Grace | The payment has not been overdue for long. During the grace period the penalty is calculated for information purposes but no accruals are posted. Depending on parameter settings a payment made during the grace period may have the calculated penalty waived or imposed. |
| PDO | Past Due Obligation | The payment is now definitely overdue. The penalty interest is calculated, accrued and posted. |
| NAB | Non-Accrual Basis | The payment has been overdue for some time and the bank is unlikely that it will receive payment. Hence, penalty interest accruals cease, though the calculations continue. |
| WOF | Write off | The past due payment is not received and so is written off from the bank’s books. |
| FWOF | Financial write off | If this option is chosen, then not only the past dues but also the amount in the underlying parent contract is written off. |

**Hybrid Pooling**

| Account Type | Company Name | System Date |
|---|---|---|

**Loan Securitisation**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Bank Role | Holds the owning bank’s role in the loan arrangement. It is the AA Customer Role of Bank Role Type. Agent – Bank works as an agent, holding no position of the asset. Hence, no accounting entries for commitment are required to be generated for the bank. Only the accounting entries of related fees and charges are generated. Agent Cum Participant – The bank works as an agent and also holds some position of the underlying asset (a portion of the loan is with the bank). So the bank acts as agent cum participant. Participant – The bank only acts as participant where the gent role is played by yet another bank and the bank has bought the asset from another bank. It is mandatory to define the Owning Bank’s role, either at the product level or at the arrangement level during capture share transfer activity. |
| Participant | Specifies the participant who has bought the asset from the bank. This is a valid customer ID and is defaulted as the investor from the pool selected during loan securitisation (capture share transfer activity). |
| Participant Role | Mentions the role of each participant in the loan. For a loan being securitised, the role of the participant must have the Bank Role Type as Sub Participant in the AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE application. |
| Own Commit Amt | Specifies the owning bank commitment share in amount. The system populates the own share amount based on the participant's share amount during the Capture Share Transfer activity. The net share amount of the owning bank and the participant banks amounts must be equal to the borrower amount. |
| Commitment Amt | Specifies the participant commitment share amount on the total loan amount. Validation is in place to ensure the sum of participant share amount including own share amount does not exceed the borrower amount or the loan commitment amount during the Capture Share Transfer activity. |
| Commitment Perc | This is a system-calculated field which indicates the participant commitment share in percentage on the total loan commitment. Either the commitment amount or the commitment share can be input, and the system splits the share portion of investors’ and owning bank accordingly. |

**Loan Securitisation**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Participant | Specifies the participant who has bought the asset from the bank. This is a valid customer ID and is defaulted as the investor from the pool selected during loan securitisation (Capture Share Transfer activity). |
| Beneficiary Ccy | Specifies the currency to match currency specific beneficiary account for the participants. At least one beneficiary currency must match the arrangement currency. |
| Beneficiary Id | Indicates the participant/investor's beneficiary account details for cash outflow. Account indicated in the beneficiary record is be used to credit investor's share of funds upon borrower repayment. Allowed values are valid ID from the BENEFICIARY application. This field will be defaulted from the Securitsation Pool ID during Capture Share Transfer Activity. It can be overwritten during the share transfer to the investor. When a Preferred Account (internal account) is indicated in the securitisation pool, these set of fields in the Participant condition are not referred for making payments to the investor. |
| Benf Po Product | This field denotes the payment order product that must be used by the bank to settle the investors share when a repayment is made by the borrower which sender remits the funds to intended beneficiary. When a Preferred Account (internal account) is indicated in the securitisation pool, these set of fields in the Participant condition are not referred for making payments to the investor. |

| Own Nostro | Specifies the Nostro account to which investor/participants will remit their funds. If left blank, then it is defaulted from the NOSTRO.ACCOUNT When Internal Account is indicated in the securitisation pool, these set of fields in the Participant condition are not referred for making settlements with the investor. |
| Payin Po Product | This field denotes the payment order product used to settle the funds during securitisation. It is a mandatory input field for Pay in Payment Order product, while updating the settlement instructions of the participants. When Internal Account is indicated in the securitisation pool, these set of fields in the Participant condition are not referred for making settlements with the investor. |

**Loan Securitisation**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Property | Specifies the property for which skims and margins are to be applied. Only Interest is allowed. |
| Operand | Specifies the skim and margin operand to be used. The allowed value is Sub. |
| Skim rate | Specifies the skim margin rate that needs to be applied for the Investors share. |
| Negative rate | Specifies when the skims have to be blocked in case of All-in-Rate results in a negative rate after deducting the skims. The options allowed are: NO - Rate for the investor is applied as zero. Block Margin - Rate for the investor is applied as borrower rate and skim rate is ignored. |

**Misc**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Account | The Account property class determines the accounting during securitisation. The user can choose between participant accounting and regular bilateral loan accounting. . |
| Accounting | The Accounting property class is used by all products. Arrangement Architecture (AA) uses activity-based accounting. Each property has different actions, which require accounting. For each action, a corresponding allocation rule definition is required. Allocation rules can be defined either at property or property class level. |
| Participant | The Participant property class holds information (such as ID, share percentage, beneficiary information) for the investors that participate in the loan (who have fully or partially bought the loan arrangement). Further, the accounting option for the participant as memo or contingent type of accounting is updated in Participant condition. |
| Share Transfer | The Share Transfer property class transfers shares between investors during the life of the loan. The buyer or seller are an existing or new lender or entity. |

|---|---|
| Mortgages | Securitised Mortgage Loan is a mortgage product with periodic interest setup and constant repayment schedule having automatic disbursement configured. The bilateral loan created in this product can be sold to an investor. Loan securitisation is part of the existing AA Lending product line, and it allows the user to sell a group of loans to a third-party investor. The Accounting condition is updated to support loan securitisation. |
| Consumer Loan | Accounting Condition for this product is enabled for bilateral loan securitisation. Participant Property of Sub-Participant Type is added to the product. Single or Multiple disbursement loan with the cancel period of 7 Days. No Interest Definition. Instead a DISBURSEMENTFEE is added based on the current disbursement amount. DISBURSEMENTFEE is a tiered charge with a cap of 250. REFUNDFEE is given as Credit Type to the customer on doing a repayment. |

**Misc**

| S.NO | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account | The Account property class is used by all the products which are account based. This property class primarily controls the description of the account. The ACCOUNT property allows the user to define and control balance treatment, posting restriction, linked account number (for memo accounts), currency market, date convention related setup for the account. Although the account names are account specific, generic titles can be defaulted from the product and can be replaced or given additional detail at the arrangement level. Each product defined and processed in AA can have a single ACCOUNT Property defined. |
| 2 | Activity Charges | The Activity Charges property class defines the charges that have to be applied when a particular activity is triggered on the arrangement. The charges so applied can be made due, capitalised or deferred. The user can enable auto settle the charges made due from unallocated credit balance by setting this to Yes. In accounts, charges are enabled for dormancy, settle payoff and ageing. This property class is also extensively used for all AA related modules, charges are set for various other activities. |
| 3 | Activity Restriction | The Activity Restriction property class is used to specify a restriction on a particular transaction. The restriction rules including the relevant periodic attributes and activities are defined in the product condition. These rules are then used to define activity based or property based restrictions. A rule if broken can be set to result in an override or error. A charge can be attached for this and can be set to be made due, capitalised or deferred. For the AR module, activity restriction is extensively used for restricting transactions by number, type, and so on. This is also extensively used in other modules to restrict the user from doing various user activity based on the life cycle status of contracts. |
| 4 | Balance Availability | The Balance Availability property class allows the user to control the following features pertaining to AR module: Notice amount and period, which needs to be given by a customer for withdrawing money from his account. Default Credit Check and Available Balance update related set up. Activity class or Activity specific credit check, and NSF related fees pertaining to it Tolerance Amount or Tolerance Currency - To indicate the grace amount, which is the allowed overdraft before the bank imposes NSF or OD fees. Overdraft Grace Period - To waive the NSF fee levied on the account, if the customer clears the debit balance within the stipulated grace period. |
| 5 | Dormancy | The Dormancy property class allows the user to control the parameterisation of inactive or dormant accounts and movement of the same into various buckets at the arrangement or product level. The same can be controlled based on period, and some exceptions or rules also can be added for evaluation and movement. The user can include or exclude certain activity or activity class for the evaluation. It is possible to, Configure different Dormancy status based on the period of inactivity Specify different charges and charging frequency for each Dormancy status Apply some exception rule filtering at an individual arrangement level (for example, account is in debit balance) and such rules can either be an API or a rule created using the Rules Engine Specify notices and notice frequency for each Dormancy status Specify Activities or Activity Classes or Activity Initiation Types which are qualified to keep an account active. Auto Reset can be enabled based on status or on Activity Type. |
| 6 | Facility | The Facility is a service component for financial products designed using arrangement architecture. The Facility property class controls the list of available services for an arrangement account. When an external activity (financial or non-financial) is triggered and the corresponding service group is mapped to an activity through Activity Mapping and EB.EVENTS . And the same came allowed or restricted or charged corresponding error message is raised to stop the activity. |
| 7 | Inheritance | The Inheritance property class is used for BN pool structure for inheriting the product conditions set at Parent level arrangement to the Child level arrangement accounts. The product conditions that are set for inheritance are attached to Property records with type as Inheritance Only. The properties to be inherited can be controlled both at source and target level. |
| 8 | Interest | The Interest property class is used for all interest definition and processing in AA. A product defined and processed in AA can have multiple interest properties defined (for example, principal interest, penalty interest, commission, etc. Interest rates can be defined as fixed , floating , periodic or linked rate (referring an INTEREST property from other arrangement), routine based calculation. Tiered interest can also be defined. Further it is possible to define a negative rate, minimum interest amount and waive the interest. Interest adjustment can be done in run time, and adjustment related detail or values can be captured in adjustment related fields. |
| 9 | Limit | The Limit property class primarily controls the use of LIMIT module by the product. We can set up single or shared limit. We can define the LIMIT.REFERENCE applicable for a specific product such that the system defaults the same in an arrangement. For a new limit, at the arrangement level, the LIMIT.SERIAL has to be given as NEW. The AR module can have self-contained secondary limit without having actual limit attached to it. Overdraft status or notice for AR module is handled inside the Limit Property class. Further Limits can be set to use the LIMIT module (AL and AD) or it can be managed only within the arrangement architecture framework. |
| 10 | Payment Schedule | The Payment Schedule property class is used by all products which have amounts billed (that is,made due) or capitalised or Pay. A Payment Schedule can be comprised of one or more payment definitions with conditions such as payment Type and Method, arrangement properties, dates and amounts. The AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application is used to define the standard payment types such as constant, linear, actual and fixed equal and so on, that can be used by a product. This payment type is then attached to each payment schedule definition. The start and end date can be specified, the user can specify the repayment of arrangement to commence after ‘n’ months from the arrangement date or ‘n’ months before the maturity or ‘n’ months after the change product or reset and rollover has happened. |
| 11 | Periodic Charges | The Periodic Charges property class acts as a container to group different charge properties and calculate a periodic charge amount. The Payment Schedule property class drives this property class. A periodic charge property can be attached in payment schedule and on schedule date periodic charge amount is calculated. At the arrangement level adjustment can be done by the user on whole periodic charge. |
| 12 | Statement | The Statement property class is used to define the legacy ACCT.STATEMENT feature at the AA level. Statements may be produced daily (every working day), every 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or every 1-12 months on any day of the month. Up to nine statement cycles may be specified for each account, and each statement cycle is independent. In addition to this, special interim statements can be enabled. This property class also controls whether or not advices are to be produced when interest and charges are applied, and whether detailed interest statements (interest scale) should be produced. Within a statement cycle, it is possible to define multiple frequencies with a combination of weekly and monthly, such that statements are produced on the dates specified by both frequencies, but only contain details of entries since the last statement in that cycle. |

### lending - PD (PD)


**Misc**

| Status | Description | Processing |
|---|---|---|
| CUR | Current | This is the status of a past due payment when it is fully up to date , that is, there is nothing outstanding. |
| PRE | Pre Grace | No penalties are applied whilst the payment is in pre-grace. Penalties are neither calculated, accrued nor posted. |
| GRA | Grace | The payment has not been overdue for long. During the grace period the penalty is calculated for information purposes but no accruals are posted. Depending on parameter settings a payment made during the grace period may have the calculated penalty waived or imposed. |
| PDO | Past Due Obligation | The payment is now definitely overdue. The penalty interest is calculated, accrued and posted. |
| NAB | Non-Accrual Basis | The payment has been overdue for some time and the bank is unlikely that it will receive payment. Hence, penalty interest accruals cease, though the calculations continue. |
| WOF | Write off | The past due payment is not received and so is written off from the bank’s books. |
| FWOF | Financial write off | If this option is chosen, then not only the past dues but also the amount in the underlying parent contract is written off. |
